payload.title: FD M0 — Two parallel spikes (the de-risk milestone)

children.title: M0-01 Scaffold: replace the static visual study with the TDD architecture skeleton
M0-02 SimCore boundary lint: L0-only / no-float / no-std / no-g_xEngine grep gate with self-tests
M0-03 SimCore containers: FD_Ring (pow2 growable POD ring), FD_SlotMap (generation-checked), FD_Bitset
M0-04 Deterministic foundation: FD_Fixed Q16.16, per-tick content conversion, named XorShift32 streams, integer value noise, FNV-1a digests
M0-05 Seed Foundry living docs: Status, TestPlan, SaveFormat, Shortfalls, Questions, DecisionLog, AgentBriefing
M0-06 Command queue, FD_Sim::Tick phase skeleton, and the accumulator with 3-tick debt clamp
M0-07 World data model: FD_Chunk 32x32 layers, chunk hashmap + sorted chunk list, occupancy, packed entity handles
M0-08 Belts spike: transport lines with head-gap compression, 128-tile cap, wake/sleep, two lanes
M0-09 Belts spike: splitters, lane-precise sideloads, underground belts, circular-run anchors
M0-10 Inserters as event-scheduled swings + the timer wheel
M0-11 Machine archetype SoA tables, one crafting archetype (furnace), wake links and wake/sleep
M0-12 Digest + op-count harness: canned FD_TestFactory scripts, per-module sub-digests every 64 ticks, pinned goldens
M0-13 Belt-city generator + SimCore spike exit measurement (10k lines / 50k items, tick < 2 ms desktop, /Od vs /O2 digests equal)
M0-14 Device render spike harness: 20k building + 5k moving instances with tint/anim churn on Flux_InstanceGroup + UnifiedMesh
M0-15 Device render spike: run on the floor Adreno phone and one Mali device; record numbers; take the fallback decision
M0-16 Human edits after the scaffold: Foundry unit-gate line, doc-lint game array, foundry-tests.yml workflow
M0-17 M0 milestone acceptance: both spike exits recorded, go/no-go on the render path

children.title: M2-01 Gesture recognizer over Zenith_Pointers: pinch, two-finger pan, long-press, double-tap, two-finger tap, hold-to-peek
M2-02 Touch build flow: release ≠ commit, drag-run commit on release with 3 s undo toast, radial long-press menus

M2-07 Engine #4 basics: target-framerate control (30/60) via paced present + ANativeWindow_setFrameRate hint
M2-08 Engine #8: ScrollView fixes — scroll offset in hit-testing, drag-vs-tap arbitration window, textured-quad clipping, units
M2-09 Fat-finger law audit + safe-area HUD anchoring + automated layout assertions
M2-10 Android build & cook for Foundry: AGDE configs green, uncompressed RGBA8 stopgap textures, x86_64 emulator boot
M2-11 Device session: Android digest run green on the floor phone, kill-after-background survives, 60 fps held, touch slice playthrough
M2-12 Settings screen (battery 30/60, camera snap, colorblind palettes, alert mutes) + new-game world-gen options + title/new/continue flow
M2-13 Touch automated test suite: FD_TouchBuild, FD_TouchInspect, FD_PinchZoomTiers, FD_TwoFingerUndo on the Null backend
M2-14 M2 milestone acceptance: touch-playable slice on the floor phone

payload.goal:
TDD §6 "The container gap": the engine has no deque, growable ring, slot map or usable pool (`Zenith/Collections/` holds `Zenith_Vector`, `Zenith_HashMap`/`Set`, a compile-time-capacity `Zenith_MemoryPool` and a `Zenith_CircularQueue` that destroys/reconstructs per pop), and `Zenith_Vector`'s default constructor mallocs 8 elements, a policy SimCore's SoA tables must not inherit. Ship under `Source/SimCore/Containers/`:
- `FD_Ring<T>` — power-of-two growable POD ring, no allocation until first push, push/pop both ends, index-from-head, `Reserve`, iteration in head order.
- `FD_SlotMap<T>` — dense storage with per-slot generation, freelist reuse, `u_int32` handles packed as `generation | slot`, generation-checked `Get` returning null for stale handles, index-order iteration over live slots.
- `FD_Bitset` — fixed-or-growable bit array with set/clear/test/`FindFirstSet`, word-aligned.
All three route allocation through `Zenith_MemoryManagement` (L0) and pass the SimCore lint. Unit tests in `Tests/FD_Tests_Containers.cpp` (repo mandate: every new type gets dedicated coverage).

payload.goal:
TDD §4 rules 1–3 and 5–6. Deliver in `Source/SimCore/`:
- `FD_Fixed.h`: Q16.16 fixed point with 64-bit intermediates for mul/div, saturating narrow, `consteval` constructors from designer per-second / per-tile values so `TICK_RATE` is consulted once at table definition (TDD §17). Belt tiers must convert to exactly 16 / 32 / 48 sub-tile units per tick (1/256-tile units, TDD §1).
- `FD_Rng.h`: named `XorShift32` streams (`Zenith/Maths/Zenith_Noise.h` is the engine's one stream-portable PRNG) — worldgen, threat, drones, … — each seeded from the world seed; advancing only inside a tick is the caller's rule, documented.
- `FD_Noise.h`: 2–3 octaves of integer value noise over `HashCoords`/`HashUInt` (bit-exact; the float `ValueNoise`/`FBM` in the same header are banned).
- `FD_Digest.h`: FNV-1a 64 over explicitly little-endian field serialization (never struct memcpy), with a per-module sub-digest accumulator.

payload.goal: TDD §3. "The command queue is the ONLY write path into SimCore": UI callbacks fire after `Scenes().Update` in the frame, so every mutation is an `FD_Command` (`PlaceBuilding{archetype, tile, rot}`, `RemoveBuilding{handle}`, `SetRecipe{handle, recipe}` … — start with the variants M0 needs, leave the enum open) appended to an `FD_Ring` that `FD_Sim::Tick()` drains **first**, in order. Every command carries its inverse (the undo stack in M1 rides this). Implement the fixed phase order of TDD §3 as named empty phase functions (drain → timer wheel → electric → belts → splitters → inserters → fluids → trains → drones → circuits → threat → swap/advance RNG/`++m_uTick`) so later tickets fill slots without reordering. `FD_GameComponent::OnUpdate` gets the accumulator verbatim from TDD §3: `ClampDt`, at most `uMAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME = 3` ticks per frame, leftover debt discarded with a log line, pause = don't call `Tick`. A `(tick, command)` replay log plus the world seed reproduces a run bit-for-bit — the digest harness's spine.

payload.goal: TDD §5. `FD_World` owns `Zenith_HashMap<u_int64 /*packed s32,s32*/, FD_Chunk*>` for point lookup plus a **sorted-by-key chunk list** rebuilt on chunk create for every deterministic whole-world scan (hashmap iteration is slot-order and capacity-history dependent — `Zenith/Collections/CLAUDE.md`). `FD_Chunk` layers allocated lazily: terrain (1 KB tile bytes: ground type, resource id — always present), occupancy (`u_int32` handle per tile, 4 KB, on first construction), threat (pollution `u_int32`, nest list, pathing cost byte). Entity handles are `archetype(6) | generation(6) | slot(20)`, handle 0 is null. Multi-tile buildings write their handle into every covered tile from the archetype footprint. Terrain generation itself is M1; here the generator is a stub that fills a recognizable pattern from the seed.

payload.goal: TDD §6 "the load-bearing deep dive". Contiguous straight-through belt tiles merge into **transport lines** (two per belt run, one per lane), capped at **128 tiles**. A line stores `u_int32 m_uHeadGap` (1/256-tile), an `FD_Ring` of `{u_int8 uItem, u_int8 uFlags, u_int16 uGapToPrev}` (4 bytes per item), `{speed, length, state, wake links}`. Tick semantics: an unblocked line advances by decrementing `m_uHeadGap` by its per-tick speed (16/32/48) — one integer op; when the head reaches the line end it transfers (next line / blocked); a **blocked line sleeps entirely** and is woken by its consumer. Placing/removing a belt splices lines (merge / split at the edit tile). Deterministic counters: `uHeadAdvances`, `uLinesWoken`, `uSplices` per tick, exposed for op-count pins (TDD §18). Presentation-side position derivation is M1; this ticket is pure SimCore. Belt tiers Mk1/Mk2/Mk3 from GDD §5.2.

payload.goal: TDD §6: "Splitters/sideloads are nodes in the line graph with explicit, serialized round-robin state (deterministic fairness). Circular runs are detected at merge time and assigned a deterministic anchor tile (no head)." GDD §5.2: splitters split/merge strict round-robin with input/output priority and a single per-side item filter as researched upgrades; undergrounds jump 4/6/8 tiles by tier; sideloading is lane-precise. Implement `FD_Splitter` nodes with serialized `uNextOutput`/`uNextInput`, priority and filter fields (default off; research toggles them in M1), sideload transfer onto the near lane, underground pairing on placement with tier-specific max span, and circular-run detection assigning the anchor at the lowest packed tile key.

definitionOfDone.text: A 2-in/2-out splitter fed unequal inputs distributes exactly round-robin over 1,000 items (counts differ by at most 1)
Output priority sends every item to the priority side while it has room; filter routes only the filtered item to its side
Sideload onto a belt lands on the correct lane for all four approach directions
An underground pair beyond its tier span is refused at placement with a reason code; within span, items traverse with correct timing
A circular loop of belts carries items around indefinitely with conservation and a pinned digest; Foundry pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED Null run

payload.goal: TDD §7: "Inserters are event-scheduled, never integrated: a swing is `{eState, uStartTick, uDuration}`; the sim touches an inserter only at transitions (pick, swing-end, place, return-end)." Build the **timer wheel** (`FD_TimerWheel`: buckets keyed by absolute tick, zero cost until due) used by every machine whose next state change is at a known tick, and the inserter archetype on it: three tiers (Inserter ~1 swing/s, Long 2-tile reach, Fast ~2.3 swings/s — GDD §5.3), pick from belts (lane-aware, via binary search over prefix gaps then a bounded splice), machines and containers, place into the same, cached `(line id, offset)` targets invalidated by belt edits through the line graph. Counters: `uInserterTransitions` per tick for op-count pins.

payload.goal: TDD §18: "canned command scripts build factories → run N ticks → FNV-1a over serialized state == pinned digest" as the determinism gate, and "the same runs assert exact deterministic counters" as flake-free perf regression guards — deliberately not wall-clock (the repo shipped a wall-clock CI flake, commit `9bdc28be`). payload.goal: TDD §20 calls the device render spike "the single riskiest assumption in the project": the in-tree instancing record is 2,520 instances (desktop) and Foundry needs ~20k sustained. Build `FD_RenderSpike_Test` (automated, `requiresGraphics`): a flat ground of tiled quads, 20,000 static building instances across ~12 placeholder meshes in `Flux_InstanceGroup`s (`Zenith/Flux/InstancedMeshes/Flux_InstanceGroup.h`), 5,000 moving item instances updated every frame, RGBA8 tint churn on 10% per frame, one sun cascade set, uncompressed textures. Measure extract / upload / cull / draw via the CPU+GPU profiler and dump per-frame timings to `Build/artifacts/foundry/spike/*.json`. Flip `Foundry.zproj` to `"android": true` and regen so the same test builds for AGDE (the on-device run is the sibling ticket). Add `--spike-instances N` to scale the harness.

## Goal
TDD §20 calls the device render spike "the single riskiest assumption in the project": the in-tree instancing record is 2,520 instances (desktop) and Foundry needs ~20k sustained. Build `FD_RenderSpike_Test` (automated, `requiresGraphics`): a flat ground of tiled quads, 20,000 static building instances across ~12 placeholder meshes in `Flux_InstanceGroup`s (`Zenith/Flux/InstancedMeshes/Flux_InstanceGroup.h`), 5,000 moving item instances updated every frame, RGBA8 tint churn on 10% per frame, one sun cascade set, uncompressed textures. Measure extract / upload / cull / draw via the CPU+GPU profiler and dump per-frame timings to `Build/artifacts/foundry/spike/*.json`. Flip `Foundry.zproj` to `"android": true` and regen so the same test builds for AGDE (the on-device run is the sibling ticket). Add `--spike-instances N` to scale the harness.

## Goal
GDD §4: "Procedurally generated, effectively unbounded. The world is a flat plain streamed in chunks … seed-deterministic." Resources: iron, copper, coal, stone patches; crude oil seeps; water lakes; trees as a pollution buffer; no elevation. TDD §5: patches are generated from the integer hashes at chunk-first-touch and registered in a global patch table; only deltas persist. Implement `FD_WorldGen` over `FD_Noise`: ground type, lakes, tree density, patch placement with richness/distance scaling, the starting-area guarantee (iron/copper/coal/stone/water within reach, oil slightly out — GDD §4), and the world-gen options struct (richness, enemy density, evolution speed, peaceful) threaded through so M2's new-game screen can set them. Patch depletion counters live in the delta layer.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Same seed + options → identical chunk bytes and patch table (digest-pinned for seeds 1, 0x7BF32CA4 and 0xFFFFFFFF)
- [ ] The starting 5×5 chunk area contains every guaranteed resource for 100 random seeds (unit sweep)
- [ ] Chunk generation touches only its own chunk's RNG state (generating chunks in a different order yields identical bytes)
- [ ] Trees and water tiles are impassable in the occupancy query; oil seeps accept only a pumpjack footprint
- [ ] Foundry pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED Null run

payload.goal: GDD §5.0 — the no-avatar answer. The **Core** is the starting structure, a container that accepts belts/inserters. The **Build Reserve** = Core contents + every Depot flagged build-accessible; placing a building draws its cost from the Reserve instantly, deconstruction refunds it (the fiction is teleported construction material — never a per-placement delivery). The **Core Fabricator** is a slow one-at-a-time crafter inside the Core queuing basic recipes from the Reserve. **Bootstrap:** `HarvestSurface{tile}` commands on rocks/trees yield starter ore/wood → queue a burner drill + stone furnace → place → feed plates back. All as `FD_Command`s with inverses. `PlaceBuilding` is refused with a reason code when the Reserve cannot afford it.

The Fabricator crafts strictly one recipe at a time at its table rate, via the timer wheel
Harvesting a rock yields the table amount, removes the rock from occupancy, and is undoable in principle (inverse command recorded)
Golden digest of the bootstrap script (harvest → fabricate → place → feed) pinned; Foundry pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED Null run

payload.goal: TDD §8 and GDD §5.5. Poles (small/medium/large) union by wire reach on placement; machines map to the covering pole's root; removal marks the network dirty and an end-of-tick BFS over the pole graph rebuilds it. Per network per tick: production capacity and demand maintained incrementally (never rescanned) → `satisfaction = min(1, supply/demand)` in Q16.16 → consumers scale by it (brownout: everything slows, nothing hard-stops). Accumulator priority solar → accumulator → steam resolved in the same pass (solar/accumulator archetypes land in M1-08). "Stats rings designed in now": per network, 64-sample rings at tick/second/minute cadence of production and consumption per category. Multiple isolated networks are legal. Phase 3 of the tick order.

Demand 2× supply gives every consumer satisfaction exactly 0.5 in Q16.16 and halves craft progress per tick (pinned)
Satisfaction changes wake no sleepers (`uMachinesWoken` pinned at 0 across a brownout transition); a full network-off transition does wake them
Stats rings hold the last 64 samples at each cadence and the minute ring is the mean of its seconds

payload.body:
## Goal
TDD §8 and GDD §5.5. Poles (small/medium/large) union by wire reach on placement; machines map to the covering pole's root; removal marks the network dirty and an end-of-tick BFS over the pole graph rebuilds it. Per network per tick: production capacity and demand maintained incrementally (never rescanned) → `satisfaction = min(1, supply/demand)` in Q16.16 → consumers scale by it (brownout: everything slows, nothing hard-stops). Accumulator priority solar → accumulator → steam resolved in the same pass (solar/accumulator archetypes land in M1-08). "Stats rings designed in now": per network, 64-sample rings at tick/second/minute cadence of production and consumption per category. Multiple isolated networks are legal. Phase 3 of the tick order.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Two pole clusters joined by one pole become one network; removing that pole splits them at end of tick with per-side satisfaction recomputed (unit)

payload.goal: GDD §5.5: burner boot → steam (offshore pump → boiler → steam engine) → solar + accumulator. Boiler burns fuel via the timer wheel; engine contributes production capacity while steam is available. Solar contributes by a fixed day fraction (no day/night cycle in v1 — record as `FD-D-` decision); accumulators charge/discharge with the §8 priority.

definitionOfDone.text: Pump→boiler→engine chain powers an electric drill at satisfaction 1.0 when supply ≥ demand (tick-exact pin)
Removing the boiler's fuel stops the engine's contribution on the tick the fuel timer fires

`FD_FluidEndpoint` throughput caps are respected per tick (boiler cannot draw more than its table rate)

payload.goal: TDD §14–§15: "factory size never reaches the renderer." `FD_Sim::PostTickExtract(FD_Presentation&, alpha)` publishes presentation-owned snapshot buffers at tick rate (positions/phases for visible movers); render frames interpolate between the last two extracts. Only entities inside the camera rect (+1-chunk margin, + a shadow-length pad toward the sun) have render instances at all; Presentation materializes/dematerializes per chunk on visibility enter/exit from pooled per-mesh instance budgets. **Slot ledger:** `RemoveInstance` swap-and-pops without reporting the moved id, so keep a per-group `slot → owner` array and patch the tail owner on each removal — never clear-and-respawn per frame. Hard caps by tier (Workshop ≤ ~8k buildings + ~10k items; Logistics ≤ ~15k; Map ≤ ~10k quads) enforced by representation switching before budgets inflate, because group capacity is grow-only. Implement Workshop tier for buildings here; belt items/arms are M1-11, other tiers M3a. Honour `FD-D-001` if the fallback renderer was chosen.

Only entities inside the camera rect (+1-chunk margin, + a shadow-length pad toward the sun) have render instances at all; Presentation materializes/dematerializes per chunk on visibility enter/exit from pooled per-mesh instance budgets. **Slot ledger:** `RemoveInstance` swap-and-pops without reporting the moved id, so keep a per-group `slot → owner` array and patch the tail owner on each removal — never clear-and-respawn per frame. Hard caps by tier (Workshop ≤ ~8k buildings + ~10k items; Logistics ≤ ~15k; Map ≤ ~10k quads) enforced by representation switching before budgets inflate, because group capacity is grow-only. Implement Workshop tier for buildings here; belt items/arms are M1-11, other tiers M3a. Honour `FD-D-001` if the fallback renderer was chosen.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] A scripted camera sweep over a 200-chunk factory never exceeds the Workshop instance cap (asserted in an automated test on the Null backend via the ledger counts)
- [ ] The ledger is consistent after 10k random add/remove operations (owner of every live slot is correct — unit)
- [ ] Instances exist only for chunks intersecting the view rect + margin; chunks leaving the view release their slots within one frame
- [ ] Interpolation alpha is derived from the accumulator and never reads sim state directly (Presentation reads only snapshot buffers — enforced by the lint direction: SimCore has no Presentation include, Presentation has no `FD_Sim` mutable reach)
- [ ] Foundry pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED Null run

payload.goal: TDD §16: adopt the Zenithmon module codec shape verbatim (`Games/Zenithmon/Source/Core/ZM_SaveSchema.{h,cpp}`, `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/SaveFormat.md`): engine `Zenith_SaveData` owns the envelope; the payload is `FDSV` = header + length-framed modules `{moduleId, moduleVersion, byteLength, payload}`, one per sim system (world-deltas, belts, machines, power, research, presentation-prefs for M1; ids reserved for fluids, rail, drones, circuits, threat, blueprints/undo). Readers land exactly on `byteLength`; every read bounds-checks before allocating; writes stage + validate into a private stream before `Zenith_SaveData::Save`; reads parse into a temporary and publish only on complete success. Chunk deltas over procedural regen. Binding rule: every schema change ships its version bump + a compiled-blob migration test in the same commit. `Zenith_SaveData::Initialise("Foundry")` at boot with the between-tests clear hook.

`Docs/SaveFormat.md` documents every module id, version and field order

## Goal

payload.goal: GDD §6.1 control vocabulary and TDD §19 "explicitly game-side": the gesture recognizer is built on `Zenith_Pointers`' verified primitives (8 slots, per-pointer start/excursion/down-time, claims) and publishes through `Zenith_InputActions::PublishVirtualButton/PublishVirtualAxis`. Recognize: pinch (continuous zoom with focus point), two-finger drag (pan), long-press (≥ 350 ms, no excursion), double-tap, two-finger tap (undo accelerator), two-finger tap-hold (rotate in place), and the hold-to-peek variant that cancels on swipe. No gesture with more than two fingers, no shake, no tilt (GDD §6.7). `FD_GestureRecognizer` is a pure state machine over a pointer-event stream so it is unit-testable with synthetic streams and identical on mouse (single pointer) and touch.

payload.goal: TDD §19 #8: `Zenith_UIScrollView` exists, is unused by any game, untested, with three verified defects: child hit-testing ignores the scroll offset (input lands where rows were at scroll 0), a drag started on a child button can never become a scroll (the child claims first), and the textured-quad path (`SubmitQuadWithUV`) is not clipped to the viewport (`Zenith/UI/Zenith_UIScrollView.cpp`, `Zenith_UICanvas.cpp`). Fix all three: apply the offset in the input walk, add a candidate-arbitration window before child claims commit (the standard scroll-view gesture dance), clip + UV-adjust textured quads. Acceptance: a list of buttons scrolls by dragging anywhere and taps hit the visually-correct row.

## Goal
GDD §2: Android first, landscape. TDD §17: texture export is BC-only today and BC support is not device-checked, so uncompressed RGBA8 is the M0–M2 stopgap (ZM's approach) — declare it in `Assets/Textures/TextureUsage.ztexdecl` for every Foundry texture. Build `Vulkan_arm64_v8a_vs2022_Debug_Agde_False` and `Vulkan_x86_64_vs2022_Debug_Agde_False`, package assets for the APK per the ZM Android precedent, and boot `FD_Boot_Test` on the x86_64 emulator (the only ABI a machine without an ARM device can run — `adb install` needs `-t`). Record the emulator boot log in the work log; physical-device runs are M2-11.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both AGDE configs build from `foundry_agde.sln`
- [ ] Every Foundry texture is declared uncompressed in `TextureUsage.ztexdecl`
- [ ] The x86_64 emulator boots Foundry to the title screen and `FD_Boot_Test` passes there (log attached)
- [ ] `Docs/BuildEnvironment.md` records the Android build/install commands for Foundry

payload.goal: TDD §13: units follow the group corridor with local steering — spatial-hash separation (incrementally re-binned, 8-neighbour cell query) + integer steering toward the corridor; active units hard-capped at **5,000** (wave scheduling holds excess; off-screen groups far from any player structure advance along their corridor in bulk instead of steering). TDD §14: threat steering fans out in unit shards by spatial-hash region on `Zenith_DataParallelTask` with pre-partitioned shards, shard-local writes, per-shard effect queues merged in fixed shard order — the nondeterministic claim order is invisible. Budget: separation+steering ≈ 0.8–1.3 ms at the cap on the floor device.

payload.body:
## Goal
TDD §13: units follow the group corridor with local steering — spatial-hash separation (incrementally re-binned, 8-neighbour cell query) + integer steering toward the corridor; active units hard-capped at **5,000** (wave scheduling holds excess; off-screen groups far from any player structure advance along their corridor in bulk instead of steering). TDD §14: threat steering fans out in unit shards by spatial-hash region on `Zenith_DataParallelTask` with pre-partitioned shards, shard-local writes, per-shard effect queues merged in fixed shard order — the nondeterministic claim order is invisible. Budget: separation+steering ≈ 0.8–1.3 ms at the cap on the floor device.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Digest of a 5,000-unit scripted march is identical with 1, 4 and 16 workers (determinism across fan-out)
- [ ] The active-unit count never exceeds 5,000 while a nest tries to spawn 8,000 (unit)
- [ ] Off-screen bulk advance is op-count cheap: a far group of 50 costs 1 update per tick, not 50
- [ ] Separation keeps any two units ≥ the table radius apart after settling (unit with 200 units in a corridor)
- [ ] Foundry pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED Null run

payload.goal:
ZEN-2 added a per-chunk span table (`m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans`) alongside `m_pxPhysicsGeometry`. Its lifetime invariant is currently **subtle rather than simple**, and the header says so because the simple version is not true:

`Zenith_TerrainComponent_Editor.cpp` (`CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerate`, ~1162-1167) deletes and nulls `m_pxPhysicsGeometry` and leaves the span table standing. That is *safe today* for a two-step reason: the query gates on null geometry first, and `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore` — the only site that assigns a fresh mesh — calls `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` unconditionally. So a leftover table is a delayed free, not a use-after-free.

But "safe because of how two other functions happen to behave" is a worse invariant than "every site that discards the geometry frees the table", and the ZEN-2 review had to reason through it to confirm it holds. The editor TU can call `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` — it is a private member of the same class and there was never a technical barrier, only that the file was outside that ticket's scope.

Note the review also found the *original* safety argument was wrong on its premise: "its caller always then calls `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometry()`" is false, because `Zenith_TerrainComponent_Editor.cpp:1056-1061` returns early when `DeleteExistingTerrainFilesInDirectory` fails. The conclusion survived; the reasoning did not. That is exactly the kind of invariant worth making mechanical.

**Second, smaller item in the same file family.** `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp:732-739` still opens its AABB comment with "This is an accelerator". It is not *only* an accelerator: it CLIPS the ±`fBARYCENTRIC_EPSILON` band, which is what prevents rim extrapolation, so it changes the answer rather than merely speeding it up. The precise wording already landed in the header and `Components/CLAUDE.md` under ZM-49; the `.cpp` line was outside that fix-forward's file list.

## Goal

ZEN-2 added a per-chunk span table (`m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans`) alongside `m_pxPhysicsGeometry`. Its lifetime invariant is currently **subtle rather than simple**, and the header says so because the simple version is not true:

`Zenith_TerrainComponent_Editor.cpp` (`CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerate`, ~1162-1167) deletes and nulls `m_pxPhysicsGeometry` and leaves the span table standing. That is *safe today* for a two-step reason: the query gates on null geometry first, and `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore` — the only site that assigns a fresh mesh — calls `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` unconditionally. So a leftover table is a delayed free, not a use-after-free.

But "safe because of how two other functions happen to behave" is a worse invariant than "every site that discards the geometry frees the table", and the ZEN-2 review had to reason through it to confirm it holds. The editor TU can call `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` — it is a private member of the same class and there was never a technical barrier, only that the file was outside that ticket's scope.

Note the review also found the *original* safety argument was wrong on its premise: "its caller always then calls `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometry()`" is false, because `Zenith_TerrainComponent_Editor.cpp:1056-1061` returns early when `DeleteExistingTerrainFilesInDirectory` fails. The conclusion survived; the reasoning did not. That is exactly the kind of invariant worth making mechanical.

**Second, smaller item in the same file family.** `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp:732-739` still opens its AABB comment with "This is an accelerator". It is not *only* an accelerator: it CLIPS the ±`fBARYCENTRIC_EPSILON` band, which is what prevents rim extrapolation, so it changes the answer rather than merely speeding it up. The precise wording already landed in the header and `Components/CLAUDE.md` under ZM-49; the `.cpp` line was outside that fix-forward's file list.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every site that discards `m_pxPhysicsGeometry` also frees the span table, including the editor path
- [ ] The header states the SIMPLE invariant, because it is now true
- [ ] `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp`'s AABB comment says the box clips the epsilon band rather than only accelerating
- [ ] No behaviour change beyond the earlier free: the query still gates on null geometry, and no test count moves

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZEN-4 -->
ran on sonnet/low via SIMPLE+MEDIUM · category Engine

**Done** — merged to `master` as `71bbd6ab`. **Claimed via `zagent next` in queue mode**, the first tick this session not to name a key.

`CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerate` now frees `m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans` in the same block it discards `m_pxPhysicsGeometry`, so the header states the **simple** invariant because it is finally true. Previously it held only via a two-step argument spanning the query's null-gate and `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore`'s unconditional clear — and the original argument for it was **wrong on its premise** (it claimed the caller always reloads; there is an early-return path when `DeleteExistingTerrainFilesInDirectory` fails). The conclusion survived by a different mechanism than the one anybody had checked.

The reviewer independently traced all eight discard/transfer sites and confirmed both members end null-or-matched together after each, and that `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` is null-safe, idempotent, and compiled in every configuration.

**The blocking finding was the absence of evidence, not a defect.** The fixed line had **zero execution coverage**, and the one adjacent test asserts the operation is rejected *before* cleanup runs — checking a sentinel file still exists specifically to prove cleanup was never reached. Green gates and unmoved pins said nothing about it.

Fix-forward 1/3 added `TerrainPhysicsGeometryCleanup/CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerateFreesGeometryAndSpans`, which drives the function directly against members populated through a **real** `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore` call, asserting both non-null *before* cleanup so the after-check cannot pass vacuously.

The `#ifdef ZENITH_TOOLS` guard matters for a sharper reason than "it would compile out": `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp` includes the `.inl` unconditionally, so without it this would **break the build in every `ToolsEnabled=False` config for every game**.

Pins +1 each, observed: **3366 / 1650 / 1741**. Gates: 6 legs green.

Note the DoD said "no test count moves" — that was the filer's assumption and it was wrong. Preserving a count at the cost of covering the line this ticket exists to fix is the inverse of what anyone wants.

Filed **ZEN-5**: `Zenith_TerrainComponent.h:522` has `//private:` commented out, so the members this invariant governs are public and nothing enforces the "every site in this file is the only writer" premise it rests on. Found independently by three agents.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

## Goal

ZEN-2 added a per-chunk span table (`m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans`) alongside `m_pxPhysicsGeometry`. Its lifetime invariant is currently **subtle rather than simple**, and the header says so because the simple version is not true:

`Zenith_TerrainComponent_Editor.cpp` (`CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerate`, ~1162-1167) deletes and nulls `m_pxPhysicsGeometry` and leaves the span table standing. That is *safe today* for a two-step reason: the query gates on null geometry first, and `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore` — the only site that assigns a fresh mesh — calls `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` unconditionally. So a leftover table is a delayed free, not a use-after-free.

But "safe because of how two other functions happen to behave" is a worse invariant than "every site that discards the geometry frees the table", and the ZEN-2 review had to reason through it to confirm it holds. The editor TU can call `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` — it is a private member of the same class and there was never a technical barrier, only that the file was outside that ticket's scope.

Note the review also found the *original* safety argument was wrong on its premise: "its caller always then calls `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometry()`" is false, because `Zenith_TerrainComponent_Editor.cpp:1056-1061` returns early when `DeleteExistingTerrainFilesInDirectory` fails. The conclusion survived; the reasoning did not. That is exactly the kind of invariant worth making mechanical.

**Second, smaller item in the same file family.** `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp:732-739` still opens its AABB comment with "This is an accelerator". It is not *only* an accelerator: it CLIPS the ±`fBARYCENTRIC_EPSILON` band, which is what prevents rim extrapolation, so it changes the answer rather than merely speeding it up. The precise wording already landed in the header and `Components/CLAUDE.md` under ZM-49; the `.cpp` line was outside that fix-forward's file list.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every site that discards `m_pxPhysicsGeometry` also frees the span table, including the editor path
- [ ] The header states the SIMPLE invariant, because it is now true
- [ ] `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp`'s AABB comment says the box clips the epsilon band rather than only accelerating
- [ ] No behaviour change beyond the earlier free: the query still gates on null geometry, and no test count moves

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZEN-4 -->
ran on sonnet/low via SIMPLE+MEDIUM · category Engine

**Done** — merged to `master` as `71bbd6ab`. **Claimed via `zagent next` in queue mode**, the first tick this session not to name a key.

`CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerate` now frees `m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans` in the same block it discards `m_pxPhysicsGeometry`, so the header states the **simple** invariant because it is finally true. Previously it held only via a two-step argument spanning the query's null-gate and `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore`'s unconditional clear — and the original argument for it was **wrong on its premise** (it claimed the caller always reloads; there is an early-return path when `DeleteExistingTerrainFilesInDirectory` fails). The conclusion survived by a different mechanism than the one anybody had checked.

The reviewer independently traced all eight discard/transfer sites and confirmed both members end null-or-matched together after each, and that `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()` is null-safe, idempotent, and compiled in every configuration.

**The blocking finding was the absence of evidence, not a defect.** The fixed line had **zero execution coverage**, and the one adjacent test asserts the operation is rejected *before* cleanup runs — checking a sentinel file still exists specifically to prove cleanup was never reached. Green gates and unmoved pins said nothing about it.

Fix-forward 1/3 added `TerrainPhysicsGeometryCleanup/CleanupPriorGenerationForRegenerateFreesGeometryAndSpans`, which drives the function directly against members populated through a **real** `LoadCombinedPhysicsGeometryCore` call, asserting both non-null *before* cleanup so the after-check cannot pass vacuously.

The `#ifdef ZENITH_TOOLS` guard matters for a sharper reason than "it would compile out": `Zenith_TerrainComponent.cpp` includes the `.inl` unconditionally, so without it this would **break the build in every `ToolsEnabled=False` config for every game**.

Pins +1 each, observed: **3366 / 1650 / 1741**. Gates: 6 legs green.

Note the DoD said "no test count moves" — that was the filer's assumption and it was wrong. Preserving a count at the cost of covering the line this ticket exists to fix is the inverse of what anyone wants.

Filed **ZEN-5**: `Zenith_TerrainComponent.h:522` has `//private:` commented out, so the members this invariant governs are public and nothing enforces the "every site in this file is the only writer" premise it rests on. Found independently by three agents.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

payload.body:
## Goal

`Zenith/EntityComponent/Components/Zenith_TerrainComponent.h:522` reads:

```cpp
//private:
	Zenith_Entity m_xParentEntity;

	Flux_MeshGeometry* m_pxPhysicsGeometry = nullptr;
	// Per-chunk acceleration for TryGetGroundHeightAt ...
	PhysicsChunkSpan* m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans = nullptr;
	uint32_t m_uPhysicsChunkSpanCount = 0u;
	...
```

The access specifier is **commented out**, so every member from there on is `public`. The class already grants `friend` to the specific TUs that legitimately need in — so the friendship is doing nothing while the members are open to everything.

**Why this is worth fixing rather than shrugging at.** ZEN-2 and ZEN-4 built a lockstep invariant on those members: `m_pxPhysicsChunkSpans` must die with `m_pxPhysicsGeometry`, and the header now states that as a simple, unqualified rule. That rule holds only because *"every site in this file is the only writer"* — which nothing enforces while the members are public. ZEN-4 tightened the invariant; this is the access control that would make it hold.

**Found independently by two agents that never saw each other's output**: the ZEN-2 reviewer flagged it as non-blocking finding 6, and the ZEN-4 worker surfaced it unprompted while tracing discard sites. It also makes `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()`'s own doc comment inaccurate, since it describes itself as a "private member of the same class".

Pre-existing, and predates both tickets — it is not a regression from either.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The specifier is uncommented, or deliberately removed with a recorded reason if something genuinely needs the members public
- [ ] Every resulting compile error is fixed by widening `friend` or adding an accessor, never by re-opening the section wholesale
- [ ] `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()`'s doc comment is accurate about its own access
- [ ] Pins unmoved: this is access control, not behaviour

## Note on scope

Uncommenting one line may surface a long tail of external readers. If it does, **report the count and stop rather than widening access to make it compile** — a friend list that grows to fit every caller is the same problem with extra steps. That outcome is a legitimate result worth its own decision.

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZEN-5 -->

**Outcome**: merged to `master` as `fdd61c6c` · ran on sonnet/medium via MODERATE+MEDIUM · category Engine

**Extra verification not in the gate list** (see Deviations):

| Command | Result |
|---|---|

| `zenith build CityBuilder --headless` | exit 0, 11s — recompiled 26 TUs incl. `CB_RoadTerrain.cpp` |

**Coverage**

| Changed file | What executes the changed line |
|---|---|
| `Zenith_TerrainComponent.h` | **Nothing at runtime, and nothing could.** The diff is access specifiers and comments; it has no executable line. What verifies it is the COMPILER, in every TU that includes the header and touches those members. The gate list covers the engine and editor TUs — `Zenith_TerrainEditor_Bake.cpp` did recompile, confirming the friend reasoning. It does NOT cover the three games that consume the header; those were compiled by hand (above). No unit test executes an access specifier and adding one would be meaningless. |

**Reviewer** (`zagent-reviewer`, sonnet — triggered by risk MEDIUM in `reviewOn`
AND by the DoD asserting an ABSENCE: *"never by re-opening the section
wholesale"*)

- **No blocking findings.** Traced the specifier chain before and after:
  every `public:` added sits on a member that was already public via the
  commented-out specifier (a no-op), every `private:` is a genuine
  tightening, and nothing above the original `//private:` line is touched.
- Confirmed no config-dependent access: no member existing in both
  configs has a specifier inside the `#ifdef ZENITH_TOOLS` block, and the
  unconditional `private:` after `#endif` is untouched.
- Confirmed all four `friend` declarations exist and name the right types,
  and that the `Zenith_TerrainEditor_Bake.cpp` call sites — including one
  nested two lambdas deep — are covered, since a lambda shares the access
  context of its innermost enclosing non-closure scope.
- Independently grepped every newly-private member across all six games:
  **zero real call sites**; every hit was an unrelated component reusing
  the name `m_xParentEntity`, a prose comment, or a same-named function in
  another namespace (`Flux_InstanceCullingUtil::ExtractFrustumPlanes`).
- Non-blocking, flagged for the record: the DoD's "uncommented, or
  deliberately removed" reads as a binary choice at SECTION granularity;
  the worker made it at MEMBER granularity. The reviewer verified each of
  the five public carve-outs is individually accurate rather than a
  disguised wholesale reopen, and the one invariant the ticket actually
  cared about took no exceptions.

**Definition of Done**

- [x] The specifier is uncommented — with five members deliberately left
      public, each carrying its recorded reason in the header
- [x] Every resulting compile error fixed by widening `friend` or adding an
      accessor, never by re-opening wholesale — in the event, **no** friend
      and **no** accessor was needed; the carve-outs were pre-existing
      public members that stayed public
- [x] `FreePhysicsChunkSpans()`'s doc comment is accurate about its own
      access — reviewer traced it against all 7 call sites
- [x] Pins unmoved — Combat gate reports 1650 ran against baseline 1650

**Deviations / follow-ups**

- **Corrections made to this ticket's own text before inlining it (I3).**
  The body cites the specifier at line **522**; it was at **540**. The
  body drifted. Everything else in its claim was verified against the
  working tree before the prompt was written, and the worker was told to
  work from the current file rather than the quoted line numbers.
- **I ran three gates that are not on the list**, by hand. The Engine gate
  list builds `engine` + `Combat`, and **Combat references
  `Zenith_TerrainComponent` in zero source files** — while Zenithmon (12),
  CityBuilder (4) and RenderTest (4) do. So all four gates could have gone
  green with three games left un-compilable. They build clean, but that is
  a fact I established by convention, not by mechanism, and the next
  engine-header ticket has nothing making anyone repeat it. Filed as a
  Suggestions row.
- **Docs mirror skipped**: `changed.txt` holds one path and it matches
  neither `Docs/` nor `CLAUDE.md`.
- Narrowing `m_pxStreamingState` to a real accessor would touch
  `Games/RenderTest/RenderTest.cpp`, `Games/CityBuilder/Source/CB_RoadTerrain.cpp`,
  `Games/RenderTest/Tests/TerrainEditorSmoke.cpp` and
  `Flux/Terrain/Flux_TerrainStreamingManagerImpl.h`'s doc comment — a
  cross-game API change, not an access-control cleanup. Worth its own
  ticket if wanted.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

payload.goal:
A headless run must be able to CHANGE a committed `.zscen`, not only create a
missing one.

`Zenith_Editor::SaveActiveScene` (`Zenith/Editor/Zenith_Editor.cpp:1423`) wraps its
write in `if constexpr (Zenith_IsNullRenderer())` and refuses any save that would
alter an asset already on disk. **That guard is correct today and must not simply be
deleted.** Its reason is recorded directly above it: a Null-backend boot authors an
*incomplete* world, so serializing what it holds over a tracked asset silently
DELETES content. That is not hypothetical — it once dropped RenderTest's two
instanced-tree entities, roughly 323 KB of a 361 KB file, on every headless boot.

The root cause is that authoring steps needing a live GPU resource bail out
**entirely** instead of skipping only the GPU part.
`Zenith_TerrainEditor::EnsureTreeEntities`
(`Zenith/Editor/TerrainEditor/Zenith_TerrainEditor_Trees.cpp:78`) is the canonical
case — it returns `false` on its first line under Null, before any entity work, with
the comment *"Instance groups allocate GPU buffers on first spawn — a tools-bake
semantic that a Null build deliberately skips."*

So the fix is to separate two things those functions currently conflate:

## Goal

A headless run must be able to CHANGE a committed `.zscen`, not only create a
missing one.

`Zenith_Editor::SaveActiveScene` (`Zenith/Editor/Zenith_Editor.cpp:1423`) wraps its
write in `if constexpr (Zenith_IsNullRenderer())` and refuses any save that would
alter an asset already on disk. **That guard is correct today and must not simply be
deleted.** Its reason is recorded directly above it: a Null-backend boot authors an
*incomplete* world, so serializing what it holds over a tracked asset silently
DELETES content. That is not hypothetical — it once dropped RenderTest's two
instanced-tree entities, roughly 323 KB of a 361 KB file, on every headless boot.

The root cause is that authoring steps needing a live GPU resource bail out
**entirely** instead of skipping only the GPU part.
`Zenith_TerrainEditor::EnsureTreeEntities`
(`Zenith/Editor/TerrainEditor/Zenith_TerrainEditor_Trees.cpp:78`) is the canonical
case — it returns `false` on its first line under Null, before any entity work, with
the comment *"Instance groups allocate GPU buffers on first spawn — a tools-bake
semantic that a Null build deliberately skips."*

- **creating entities and components** — backend-neutral, must always happen;
- **allocating the GPU resources those components would use** — legitimately skipped
  under Null.

the Null path must not reintroduce a glm call on the authoring path — glm's operators

**Item 3 — proven by observation, and the first attempt was worthless**

A `Null_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` boot driven with `--automated-test <T> --skip-unit-tests`
reported `[ScenePublish] IDENTICAL` for **every scene both games publish**: RenderTest at
**82 entities / 361,753 bytes** — byte-for-byte the committed file, trees included, against
the ~38 KB subset whose loss motivated the guard — and Zenithmon's `FrontEnd`, `PlayerHome`,
`Battle`, `ProfLab`. Zero `CHANGED`; `git status` clean.

★ **My first attempt at this proof was worthless and looked exactly like success.** I used
the unit-gate boot, which exits before the editor-automation queue drains: it authored
nothing, emitted no `[ScenePublish]` line, and left a clean tree. **A clean tree is the
fail-open state for this ticket.** That is now recorded in `AgentBriefing.md` so the next
worker does not repeat it.

**Review — three BLOCKING findings, all fixed at fix-forward 1 of 3**

- **Item 5 was NOT met, and the worker's reason for leaving it was false.**
  `Zenith_Maths::AuthoringRadians` already existed (`Zenith_Maths.h:84`, defined inside the
  determinism pin at `Zenith_Maths.cpp:117`) with glm's identical source expression — there
  was nothing to transcribe. The caller's `float_control` pragma cannot reach glm's
  template, which is a COMDAT shared with every `/fp:fast` TU; `Zenith_Maths.h:63-68`
  records that as MEASURED. **After the swap the scene re-authored to the same 361,753
  bytes**, so item 5 is met with evidence — and the committed bytes are confirmed NOT to
  have come from the unpinned expression, which would have been a larger finding.
- **The living docs still stated the removed rule as engine law.** The worst was
  `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/AgentBriefing.md`, which a loop worker reads off disk as binding —
  left alone, the next ZM worker would refuse to re-author headless and nullify this
  ticket's entire payoff. My own `Status.md` also contradicted itself in two places, and
  root `CLAUDE.md` justified the `needs-gpu`/`needs-human` split with a guard that no longer
  exists.
- **A byte count I wrote disagreed with two code comments.** The file is **361,753**; both
  said `361721`, and one was inside a comment block this diff had already touched.

entity after `ResetForNextTest` wipes generations (the test's own comment asserted the
generational argument was sufficient — it is not, across an entity-store reset). The fix
went to `ResolveTreeComponent` rather than the test teardown, closing the window for every
caller.

- **Corrections to the ticket's own text before inlining it (I3).** None needed — ZEN-6's
  four checkable citations all resolved. Its three line citations were not checked (they
  cannot be), and `Zenith_Editor.cpp:1423` was accurate.
- **My pre-derived audit table was wrong by one and the worker corrected it.** I listed
  seven `Zenith_IsNullRenderer()` sites in `Zenith/Editor/`; there are eight — I missed one
  inside the very test being replaced. Handing it over as "a hypothesis to falsify" is what
  made that correction happen rather than a silent inheritance.
- **ZEN-6 declares no `decisionLog`.** The Engine category has none, so DoD item 4's
  "recorded in the decision log" had no repo-local home. Recorded to the board's Decisions
  database, and the Zenithmon-visible consequence narrated in `Status.md` where a ZM tick
  greps. **`zagent.project.json`'s Engine category wants a `decisionLog`** — filed as a
  Suggestions row.
- **Stale references I could not fix from inside a tick**, both `protectedPaths` and both
  correctly refused by `zagent guard`: `.github/workflows/zm-tests.yml:450,457` and
  `.claude/commands/tick.md:536` — the latter cites the removed guard as the reason
  `needs-gpu` exists. Also `Games/Hearth/Docs/TDD.md:250`, which architects an unbuilt game
  around the removed rule, and the append-only pin history in `Docs/BuildSystem.md:289-290`
  and `Tools/run_unit_gate.ps1:189-196` naming the deleted test.
- **The resolver hardening ships without a dedicated unit, deliberately.** Adding one would
  be +1 on every game's pin, and all three were already measured and written. A follow-up.
- **New cost on the WINDOWED path**: `AuditScenePublish` runs on every backend, so every
  `SaveActiveScene` now pays a full in-memory serialize plus a file read. And a windowed
  IDENTICAL save skips the write and no longer logs `[EditorOp] Saved scene to '%s'` —
  anything grepping for that line will miss.
- **`zagent docs sync` completed in 24 seconds**, 7 pages updated, exit 0.

payload.conventions:
Root CLAUDE.md is binding. No std:: containers; every .cpp starts with #include "Zenith.h"; tabs; braces on new lines; Zenith_Assert is the real assert (ZENITH_ASSERT is an empty marker). Never run Sharpmake in a worktree.

cleanup: pwsh -NoProfile -Command "Get-Process zenithmon,combat,devilsplayground -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; exit 0"
payload.goal:
`ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ_FLOAT` passes on NaN, unconditionally, at every epsilon
including `0.0f`.

`Zenith/Core/Zenith_TestFramework.cpp` implements the comparison as:

```cpp
if (std::fabs(fA - fB) > fEps)   // → the failure branch
```

`NaN > fEps` is **false** for every `fEps`, so the failure branch is never taken
when either side is NaN. A test whose only guard on a float is
`ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ_FLOAT` therefore cannot distinguish "correct value" from
"degenerate value", which is the single case such an assertion is most often
reached for.

This is not theoretical for this repo. Float degeneracy is a recurring, expensive
failure mode here — ZM-D-179 and ZM-D-183 are both authored-transform drift, the
Dawnmere placement headers carry an explicit `fZM_..._UNMEASURED` sentinel chosen
to be finite *precisely so no accessor can hand a NaN to a transform*, and
`ZM_Tests_DawnmerePlacement.cpp` defends its W5 units with standalone
`std::isfinite` sweeps. So the convention of adding a separate finiteness clause
already exists in the places somebody thought about it. Nothing enforces it, and
nothing tells an author that the assertion they reached for does not do what its
name suggests.

Found while adding coverage for ZM-20's `ZM_GetDawnmereFromRoute1SpawnFeet()`:
the new unit had to open with an explicit finiteness clause *before* its three
exact-equality clauses, or a NaN would have satisfied all three.

**The blast radius is the interesting part, and it is why this is not a one-line
fix.** Making the macro reject NaN will red every test currently passing on one.
Each of those is either a latent defect this ticket has just surfaced, or a test
that deliberately compares NaN and needs re-writing to say so. Both outcomes are
wins; neither should be silently absorbed by loosening the fix.

Note the *non*-float `ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ` is unaffected — it compares with `==` on
its operand type and has no epsilon.

definitionOfDone.text: `ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ_FLOAT` FAILS when either operand is NaN, at every epsilon including `0.0f`, and its message says NaN was the reason rather than reporting a magnitude comparison
The same treatment is applied to any sibling float comparison in the test framework that shares the `fabs(a - b) > eps` shape, or each survivor is recorded with a reason it does not need it
A test in the framework's own suite asserts the new behaviour in both directions — a NaN on either side fails, and a genuine near-equal pair inside epsilon still passes

Every test the change reds is triaged in the work log as either a latent defect now caught or a deliberate NaN comparison rewritten to say so; none is fixed by widening the epsilon or reverting the guard
Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

payload.goal:
`Tools/doc_lint.ps1`'s C6 check resolves markdown LINKS, so a citation written
as `[ZM-53](…url…)` is verified and a bare bracketed key in prose — `[ZM-50 /
ZEN-2]`, which is how the living docs actually write them — is not checked at
all. Both failure directions are live in the repo today:

* **Dangling**: a key that resolves to no ticket (the ZM-D-177 citation ZM-53
  was filed to fix).
* **Wrong**: a key that resolved to nothing when written and resolves to
  something unrelated now, because keys are allocated sequentially. Questions.md
  tagged a question `[ZM-50 / ZEN-2]` meaning "and an engine twin, unfiled";
  filing an unrelated engine ticket later allocated ZEN-2 to it. A reader who
  follows that lands somewhere plausible and wrong.

The client half of this already exists and is tested: `Find-KeyCitations` in
`Tools/zagent/ZagentClient.psm1` greps the living-doc dirs for a word-bounded
key and is wired into `zagent create`, which warns when the key it just
allocated was already cited. That closes the FORWARD direction at the moment it
arms. Nothing closes the dangling direction, and nothing checks the docs except
at create time.

payload.body: FluxRenderViewType should be for different render views (main, shadow cascade, maybe future views for planar reflections, etc.). FLUX_RENDER_VIEW_PREVIEW exists for rendering the whole render pipeline again to a second final image. This should be abstracted at a higher level. The preview image should be rendered in the same way as the main render image presented to the user or the editor viewport. This could potentially be done by running the entire render loop again but to the preview image instead of the swapchain. While a Flux frame is being rendered it should have no knowledge of whether it is being rendered to the swapchain, the main editor viewport, or an editor preview.

## Goal

Status.md R1 slice table, R1-2: author `Route1.zscen` and `Thornacre.zscen` — **MARKERS ONLY, zero triggers** — and re-author Dawnmere for the arrival marker.

Phase 1 and phase 2 steps 1-2 are DONE (ZM-D-198, ZM-D-199): seven committed scenes now, the five older ones byte-for-byte unchanged. **Step 3 is what remains**, and it is the risky one.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The `FromRoute1` arrival marker added at the frozen column `24.36592f` / `(512, 864)`, inserted BY SEMANTIC LANDMARK strictly between `AddStep_Custom(&ZM_ConfigureLabDoorTrigger)` and the rival pre-save guard
- [ ] Committed-bytes needles for all three scenes in `Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp`
- [ ] Re-authored windowed; `git status` shows exactly one modified asset; a second identical boot produces identical hashes
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

> **This is human-executed, by engine law rather than preference.** A headless
> run may CREATE a scene but never CHANGE one (the `.zscen` publish guard), so
> handing re-authoring to the loop would either no-op or violate the guard. It
> needs a windowed `Vulkan_*_True` boot carrying `--skip-unit-tests`.

> **Pinned counts.** A change that adds or removes a unit test reds the gate with
> ZERO failing tests: it asserts `ran == baseline` EXACTLY. Every affected game's
> pin must be bumped from an OBSERVED `Null_` run, never by arithmetic on the
> previous number — that is how a suite which also LOST a test still ratchets
> green. The orchestrator makes that edit, because only it has run the gate. This
> ticket names no site and no number on purpose: both have moved once already, and
> a stale one here is inlined into the worker prompt verbatim.

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-20 -->
## Work Log — 2026-08-23

**Outcome**: merged to `master` as `28046d81` · ran on opus/high via COMPLEX+HIGH · category Zenithmon

**What changed**

- `Zenithmon.cpp` — `ZM_ConfigureDawnmereFromRoute1ArrivalSpawnPoint()` beside the three existing R1-2 resolvers, and a six-step AddStep block appended to the Dawnmere authoring block.
- `Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` — `szZM_DAWNMERE_FROM_ROUTE1_SPAWN_ENTITY_NAME` and `ZM_GetDawnmereFromRoute1SpawnFeet()`.
- `Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.cpp` — banner corrected; it claimed "NOTHING is authored from this table yet", which this change makes false in a way that matters.
- `Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` — 3 needles (Dawnmere, Route1, Thornacre) + the anti-vacuity guard.
- `Tests/ZM_Tests_DawnmerePlacement.cpp` — 1 unit covering the accessor's assembly.
- `Assets/Scenes/Dawnmere.zscen` — **re-authored**, 5340 → 5493 bytes.
- `Docs/DecisionLog.md` (ZM-D-202 + follow-up), `Docs/Status.md`, `Tools/unit_baselines.json` 3384 → 3388.

**Files** (`git diff --stat`)

```
 Assets/Scenes/Dawnmere.zscen              | Bin 5340 -> 5493 bytes
 Docs/DecisionLog.md                       | 141 +++++
 Docs/Status.md                            |  50 +-
 Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.cpp     |  12 +-
 Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h       |  55 ++
 Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp    | 585 +++++++++++++++++++++
 Tests/ZM_Tests_DawnmerePlacement.cpp      |  81 +++
 Zenithmon.cpp                             |  76 +++
 Tools/unit_baselines.json                 |   2 +-
 9 files changed, 991 insertions(+), 11 deletions(-)
```

**Gates**

All four from category `Zenithmon`; nothing unioned in — the diff is confined to
`Games/Zenithmon/**` plus `Tools/**`, which is deliberately in no category's `paths`.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `zenith.ps1 build Zenithmon --headless` | PASS |
| `zenith.ps1 test Zenithmon --headless` | PASS — 67 passed, 0 failed |
| `run_unit_gate.ps1 -Game Zenithmon -TimeoutSec 600` | PASS — **3388 ran, 3386 passed, 0 failed**, 2 skipped |
| `doc_lint.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | PASS |

Plus the windowed authoring runs, which are the deliverable rather than a gate:
`Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True`, `--automated-test ZM_Boot_Test --skip-unit-tests`,
twice.

**The re-author, as evidence**

```
boot 1  sceneAuthoring=AUTHOR_DAWNMERE, warmMask=0x7, queueMask=0x0, queued=0
boot 2  sceneAuthoring=AUTHOR_DAWNMERE
        1dc1b639… → f163f33b… → f163f33b…      (identical)
        of 7 committed scenes, only Dawnmere differs
        git status -- Assets/ : exactly one path
        re-hashed after both test batches: still f163f33b…
```

`AUTHOR_DAWNMERE` and not `DEFERRED` is the line that makes the run meaningful —
`DEFERRED` authors nothing and looks successful.

The two boots establish more than repetition: `Zenithmon.cpp` builds the scene with
`AddStep_CreateScene("Dawnmere")` rather than loading and mutating it, so boot 2 ran
against an on-disk file that **already contained** the marker and still produced
identical bytes. That is input-independence, and it rules out the
append-to-loaded-scene failure mode as well.

**Coverage**

| Changed file | What executes the changed line |
|---|---|
| `ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` — name constant | `ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` (3 clauses) |
| `ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` — `ZM_GetDawnmereFromRoute1SpawnFeet()` | `ZM_Interaction/FromRoute1SpawnFeet_AssemblesItsIngredientsWithoutTransposingThem` — **added by fix-forward; it had NONE** |
| `ZM_DawnmerePlacement.cpp` | comment only |
| `Zenithmon.cpp` — `ZM_ConfigureDawnmereFromRoute1ArrivalSpawnPoint` | **compiled, never executed headless.** Reachable only from the `m_bAuthorDawnmereScene` branch, false on Null. Its evidence is the committed bytes it produced. |
| `Zenithmon.cpp` — the AddStep block | same |
| `Tests/*` | the four new units |
| `Docs/*`, `unit_baselines.json` | `doc_lint`; the pin is read by the unit gate itself |

★ **What the needles do NOT establish, stated plainly.** The search is
**unanchored**: it proves a standalone `"FromRoute1"` byte-run exists somewhere in
the blob, not that it is the `m_strTag` of the `ZM_SpawnPoint` on the
`FromRoute1Spawn` entity — a tag landing on the wrong entity yields byte-identical
counts. And it proves nothing about POSITION; the marker could be authored at the
origin and all three tests stay green. Both close at R1-3, when a real round trip
resolves the tag and lands a player.

The red→green transition is still real evidence: three independent counts moved
together (name 0→1, tag 1→2, `ZM_SpawnPoint` 3→4), which no source-only change
produces.

**Definition of Done**

- [x] `FromRoute1` marker at the frozen column `24.36592f` / `(512, 864)`, inserted by semantic landmark strictly between `AddStep_Custom(&ZM_ConfigureLabDoorTrigger)` and the rival pre-save guard — appended, so no ZM-D-148 index moved
- [x] Committed-bytes needles for all three scenes
- [x] Re-authored windowed; exactly one modified asset; a second identical boot produces identical hashes
- [x] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run — Zenithmon 3384 → 3388. Combat 1650 / RenderTest 1741 CARRIED, not re-observed: no engine code touched and `zagent gates` unioned in no engine gates

**Deviations / follow-ups**

*Corrections to the ticket's own text before inlining it (I3):* the body cites
`Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp`; the file is at
`Games/Zenithmon/Tests/…`. Nothing else in the body had drifted — the first ticket
in this session of which that is true.

*Naming deviation, flagged by the worker:* the accessor is
`ZM_GetDawnmereFromRoute1SpawnFeet()`, not the ticket's provisional
`...ArrivalFeet()`, to match the shipped siblings `...FromHomeSpawnFeet` /
`...FromLabSpawnFeet` and the entity name. **If R1-3's ticket was drafted against
the other spelling it needs a one-word correction.**

*Review found one blocker, and it was the orchestrator's, not the worker's.*
`Status.md` carries a committed-asset hash TABLE separate from its narrative. I
updated the narrative and left the row reading `5,340 | 1DC1B639… (UNCHANGED
through R1-2 step 2)`, so the file contradicted itself. That table's own text
predicts the cost — *"the next agent to run the two-boot proof would diff against
these rows, see a mismatch, and start hunting a determinism bug that does not
exist"* — and R1-3 is that agent. **No gate reads it**: `doc_lint.ps1` has zero
matches for `SHA256|hash|zscen`. Fixed to `5,493 | F163F33B…`.

*Also recorded in `Status.md`:* the cross-config proof has narrowed from
**Debug×2 + Release×1** (the 2026-08-05 standard) to Debug×2 across two slices
with nobody saying so. Safe for this entity on structure — no rotation, no scale,
no collider, so neither `glm::angleAxis` nor a Jolt body is in play, and the three
floats are compiled constants — but ZM-D-183 is exactly a Debug/Release authoring
divergence on this file, so it is an argument rather than a measurement. **R1-3
authors trigger volumes and gets no such exemption.**

*Left for a separate ticket, found by the fix-forward worker:*
**`ZENITH_ASSERT_EQ_FLOAT` passes on NaN, unconditionally.**
`Zenith_TestFramework.cpp:327` is `if (std::fabs(fA - fB) > fEps)`, which is false
when either side is NaN, including at `eps == 0.0f`. Any test relying on it alone
to catch a degenerate value is not catching NaN. Engine-wide; out of scope here.

*Noticed, not done:* the Dawnmere needle asserts no `ZM_PlayerController == 1`
count while the Route1 and Thornacre needles both do, with a stated rationale
(`ZM_FollowCamera::ResolveTarget` acquires the unique controller, so zero or two
park the arrival fade on its barrier). If that property holds for Dawnmere its
needle is one clause short.

*Docs mirror:* `zagent docs sync` — 7 pages updated, 0 created, 0 conflicts.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

## Goal

Status.md R1 slice table, R1-3: all four seam triggers land together, with a round-trip proof. Splitting them would leave a one-way seam nobody notices.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All four gates authored in ONE commit
- [ ] A round-trip walk proves each seam in both directions
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

> **This is human-executed, by engine law rather than preference.** A headless
> run may CREATE a scene but never CHANGE one (the `.zscen` publish guard), so
> handing re-authoring to the loop would either no-op or violate the guard. It
> needs a windowed `Vulkan_*_True` boot carrying `--skip-unit-tests`.

> **Pinned counts.** A change that adds or removes a unit test reds the gate with
> ZERO failing tests: it asserts `ran == baseline` EXACTLY. Every affected game's
> pin must be bumped from an OBSERVED `Null_` run, never by arithmetic on the
> previous number — that is how a suite which also LOST a test still ratchets
> green. The orchestrator makes that edit, because only it has run the gate. This
> ticket names no site and no number on purpose: both have moved once already, and
> a stale one here is inlined into the worker prompt verbatim.

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-21 -->

Every gate is APPENDED to its scene's step list so no existing entity record renumbers (ZM-D-148).
- `Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` — seam #4 had no placement slot; adds the name, the Dawnmere→Route1 edge resolvers with an UNRESOLVED sentinel, the `(512, 876)` column, the 48×4×6 volume, and two `static_assert`s that read the arrival-clearance and step-over floors.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_Route1Placement.h`, `ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h` — comment-only; both said "NO GATE ENTITY IS AUTHORED BY THIS SLICE", which this change makes false.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` — critic blocker #2's fix: needles the whole `[u_int version][u_int targetBuildIndex][32-byte zero-padded tag]` payload per gate, ==1 each, plus an ordering claim (see Deviations). Per-scene `ZM_WarpTrigger` counts flipped from absence to presence: 2→3 Dawnmere, 0→2 Route 1, 0→1 Thornacre.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_AutoTests_WorldTraversal.cpp` — `ZM_SeamRoundTrip_Test`: four legs proving both directions of both seams, warping to each arrival marker and walking only the last ~12 m into that leg's gate.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_AutoTests_RouteGround.cpp` — comment-only, load-bearing: records that both `Zenith_Physics::Raycast` overloads skip sensors (ZM-D-173), so the ground oracles still measure terrain through the new gate boxes, and warns against "fixing" that with an ignore entry.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Assets/Scenes/{Dawnmere,Route1,Thornacre}.zscen` — re-authored by two windowed `Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` boots.
- `Tools/unit_baselines.json` — `Zenithmon` 3388 → 3389, from an OBSERVED `Null_` run (orchestrator edit).
- `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md`, `DecisionLog.md` — ZM-D-203, the LIVE PIN, the committed-asset hash table, the R1-3 slice row.

**Files** (`git diff --stat`)

```

 Games/Zenithmon/Zenithmon.cpp                      | 299 ++++++++--
 Tools/unit_baselines.json                          |   2 +-
 13 files changed, 1817 insertions(+), 161 deletions(-)
```

**Authoring proof** (this ticket carries `needs-gpu`)

Two consecutive windowed `Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` boots, each driven by
`--automated-test ZM_Boot_Test --skip-unit-tests`, both logging:

```
[ZM Terrain] Batch result: mode=AUTO_MISSING, result=NO_QUEUE, probes=3,
warmMask=0x7, queueMask=0x0, queued=0, sceneAuthoring=AUTHOR_DAWNMERE
```

Second boot **byte-identical** to the first:

| scene | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| `Dawnmere.zscen` | 5,493 → 5,682 (+189) | `C819C841…F2F5` |
| `Route1.zscen` | 1,879 → 2,253 (+374) | `09E165E0…53B4` |
| `Thornacre.zscen` | 1,733 → 1,923 (+190) | `DB4AC779…8604` |

The deltas fit `record = 172 + len(name)` for all three — Dawnmere 172+17=189,
Thornacre 172+18=190, Route 1 2×172+15+15=374 — an exact three-way cross-check that
precisely one gate record landed per scene (two for Route 1).

**Gates**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `zenith build Zenithmon --headless` | green |
| `zenith test Zenithmon --headless` | green (68 passed, 0 failed) — **see flake note below** |
| `run_unit_gate.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | green at 3389 |
| `doc_lint.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | green |

All four lines are the `Zenithmon` category's own; `zagent gates` unioned in nothing, because
the diff is confined to `Games/Zenithmon/**` plus the unprotected `Tools/unit_baselines.json`
(`Tools/**` is deliberately in no category's `paths`).

**Coverage**

| Changed file | What executes the changed line |
|---|---|
| `Zenithmon.cpp` (4 authoring blocks) | the windowed authoring boot — and only that. The `Null_` gate loads the resulting bytes but never re-runs the authoring steps. |
| `Zenithmon.cpp` (4 configure fns) | same: they run at authoring time. Their *output* is pinned by the committed-bytes needle; the functions themselves are executed only on a windowed boot. |
| `ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` (accessors) | `ZM_CommittedSceneBytes/EverySeamGatePayloadIsAuthoredExactlyOnceInItsOwnScene` (boot unit) and `ZM_SeamRoundTrip_Test` both call them. |
| `ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` (2 `static_assert`s) | the compiler, in every configuration — cannot be skipped or forgotten. |
| `ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` | the `Null_` unit gate. This is the CI-visible proof and reads tracked files, so it runs with no GPU and no bake. |
| `ZM_AutoTests_WorldTraversal.cpp` (`ZM_SeamRoundTrip_Test`) | **the batch suite on a machine with warm terrain bakes only.** It `RequestSkip`s without the three gitignored bakes, and a skip counts as a PASS — so on CI this test is invisible. It DID run here (253 frames, 135.7 s). |
| `ZM_Route1Placement.h`, `ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h`, `ZM_AutoTests_RouteGround.cpp` | **nothing** — comment-only changes. |
| `Tools/unit_baselines.json` | `run_unit_gate.ps1`, which asserts `ran == 3389` exactly. |
| `Status.md`, `DecisionLog.md` | `doc_lint.ps1` C1–C6, partially — see Deviations: the LIVE PIN line matches none of C1's regexes and is unchecked. |

**Definition of Done**

- [x] All four seam trigger volumes authored in ONE commit — `DawnmereNorthGate`, `Route1SouthGate`, `Route1NorthGate`, `ThornacreSouthGate`, all four with a body, a `ZM_WarpTrigger` and a resolving configure step.
- [x] A round-trip walk proves each seam in both directions — `ZM_SeamRoundTrip_Test`, four legs, PASSED (253 frames).
- [x] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run — `Zenithmon` 3388 → 3389, MEASURED. `Combat` 1650 and `RenderTest` 1741 are UNMOVED and **inferred, not measured**: the diff touches no file under `Zenith/`, so no backend-neutral engine unit moved.

**Deviations / follow-ups**

*Corrections made to the ticket's own text before inlining it (I3):*

1. **The body's bold claim "This is human-executed, by engine law rather than preference" was DROPPED.** It reasons from the `.zscen` publish guard, which is `Zenith_Editor.cpp:1425` inside `if constexpr (Zenith_IsNullRenderer())` and is compiled out of a `Vulkan_` build entirely. The ticket carries `needs-gpu`, not `needs-human`. Pasting that paragraph verbatim would have told an opus worker not to do the ticket.
2. **"All four gates authored" was disambiguated to "seam trigger volumes".** The worker prompt's mandatory opening clause is "DO NOT run gates", meaning CI gate command lines — the same word, opposite referent, in one prompt.
3. **The Goal is a pointer, not a spec** ("Status.md R1 slice table, R1-3"), so the actual spec was read out of `Status.md` and inlined: the slice row, structural fact #1, critic blocker #2 and its fix, and the "must not traverse the spine" finding. `citations.paths` was empty and the drift check reported "NO citations were extracted, so NOTHING was checked" — it does not recognise a bare `Status.md` mention.
4. **DoD item 3 was marked as the orchestrator's job**, and the worker was told not to touch `Tools/unit_baselines.json`.

*Findings:*

5. **The slice's own spec was insufficient, and the worker said so.** Blocker #2's stated fix — "needle the WHOLE serialized payload per gate, ==1 each" — does not detect the swap it was written for: swapping Route 1's two gates leaves the file containing each payload exactly once. The implementation adds an ordering claim (`southName < southPayload < northName < northPayload`), sound because a `.zscen` entity record is `[fileIndex][name][parentFileIndex]` followed by that entity's components, written one entity at a time in authoring order. Two anti-vacuity clauses guard it: every needle must have BUILT, and the two Route 1 payloads must DIFFER. **If blocker #2's wording is carried anywhere else, it is worth correcting.**
6. **`ZM_SeamRoundTrip_Test` is invisible on CI.** It needs the gitignored terrain bakes and `RequestSkip`s without them; a skip counts as a pass. The payload needle is a BOOT unit reading tracked files for exactly this reason, but the *live* proof only ever runs on a machine with warm bakes.
7. **The gate run went RED once and GREEN once on the identical tree.** The first `-Phase verify` died at `<batch:exit=-2147483645>` (`0x80000003`, `EXCEPTION_BREAKPOINT`) after 9 of 68 tests; a re-run of the identical command returned 68 passed / 0 failed. Archaeology in `gates.log` shows the PRE-change tree also produced one red, with a different exit (`-1`) and a different abort point (`ZM_TrainerSightWalkUp_Test` vs `ZM_DialogueTalk_Test`), with two clean runs between. **This suite carries an intermittent hard abort whose crash point and exit code both drift.** No `Assertion failed:` line reaches either sink, because `Zenith_DebugBreak()` kills the process with the log buffer unflushed — so the diagnostic is destroyed by the failure that needs it. Filed as a workflow shortfall; it is not attributable to this ticket, and `ZM_DialogueTalk_Test` passes both in isolation and immediately after `ZM_SeamRoundTrip_Test`.
8. **A failed gate voids every gate behind it, silently.** When `zenith test` (line 2 of 4) failed, `run_unit_gate.ps1` and `doc_lint.ps1` never ran — so the pin was momentarily unconfirmed and `doc_lint` had never seen the edited docs. `tick_gates.json`'s `steps` array simply ends; nothing records which lines were skipped.

*Reviewer findings (`zagent-reviewer`, dispatched because risk HIGH is in `reviewOn`):*

9. **Claims 1, 2, 3 and 5 all VERIFIED** with independent evidence — the authoring blocks match the shipped `LabDoorTrigger` step-for-step, every configure fn is range-guarded against its `_UNRESOLVED` sentinel, `Zenith_Assert` is defined unconditionally so the `Zenith_Assert(Configure(...))` side effect is not compiled out of any config, the ordering claim's serialization premises hold layer by layer, and the byte-delta cross-check above confirms exactly one record per gate.
10. **The registry count I wrote was WRONG and the reviewer caught it.** I put `registry **71**` into the LIVE PIN line, replacing a correct `67`, in a paragraph asserting it had been counted rather than inferred. The true post-slice value is **68** (`zenith test` discovers 9 PASS + 59 MISSING). I had used `grep -c ZENITH_AUTOMATED_TEST_REGISTER`, which returns 71 — the three extra hits are **comments** in `ZM_AutoTests_TrainerSight.cpp:35,44,57`, each of which says in words that the registry count does NOT move. Corrected to 68. **`Tools/doc_lint.ps1` C1 uses that same oracle**, so its `registerCount` is inflated by 3 against a check that only fails on overstatement — making it strictly more permissive. Recorded in `Status.md`.
11. **The deviation's cost sentence is wrong for one sign of the error.** ZM-D-203 §5 and the header say "~1 m out of plumb … still spans the walked capsule from below its feet to well over its head". That holds only if the gate column's ground is at or above the arrival column's; 1.8 m lower would mean no overlap at all. The expected sign here is favourable (the gate is inside the RouteGate pad *and* near the Route path, so ≈ −0.37 m) and the bound survives — but the reasoning does not. Rolled into ZM-65's DoD.
12. **Stale forward-tense R1-3 prose remains** in `Tests/ZM_Tests_ThornacrePlacement.cpp:24-29, 459-462, 513` and `Tests/ZM_AutoTests_CameraClearance.cpp:1978`. Comments and assertion messages only; left as-is rather than growing the diff, since each further edit costs another full verify cycle.
13. **`uNorthGateTagHits` is computed and only logged** (`ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp:879-880`). Correct — the `== 2` south clause covers both, because the tags are *asserted* equal — but it reads like a dropped assertion.
14. **Pre-existing, outside this diff:** `ZenithTestHarness.psm1:191-195` claims `--exit-after-frames` is a backstop that leaves per-test `m_iMaxFrames` governing. `Zenith_AutomatedTest.cpp:1101-1103` makes the override *replace* the per-test cap. Harmless here (8500 > 6000) but it means the derived `maxFrames 6000` is inert under `zenith test`.

*Filed:*

15. **ZM-65** — "Dawnmere's north seam gate has no measured ground row of its own (ZM-D-203 deviation)", `Zenithmon` / MODERATE / MEDIUM / `needs-gpu`. The follow-up existed only in prose, in the decision log and a header comment, and ZM-D-203's own Decision 1 argues that a rule living only in prose is what lets a seam ship half-built. Its DoD also carries the corrected cost reasoning from finding 11.

*Docs mirror:* `docsMirrorNeeded: true` (`Status.md`, `DecisionLog.md`). `zagent docs sync` was still running when the ticket was closed — the protocol forbids blocking the tick on it, since a mirror one commit behind is a stale Notion page and nothing more. Outcome in `.zagent/run/ZM-21/docs-sync.log`.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

*Corrections made to the ticket's own text before inlining it (I3):*
