## Goal

The one known failing test in the windowed suite. It is invisible to CI: `requiresGraphics` tests are SKIPPED-as-PASSED headless, and a skip counts as a pass — so a green `zm-tests` run says nothing about it.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The test passes windowed, or is retired with a recorded reason

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-56 -->
ran on sonnet/medium via MODERATE+LOW · category Zenithmon

**Blocked — but the ticket's real question is now answered.** No worker was dispatched and no file changed; `master` is unmoved and clean.

**I ran it windowed.** ZM-D-177 left this as *"the cause is unattributed — recorded here as deferred work requiring a windowed re-examination"*. That re-examination is done: a fresh `Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` build driven with `--automated-test ZM_InteriorTintPixels_Test --skip-unit-tests` on an RTX 2060.

| | first-run calibration | ZM-D-177 | **today** |
|---|---|---|---|
| PlayerHome red/blue | 1.3045 | 1.1888 | **1.1898** |
| ProfLab red/blue | 1.0742 | 1.0684 | **1.0686** |
| gap (floor 0.15) | 0.2303 | 0.1204 | **0.1212** |

Deltas of ~0.001 against the recorded values — run-to-run noise. **The failure is stable and reproducible, not a flake**, and 266 frames of a 1100-frame budget means nothing timed out.

**It rules out all three causes the test enumerates.** The gap is not ~0, so the tint *did* reach the framebuffer. Both absolutes are not high, so it did *not* leak into ProfLab — ProfLab sits at 1.0686 against a 1.0742 calibration. The gap is not negative, so the bedroom is correctly the warmer room. What remains is that **PlayerHome's tint fell ~0.116 from calibration on its own**: present, correctly signed, too weak.

**Why this is Blocked rather than Done.** The DoD is *"the test passes windowed, or is retired with a recorded reason"*, and neither is available here:

- *Passes* requires strengthening PlayerHome's tint, which re-authors `Assets/Scenes/PlayerHome.zscen`. That is windowed **authoring** — a headless run may CREATE a `.zscen` but never CHANGE one, so the deliverable would be silently missing with every unit green. Filed as **ZM-63**, labelled `windowed`.
- *Retired* is the wrong call and the test says so itself: *"RECORD THAT, do NOT shrink the floor until it passes."* The test is correct, the failure is real, and 0.15 is the ZM-D-176 ruling's threshold rather than a tuning knob. Retiring it — or lowering `fPT_MIN_RATIO_MARGIN` — would buy a green gate by deleting the property under test.

**A note on reachability.** This ticket was nearly declined as unreachable on the reasoning that a `requiresGraphics` test cannot be run headlessly. True of an unattended CI loop; false of a `/tick` on a box with a GPU. `tick.md` step 2 now draws that distinction, because collapsing it declines work that took a 23-second build and one command — and here that work produced the measurement the ticket existed to get.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

## Goal

silhouette, not a rendering defect. `History.md` records the finding as "no
buildings; the Trade Post and Care Center are dialogue only".

**This ticket is the SIGN-OFF only.** The buildable half — authoring the Trade
Post and the Care Center into `Dawnmere.zscen` — is ZM-71, which BLOCKS this.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] A human visual sign-off that Dawnmere reads as a town

> **`needs-human` because of the DELIVERABLE, not because of the engine.** A
> visual sign-off is a person's judgement and no runner produces one. That is the
> permanent reason, and it is independent of how the scene gets authored.
>
> **★ THE PREVIOUS JUSTIFICATION HERE WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED.** It read:
> *"This is human-executed, by engine law rather than preference. A headless run
> may CREATE a scene but never CHANGE one (the `.zscen` publish guard), so
> handing re-authoring to the loop would either no-op or violate the guard."*
> **ZEN-6 removed that guard on 2026-08-26 (`cbebea74`)** — a headless boot now
> publishes a committed `.zscen`, and the guard never had anything to do with
> whether a human was present. Left standing, that paragraph would have been
> inlined verbatim into a worker prompt under I3, telling the worker its own task
> was impossible for a reason that no longer exists.
>
> **The operational conclusion survives, for a DIFFERENT reason.** ZEN-6
> deliberately did not change Zenithmon: `Zenithmon.cpp:3848` still defers
> Dawnmere's scene authoring on a Null backend by the game's own choice, logging
> `sceneAuthoring=DEFERRED`. So re-authoring `Dawnmere.zscen` does still need a
> windowed `Vulkan_*_True` boot carrying `--skip-unit-tests` (ZM-D-190) — which
> makes that work **`needs-gpu`**, a label that gates nothing and is claimed like
> any other. It was never a reason for `needs-human`.

| | first-run calibration | ZM-D-177 | **today** |
|---|---|---|---|
| PlayerHome red/blue | 1.3045 | 1.1888 | **1.1898** |

distance: Thornacre's two columns differ by 0.254 m, Route 1's south pair by 0.475 m and its

cost as "~1 m out of plumb against a 1.8 m body, so the sensor still spans the walked capsule
from below its feet to well over its head". That holds only when the gate column's ground sits
at or above the arrival column's. If the gate column were 1.8 m lower there would be no overlap
at all and the sensor would never fire. The expected sign here is favourable — the gate at

path (18 m radius), while the arrival at `(512, 864)` is only in the path corridor — so the
error is expected around −0.37 m and the sensor is safe today. The sentence should be corrected
along with the measurement.

  byte-identity proof does NOT catch this, because two pre-freeze boots are identical

  `Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` has no cross-check tying the ground-sample
  row name `"DawnmereNorthGate"` to `szZM_DAWNMERE_NORTH_GATE_ENTITY_NAME`, unlike the

  the JSON-verdict rule working exactly as written — the notification said "stopped".

payload.body:
## Goal

Route 1 still cannot emit a wild encounter in a real boot. `ZM-22` (R1-4) landed the data and
the proof — the retuned rate via a Route-1-specific constant, the id-tagged biome table, and a
bake-independent synthetic roll-seam proof — but deliberately did **not** land the half that
makes encounters actually fire, because that half needs scene content and R1-4 was scoped
"re-authors: none".

`ZM_TallGrassSystem` is registered (ECS order 109) and, per its own header, *"Shares its entity
with the terrain component"*. Every place it is attached anywhere in the codebase is
tools-only scene authoring — the editor-automation step list plus a scene save — and there is
no production code path that attaches it. `Route1.zscen` is already committed, so attaching it
is a **change** to a committed asset, not a create.

**This is the gap R1-4's own slice row could not close.** The R1 slice table budgets R1-4 as
re-authoring nothing, while Status.md's structural fact #2 says the system is *"attached to NO
authored scene, so no shipped scene can emit a wild encounter ... Route 1 is where it comes
alive."* Those two statements cannot both be satisfied by one pure slice. The ticket is the
resolution: do the authoring half on its own, where the windowed boot it needs is expected
rather than a surprise.

**A workaround was considered and rejected, and should stay rejected.** ZM-22's worker weighed a
runtime hook — on scene load, if the scene is a ROUTE and its terrain entity lacks the
component, add it — and declined: it invents an unreviewed architectural pattern for a
component whose header says it owns nothing but the transition, and it lands in
`OnAwake`-not-firing-on-runtime-`AddComponent` territory that this project's decision log has
already been burned by. Author the scene; do not add a hook.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `ZM_TallGrassSystem` is authored onto Route 1's terrain entity, appended after the
      existing terrain-grass block so no existing entity record renumbers
- [ ] Route 1's committed scene bytes are re-authored from a windowed boot, proven by two
      consecutive boots producing byte-identical output, with the authoring log line read
      rather than the exit code
- [ ] The committed-asset hash table in the living docs is re-observed in the same commit
- [ ] A walk into Route 1 grass produces a wild encounter at the retuned rate — the in-game
      claim R1-4 could only make at the data level
- [ ] The R1 slice table row for R1-4 stops saying PARTIAL
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-66 -->
## Work Log — 2026-08-24

**Outcome**: merged to `master` as `7d3d6c49` · ran on sonnet/medium via MODERATE+MEDIUM · category Zenithmon

**Route 1 can now emit a wild encounter.** This closes the half of R1-4 that ZM-22/ZM-D-204
deliberately left undone, so slice R1-4 is complete across the two tickets.

**What changed**

- `Games/Zenithmon/Zenithmon.cpp` — **one executable line**:
  `xAuto.AddStep_AddComponent("ZM_TallGrassSystem")`, at Route 1's call site
  (`:4183`), plus 28 lines recording why it is there and not elsewhere.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` — new clause
  `Route1CarriesTheTallGrassSystemAndThornacreAndDawnmereDoNot`.
- `Games/Zenithmon/Assets/Scenes/Route1.zscen` — re-authored, 2,253 → 2,287 bytes.
- `Tools/unit_baselines.json` — `Zenithmon` 3394 → 3395, OBSERVED (orchestrator edit).
- `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md`, `DecisionLog.md` — ZM-D-205, LIVE PIN, the committed-asset
  Route 1 row, the `+N` chain, and the R1-4 slice row (no longer PARTIAL).

**The decision this ticket turned on**

`ZM_QueueTerrainHostEntity` is shared by Route 1 (`:4153`) and **Thornacre** (`:4386`); Dawnmere
is authored inline. Putting the component in the helper — the obvious implementation — would have
given **Thornacre** tall grass, changing a scene ZM-D-196 rules a deliberate TRAVERSAL STUB. It
would have looked correct and passed a naive test. The component was attached at Route 1's call
site instead.

**Authoring proof** (`needs-gpu`)

Two consecutive windowed `Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` boots driven by
`--automated-test ZM_Boot_Test --skip-unit-tests`, both logging
`sceneAuthoring=AUTHOR_DAWNMERE, warmMask=0x7, queued=0`. Second boot byte-identical.

| scene | bytes | sha256 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Route1.zscen` | 2,253 → **2,287** (+34) | `F1486214…EED9` | one component record |
| `Thornacre.zscen` | 1,923 | `db4ac779…` | **BYTE-IDENTICAL** |
| `Dawnmere.zscen` | 5,682 | `c819c841…` | **BYTE-IDENTICAL** |

`git status` showed **exactly one** modified asset. That is the load-bearing evidence.

**Gates**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `zenith build Zenithmon --headless` | green |
| `zenith test Zenithmon --headless` | green (1269 s) |
| `run_unit_gate.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | green at **3395** |
| `doc_lint.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | green |

No regen: no source file was created. All four lines are the `Zenithmon` category's own; the diff
is confined to `Games/Zenithmon/**` plus the unprotected `Tools/unit_baselines.json`.

**Coverage**

| Changed file | What executes the changed line |
|---|---|
| `Zenithmon.cpp` (the authoring step) | the **windowed authoring boot** — and only that. The `Null_` gate loads the resulting bytes; it never re-runs the step. Its *output* is pinned by the committed-bytes clause below. |
| `ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` | the `Null_` unit gate. Bake-independent and GPU-independent by construction — reads tracked files. |
| `Route1.zscen` | every test that loads Route 1, plus the new clause byte-wise. |
| `Tools/unit_baselines.json` | `run_unit_gate.ps1`, asserting `ran == 3395` exactly. |
| `Status.md`, `DecisionLog.md` | `doc_lint.ps1`, partially — the LIVE PIN line matches none of C1's regexes. |
| **`ZM_TallGrassSystem::OnUpdate` at runtime on Route 1** | **nothing automated.** No live walk test was added (see follow-up 3). The review established by inspection that it *should* function; nothing in this commit proves it does. |

**Definition of Done**

- [x] `ZM_TallGrassSystem` authored onto Route 1's terrain entity
- [x] Route 1's committed bytes re-authored, two-boot byte-identical
- [x] Committed-asset hash table re-observed in this commit
- [~] **A walk into Route 1 grass produces a wild encounter** — established by inspection, not by
  an automated test. See follow-up 3; this is the honest limit of the commit.
- [x] The R1 slice table row for R1-4 no longer says PARTIAL
- [x] Pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run — 3394 → 3395 MEASURED; Combat/RenderTest
  inferred, not measured

**Deviations / follow-ups**

1. **No corrections were needed to the ticket text.** Unusually, the drift check returned
   *"all 3 checkable citations resolve"* — the first clean result in this session's three ticks.
   The body was written from the code rather than from memory, which is the whole difference.
2. **The reviewer's headline finding was a FALSE ALARM caused by a race**, and it is worth
   recording because an unattended loop could not have told. It reported `Status.md`'s LIVE PIN
   and hash table as stale, citing `:20-21` and `:207`. They were not: the reviewer had been
   dispatched in parallel with the orchestrator's own doc edits and read the file partway through
   them — it saw a block added second but not a change made first, and its line citations no
   longer matched the file (`:207` vs the actual `:223`). Verified after: LIVE PIN `3395`,
   Route 1 row `2,287 / F1486214…`, manifest `3395`. **Cause: the orchestrator parallelised a step
   the protocol deliberately serialises.** Step 6.3 puts the review after the gates and before the
   guard for exactly this reason. Its Claims 1–4 work was unaffected and excellent, because that
   was about code, which was frozen.
3. **No live walk test.** The worker declined to extend `ZM_AutoTests_TallGrass.cpp`'s Dawnmere
   test — a ~460-line state machine it could not compile or run — reasoning that extending it
   incorrectly would be worse than not extending it, and that such a test skips as a PASS without
   the gitignored bake anyway. Recorded as ZM-D-205 Decision 3. **The gap is real**: nothing
   automated proves an encounter actually fires on Route 1. Worth its own ticket.
4. **Review verified the mechanism against the engine, not the comment** — worth not
   re-deriving: `Zenith_Editor::CreateEntity` → `SelectEntity` → `AddComponentToSelected` keeps
   the most recently created entity selected and never re-selects, so an appended
   `AddStep_AddComponent` lands on the terrain host. Route 1's recipe already paints grass density
   to **0.78** against a 0.5 threshold (pre-dating this ticket). The ROUTE1 `ZM_WorldSpec` row
   carries a 3-slot encounter table and `uZM_ROUTE1_ENCOUNTER_RATE = 20u`.
   `GetTerrainAssetDirectory()` is a plain field, so attaching *after* `ZM_TerrainGrass` carries
   no `OnAwake` ordering hazard.
5. **Pre-existing and untouched:** `Status.md`'s "Notes for next agent" section still names
   ZM-20/R1-2 step 3 as the next task, several tickets behind the file's own cold-start block.
   Flagged independently by both the worker and the reviewer. Not this ticket's to fix; worth a
   doc-cleanup ticket.
6. **Consequence for ZM-22 and ZM-23.** R1-4's goal is now met across ZM-22 + ZM-66. ZM-22 closed
   **Blocked**, and a Blocked status does not release its `blocks` link to **ZM-23** (R1-5) —
   only a DONE-category status does. With this ticket merged, re-closing ZM-22 as Done is now
   honest rather than a goalpost move, and it is what releases the rest of the Route 1 sequence.
   Left for the owner, who is mid-decision on it.

*Docs mirror:* see `docs-sync.log`. Note this command hung on both previous ticks and had to be
killed at self-imposed caps; step 7 prescribes no bound.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

payload.body:
## Goal

The three Route 1 ground-item props authored by ZM-27 (ZM-D-207) render as
`ZM_GreyboxVisual` blockouts — the engine unit cube with a flat blockout colour,
0.6 m on a side. They read as placeholders because they are placeholders. Bring
them to the visual standard the rest of the game is held to.

Zenithmon generates and bakes all art procedurally from tools builds
(`Source/Gen/` is the existing pattern — see `ZM_BuildingGen` and
`ZM_HumanAppearance`), so this is a generator plus a material, not an imported
asset.

**Scope is the presentation only.** The three props are
`ZM_GROUND_ITEM_ROUTE1_SOUTH_SALVE`, `ZM_GROUND_ITEM_ROUTE1_LANE_CATCHORB` and
`ZM_GROUND_ITEM_ROUTE1_NORTH_SALVE`. The pickup rule
(`ZM_CanPickUpGroundItem` / `ZM_TryPickUpGroundItem`), the prop registry, the
`ZM_GroundItemProp` component contract and save module 12 all shipped in ZM-27
and must not change.

★ **THE MEASURED ANCHORS ARE FROZEN AND THE REACH BUDGET IS TIGHT.** Each prop
stands on its own measured ground column, and
`Route1_GroundItemPropsAreReachableFromTheWalkedLane` holds them inside
`fZM_INTERACT_MAX_DISTANCE` (2.5 m) of the walked lane, with perpendicular
offsets of 1.60 / 2.00 / 1.75 m. A visual pass that makes a prop physically
larger must keep its interact origin where it is — growing the mesh is fine,
moving the anchor is not, and a prop nudged off the lane can never be picked up
in any playthrough while every other check stays green.

★ **AND A PROP HAS NO COLLIDER, DELIBERATELY** (ZM-D-207). Adding one would put
an obstacle in the walked lane and a SOLID body over the prop's own ground
column, which `ZM_Route1GroundTruth_Test` treats as a failure rather than a
filter. Presentation must not introduce one.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Each of the three props renders with a purpose-built mesh and material
      rather than the `ZM_GreyboxVisual` blockout cube
- [ ] The two item kinds are distinguishable from each other on sight at the
      distance a player walks past them, not only in a close-up
- [ ] A prop the current save has already collected does not still read as a
      pickup — its presentation matches the inert state
      `ZM_GroundItemProp::IsInteractable()` already reports
- [ ] Each prop still sits on its own measured ground column with its interact
      origin unmoved, and no prop gains a collider
- [ ] If authored transforms change, `Route1.zscen` is re-authored from a
      windowed `Vulkan_*_True` boot and proven reproducible by two consecutive
      boots producing byte-identical output
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run
- [ ] Before/after captures of all three props recorded in the work log, so the
      visual sign-off has something to judge

The three Route 1 ground-item props render generated `ZM_PropGen` models with baked

and no prop gained a collider**: the meshes are anchored at
`fZM_PROP_ITEM_BASE_Y = -0.5` precisely because `ZM_Route1PropCentreY` authors

**What changed**

- `Source/Data/ZM_PropData.{h,cpp}` — two silhouette kinds (`ZM_PROP_KIND_ITEM_PICKUP`
  / `_ITEM_SPENT`) and three roster rows: `ItemPhial` (FOLIAGE, 0.42 × 0.94),

**Definition of Done**

- [x] Each of the three props renders with a purpose-built mesh and material rather
      than the `ZM_GreyboxVisual` blockout cube

      0.8086, the catch orb at 1.2555, against three identical ~0.77 greys before.
      *The final judgement is the reviewer's; that is what `human-gate` means.*
- [x] A prop the current save has already collected does not still read as a pickup —
      `ZM_GroundItemPropModel` collapses to `ZM_PROP_ITEM_TAKEN` on
      `IsInteractable() == false`, pinned by

      unmoved, and no prop gains a collider — `ZM_Route1Placement.h` is comment-only

      `ZM_Route1PropCentreY(col) + fZM_PROP_ITEM_BASE_Y * fZM_ROUTE1_PROP_CUBE_EDGE ==
      ZM_Route1GroundFeetY(col)` is now asserted against the FROZEN raycast
      measurement rather than against the constant it is derived from
- [x] If authored transforms change, `Route1.zscen` is re-authored… — **the branch
      never fired.** No authored transform changed; `git status` showed no `.zscen`
      after either windowed boot

      **3399 → 3401**, read off a real `Null_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` run
- [x] Before/after captures of all three props recorded in the work log — see below

**Before/after captures**

Taken with `ZM_GroundItemPropCapture_Test` on a `Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True`
build; identical framing both times (the shot stems are the join key). Preserved at
`.zagent/run/ZM-67/before/` and `.zagent/run/ZM-67/after/`.

|---|---|---|---|
| `route1_south_salve` | (0.1843, 0.2024, 0.2395) | (0.1754, 0.2211, 0.2167) | 0.7697 → **0.8096** |
| `route1_lane_catchorb` | (0.1746, 0.1931, 0.2293) | (0.3414, 0.2675, 0.2719) | 0.7614 → **1.2555** |

gap; nothing should have grown into the walked lane; and — the actual sign-off —

silhouettes and hues separate cleanly at walking distance, but they are still

## Goal

The three Route 1 ground-item props authored by ZM-27 (ZM-D-207) render as
`ZM_GreyboxVisual` blockouts — the engine unit cube with a flat blockout colour,
0.6 m on a side. They read as placeholders because they are placeholders. Bring
them to the visual standard the rest of the game is held to.

Zenithmon generates and bakes all art procedurally from tools builds
(`Source/Gen/` is the existing pattern — see `ZM_BuildingGen` and
`ZM_HumanAppearance`), so this is a generator plus a material, not an imported
asset.

**Scope is the presentation only.** The three props are
`ZM_GROUND_ITEM_ROUTE1_SOUTH_SALVE`, `ZM_GROUND_ITEM_ROUTE1_LANE_CATCHORB` and
`ZM_GROUND_ITEM_ROUTE1_NORTH_SALVE`. The pickup rule
(`ZM_CanPickUpGroundItem` / `ZM_TryPickUpGroundItem`), the prop registry, the
`ZM_GroundItemProp` component contract and save module 12 all shipped in ZM-27
and must not change.

★ **THE MEASURED ANCHORS ARE FROZEN AND THE REACH BUDGET IS TIGHT.** Each prop
stands on its own measured ground column, and
`Route1_GroundItemPropsAreReachableFromTheWalkedLane` holds them inside
`fZM_INTERACT_MAX_DISTANCE` (2.5 m) of the walked lane, with perpendicular
offsets of 1.60 / 2.00 / 1.75 m. A visual pass that makes a prop physically
larger must keep its interact origin where it is — growing the mesh is fine,
moving the anchor is not, and a prop nudged off the lane can never be picked up
in any playthrough while every other check stays green.

★ **AND A PROP HAS NO COLLIDER, DELIBERATELY** (ZM-D-207). Adding one would put
an obstacle in the walked lane and a SOLID body over the prop's own ground
column, which `ZM_Route1GroundTruth_Test` treats as a failure rather than a
filter. Presentation must not introduce one.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Each of the three props renders with a purpose-built mesh and material
      rather than the `ZM_GreyboxVisual` blockout cube
- [ ] The two item kinds are distinguishable from each other on sight at the
      distance a player walks past them, not only in a close-up
- [ ] A prop the current save has already collected does not still read as a
      pickup — its presentation matches the inert state
      `ZM_GroundItemProp::IsInteractable()` already reports
- [ ] Each prop still sits on its own measured ground column with its interact
      origin unmoved, and no prop gains a collider
- [ ] If authored transforms change, `Route1.zscen` is re-authored from a
      windowed `Vulkan_*_True` boot and proven reproducible by two consecutive
      boots producing byte-identical output

      visual sign-off has something to judge

payload.title: Scene-aware NPC appearance distinctness — the invariant is global where the property is local
payload.conventions:
Root CLAUDE.md is binding. No std:: containers; every .cpp starts with #include "Zenith.h"; tabs; braces on new lines; Zenith_Assert is the real assert (ZENITH_ASSERT is an empty marker). Never run Sharpmake in a worktree.

payload.goal:
`Npc_AuthoredAppearancesAreMutuallyDistinct` requires 0.15 RGB separation between
**every pair** of NPC rows naming different `ZM_HUMAN_ID`s. That is stricter than
the property it exists to protect, and the gap is now load-bearing rather than
theoretical: it exhausted the palette and blocked ZM-23 (R1-5).

★ **THE INVARIANT GUARDS A PREVIEW COLOUR, NOT PLAYER-VISIBLE DISTINCTNESS.**
`ZM_GetHumanPaletteColour` (`Source/Gen/ZM_HumanAppearance.cpp:824`) is
`0.45 * outfit.primary + 0.25 * outfit.accent + 0.30 * hair`. It reads NEITHER
skin tone, build, attachment NOR hair *style* — all four of which a rendered
human actually differs by. So two NPCs measuring 0.13 apart on this scalar can be
obviously different people on screen, and the invariant reds anyway.

★ **AND IT IS GLOBAL WHERE THE PROPERTY IS LOCAL.** Two Route 1 trainers can
never share a frame with a Dawnmere townsperson — different scenes, reachable
only through a warp with a full fade. Requiring them to differ buys nothing a
player could observe, while consuming cells from a 36-cell space
(6 non-themed outfits x 6 non-DYED hairs).

## Goal

`Roadmap.md` S8, Gym 1 — **slice G1-2: author `Gym1.zscen` and the Thornacre door.**
Build the gym interior from the frozen constants G1-1 landed, place Fenna in it,
and connect it to Thornacre in both directions.

**SPLIT OUT of ZM-28 on 2026-08-25**, alongside G1-1 (the pure data and placement
header) and G1-3 (the badge and teach-move reward on a leader win). This is the
scene slice: it is the only one of the three that writes a tracked asset.

## ★ Two scene facts that decide how this slice is run

**`Gym1.zscen` does NOT exist, so this CREATES it.** The `.zscen` publish guard
(`Zenith_Editor.cpp`, inside `if constexpr (Zenith_IsNullRenderer())`) refuses a
headless boot CHANGING a committed scene, never creating one — its own comment
records that windowed boots author everything and publish unconditionally. So the
gym itself is reachable from a headless boot.

**But the Thornacre door is a CHANGE to a committed scene.** `Thornacre.zscen`
already exists and ships, and a warp into the gym has to be authored INTO it —
which the guard refuses headless. **That is why this ticket carries `needs-gpu`:**
build `Vulkan_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` and drive the boot with a short automated
test carrying `--skip-unit-tests`. A GPU is assumed available; the label selects
the build, it does not gate the claim.

★ **A WINDOWED `_True` BOOT AUTHORS BEFORE IT TESTS.** Check `git status` after
every one, and expect exactly the scene paths this ticket means to touch. Two
consecutive boots must produce byte-identical output before the bytes are
committed — reproducibility is a separate property from correctness, and only the
second pair proves the first.

## What G1-1 has already frozen — read it, do not re-derive it

`Source/World/ZM_Gym1Placement.h` carries the hedge-maze walls, the leader's
station, the entrance and the arrival point as named constants, and a headless
unit already proves the declared maze is solvable. **Author from those constants.**
If the authored scene needs a value the header does not have, add it to the header
rather than spelling a literal in the authoring code — that is what made the R1
anchors auditable.

Fenna is `ZM_HUMAN_LEADER_FENNA`, an authored row that already has an appearance,
and her trainer row landed in G1-1.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `Gym1.zscen` exists and is committed, built from `ZM_Gym1Placement.h`'s
      constants rather than from literals spelled in the authoring code
- [ ] Fenna stands at the leader station the header declares, and the hedge walls
      match the layout the G1-1 solvability unit proved
- [ ] A door in `Thornacre.zscen` enters the gym and the gym exits back to
      Thornacre — the pair works in BOTH directions, from a real boot
- [ ] The player can walk from the gym entrance to Fenna: the route the header
      declares solvable is solvable in the live scene, not only on paper
- [ ] Two consecutive windowed boots produce byte-identical output for every
      scene this ticket touches, and the committed-asset hashes are recorded
- [ ] `git status` after authoring shows exactly the intended scene paths and
      nothing else
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-69 -->
## Work Log — 2026-08-25

**Outcome**: **Blocked** — nothing committed, tree clean · ran on opus/medium via MODERATE+HIGH · category Zenithmon

**What changed**

Nothing. The worker made zero edits and stopped at its Step Zero survey, which is the
instructed behaviour when a hit lands outside the permitted file list. No gates were run:
there is no diff to gate, and `zagent guard` on a clean tree reports a failed attempt
rather than a guard result.

**Why it is Blocked — verified, not accepted on the worker's word**

The ticket is not unreachable in principle and it does not violate `protectedPaths`. It
was **unbuildable as scoped**: the file list I derived was short by two files, and one
omission is fatal in a way no test can see.

**The fatal one.** `Gym1` has no row in `Source/World/ZM_SceneRegistry.h`.
`Project_LoadInitialScene` walks that table to call `RegisterSceneBuildIndex`, and
`ZM_GameStateManager::IsWarpDestinationValid` consults **only the compiled world table**,
never the registry. So a Thornacre gym door authored without the row is ACCEPTED, fades
fully opaque, stalls in `ZM_WARP_TRANSITION_WAITING_FOR_SCENE` until the ZM-D-200 frame
budget expires, and exits with a `Zenith_Error`. A black screen — with **every unit still
green**, including the three `ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry` units that assert the gym's absence,
which stay green because the absence stays real.

That is precisely the failure `ZM-D-196` Ruling 2 cites as its reason, reproduced by doing
half of this ticket.

**Independently verified by the orchestrator** (the ticket produced a zero diff, so there
was nothing to review and this was done in the review's place):

| Claim | How it was checked |
|---|---|
| Gym1 absent from the registry | Read `ZM_SceneRegistry.h` — 7 rows, and an explicit comment: *"★ GYM1 IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT … adding a row must be a conscious act"* |
| `IsWarpDestinationValid` ignores the registry | Corroborated in four independent places, including `ZM_Gym1Placement.h:102`, which G1-1 itself wrote |
| The pad-containment blocker | All four constants read directly: `ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp:185` `"Gym"` pad centre (760, 864) radius **50.0**; `:214` `"FromGym"` landmark (760, 28, **814**) — distance **exactly 50.0 m**; `fTH_PAD_CONTAINMENT_FRACTION = 0.75` (`ZM_Tests_ThornacrePlacement.cpp:76`) → **37.5 m** limit. 50.0 > 37.5, so it reds by construction |
| A new anchor needs its OWN column | `ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h:613-619` — *"a sensor resting on its neighbour's ground is part-buried or hovering with every scale constant still correct"*; nearest existing columns are ~750 m away |

**What actually blocks it: two rulings this loop may not make**

1. **Where the gym-door ground column goes.** Filed as a Questions row. The recipe's own
   `FromGym` landmark fails the containment clause by construction, and all three fixes
   trade something real: pulling the marker inboard decouples marker from landmark (the
   coupling `U12`'s shape exists to enforce); changing the recipe re-measures every ground
   table in the game, by that header's own warning; exempting the gym column weakens a
   deliberate assertion, which the ticket forbids.
2. **`ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry` U4's independence arm.** Filed as a Questions row. After this
   ticket all eight `ZM_SCENE_ID` rows are registered, so the arm's own instruction —
   *"replace this arm with another unbacked target"* — has no target left. Rebuilding it on
   a synthetic index changes what it proves.

**The corrected file list, so a re-filed ticket need not re-derive it**

Everything the ticket listed, plus:

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `Source/World/ZM_SceneRegistry.h` | the `{ ZM_SCENE_GYM1, "Gym1" }` row — the fatal omission |
| `Tests/ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry.cpp` | 4 sites: the 7-row expected array + the `7u` literal (`:140-157`), U2's gym-absence pair (`:351-363`), U3's build-index clause (`:426-431`), U4's independence arm (`:582-604`) |
| `Tests/ZM_AutoTests_RouteGround.cpp` | `RGThornacreFreezeTarget` (`:503-560`) — a per-enumerator switch that defaults to *"freeze nothing"*, so a new anchor is silently never frozen with every test green |

**The tripwire survey — 8 sites, not the 4 the ticket named**

The four pre-authorised sites were all confirmed, and three are wider than described: the
Thornacre entity-count also needs its accessor switch extended; U14 is three sub-sites, not
one; and the committed-bytes needle's unbacked-tag loop goes **vacuous** once `"FromGym"`
is backed, so it needs restructuring rather than moving.

**Entities Thornacre would gain:** two, appended after `ThornacreSouthGate` (ZM-D-148 dense
indices — appending is free, inserting renumbers the file): a `"FromGym"` `ZM_SpawnPoint`
and a `ZM_WarpTrigger` to build index 42 asking for tag `"Door"`. Count 5 → **7**. Naming is
constrained: U14 clause (6) forbids any entity name containing an offered tag or a tag this
town's edges ask for, so `ThornacreFromGymSpawn` and anything containing `Door` are both
illegal.

**On the ruling itself — it is NOT being overridden**

`ZM-D-196` Ruling 2 says *"Explicitly NO gym door"*, but its stated **why** is *"Gym1 …
declared but unauthored"*. This ticket discharges that premise by authoring Gym1, which is
why the tripwires may move now and could not before. Read as a bare decision the ruling
forbids this ticket; read with its reason it is a precondition this ticket satisfies. What
blocks the slice is scope, not the ruling.

**Definition of Done**

- [ ] `Gym1.zscen` exists and is committed, built from `ZM_Gym1Placement.h`'s constants
- [ ] Fenna stands at the leader station the header declares, and the hedge walls match
- [ ] A door in `Thornacre.zscen` enters the gym and the gym exits back — both directions
- [ ] The player can walk from the gym entrance to Fenna in the live scene
- [ ] Two consecutive windowed boots byte-identical; committed-asset hashes recorded
- [ ] `git status` after authoring shows exactly the intended scene paths and nothing else
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

None met. No windowed boot was run, so no scene bytes were produced and no hash exists.

**Gates**

None run — zero diff. The pin stands at the `3415` ZM-28 measured; nothing in this tick
could move it.

**Coverage**

Not applicable — no source file changed.

**Deviations / follow-ups**

- **The file list was MY error, not the ticket's.** The ticket body named four tripwires
  and I inlined them; neither of us reached `ZM_SceneRegistry.h`, because it never appears
  in a grep for "gym door" — it says *"the Gym"*. The worker's suggestion is right: for a
  ticket that REVERSES a recorded assertion, grep the **subject** (`ZM_SCENE_GYM1`,
  `ZM_IsSceneRegisteredForLoad`) rather than the prose.
- **Recommended re-scope, from the worker and endorsed here.** Split G1-2:
  **G1-2a** the registry row + the four registry-test moves + `RGThornacreFreezeTarget` —
  headless, no scene bytes, independently verifiable, and it needs only ruling 2.
  **G1-2b** the authoring, the door, the ground freeze and the two windowed boots — needs
  ruling 1. The current shape asks one ticket to move eight tripwires across five files
  *and* produce two scene files from a GPU boot, which is a lot of surface for one gate run
  to bisect.
- **The worker behaved exactly as instructed** — it hit the boundary, made no edits, and
  returned a corrected list with the reasoning. That cost one dispatch and produced a
  precise re-scope; improvising would have cost a revert and shipped a black screen.
- **No fix-forward attempt was consumed.** This is not a red gate; it is a scope gap
  requiring two rulings, and `fixForwardAttempts` exists for failures the loop can fix.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

payload.body:
## Goal

`Roadmap.md` S8, Gym 1 — **slice G1-3: beating Fenna awards the Bloom Badge and
grants Verdant Lash.** Wire the reward onto the leader-defeat path and prove both
halves survive a save round trip.

**SPLIT OUT of ZM-28 on 2026-08-25**, alongside G1-1 (the pure data and placement
header) and G1-2 (authoring the scene). This slice is **PURE** — it re-authors
nothing and needs no scene, so it can run in PARALLEL with G1-2 once G1-1 lands.

## Almost all of the machinery already exists

This is a wiring slice, not a systems slice, and the scope is easy to overestimate:

- **Badge state is complete and persisted.** `uZM_BADGE_COUNT = 8`,
  `m_uBadgeMask`, `AwardBadge(uIndex)`, `HasBadge`, `GetBadgeCount` live in
  `Source/Party/ZM_GameState.h:89-176`, and save module 5 already reads and writes
  the mask (`Source/Core/ZM_SaveSchema.cpp:21`, `:980`, `:1058`). **Add no badge
  state and change no save schema.**
- **Teach-move already exists as an item effect** — `ZM_ITEM_CATEGORY_TM` and
  `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE` with `m_eTaughtMove`
  (`Source/Data/ZM_ItemData.h:30`, `:67`, `:169`). **Add no new effect kind.**
- G1-1 landed the Bloom Badge index and the Verdant Lash TM row.

So what is missing is the CONNECTION: nothing today awards a badge or grants a
reward when a leader is beaten.

## ★ Prefer a by-ROW seam over a by-id one

`ZM-D-208` §2 ruled on exactly this shape one slice earlier and the reasoning
carries: a helper keyed on `ZM_TRAINER_ID` can only ever be exercised through the
shipped roster, so its coverage dies the moment content changes, while a helper
taking a `const ZM_TrainerData&` can be driven by a hand-built row and cannot
drift. `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState` already has both shapes for the same
reason. Follow it: make the reward path reachable from a row, so the units do not
depend on Fenna specifically remaining the first gym leader forever.

★ **AND DO NOT ASSERT A REWARD THE PLAYER CANNOT KEEP.** "Persists" is the word in
the Definition of Done and it is the whole point: a badge awarded into a mask that
is never written, or a move taught to a party member that is not saved, passes an
in-memory assertion and fails the player. Prove both through an actual save/load
round trip, not by re-reading the object you just mutated.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Beating Fenna awards the Bloom Badge through the EXISTING `AwardBadge` mask
      — no new badge state, no save-schema change
- [ ] Beating Fenna grants Verdant Lash through the EXISTING
      `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE` path
- [ ] Both survive a save/load ROUND TRIP, proven by reading them back off a
      reloaded save rather than off the mutated object
- [ ] The reward path is reachable from a `const ZM_TrainerData&` row, so a unit
      can drive it with a hand-built fixture and its coverage cannot be retired by
      a content change (`ZM-D-208` §2's reasoning, applied here)
- [ ] Awarding twice does not double-grant, and the badge count is right after a
      repeat win
- [ ] **No committed scene byte moves: this slice authors nothing**
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-70 -->
## Work Log — 2026-08-26

**Outcome**: merged to `master` as `bc3a9ae7` · ran on sonnet/medium via MODERATE+MEDIUM · category Zenithmon

**What changed**

- `Source/Data/ZM_TrainerData.h` / `.cpp` — two trailing columns, `m_eBadgeReward` and `m_eItemReward`, appended per the struct's own *"New columns go AT THE END"* rule. Fenna's row is the first to carry real values (`ZM_BADGE_BLOOM`, `ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH`); every other row names the NONE sentinels. Both columns carry explicit default member initializers, backed by a compile-time probe (below).
- `Source/Party/ZM_BattleWriteBack.h` / `.cpp` — a by-ROW primitive `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool)`; the by-ID overload becomes classify → is-registered → resolve → forward. The badge goes through the shipped `AwardBadge`, the item through the shipped `ZM_Bag::Add`, **gated on `ZM_Bag::Has`**. Result gains `m_bBadgeNewlyAwarded` / `m_bItemGranted`.
- `Components/ZM_BattleDirector.cpp` — the SC5 call-site comment only; the call signature is unchanged.
- `Tests/ZM_Tests_Party.cpp` — 4 new units; the existing Vesper test strengthened with badge/item neutrality rather than duplicated.
- `Tools/unit_baselines.json` — `Zenithmon` 3415 → **3419**, from an OBSERVED `Null_` run.
- `Docs/Status.md`, `Docs/DecisionLog.md` — pin narration, **ZM-D-213** and **ZM-D-214**.

**Files** (`git diff --stat`)

```
 8 files changed · 4 new boot units · no new .cpp (so no regen needed)
 Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_Party.cpp          193 +
 Games/Zenithmon/Source/Party/ZM_BattleWriteBack.h  65 +
 ... plus the write-back .cpp, both TrainerData files, BattleDirector, 2 docs, the pin
```

**Gates**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `zenith build Zenithmon --headless` | exit 0 · 13.8s |
| `zenith build Zenithmon --config D3D12_vs2022_Debug_Win64_False` | exit 0 · 12.1s (non-tools path) |
| `zenith test Zenithmon --headless` | exit 0 · 1286.3s |
| `run_unit_gate.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | exit 0 · 91.2s — **3419 ran / 3417 passed / 0 failed**, 2 skipped |
| `doc_lint.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | exit 0 · 2.0s — C7 reconciled the LIVE PIN block against the manifest and the registry count |

All 5 category gates ran; `skipped: []`, `deferred: []`, `headSha` matched HEAD. Nothing was
unioned in — the diff stays inside `Games/Zenithmon/**` plus `Tools/**`, deliberately outside
every category's `paths`. `zagent guard` clean, `gateSelectionStale: null`.

**Coverage**

| Changed file | What executes the changed line |
|---|---|
| `ZM_BattleWriteBack.cpp` (by-ROW primitive, badge + gated item) | all 4 new units in `ZM_Tests_Party.cpp`, plus the ~10 pre-existing write-back units in Section H that now run through the refactored by-ID path |
| `ZM_BattleWriteBack.h` (result fields) | the new units assert both new fields, including `m_bItemGranted == false` on a repeat win |
| `ZM_TrainerData.cpp` (Fenna's reward values) | `TrainerReward_BeatingFennaAwardsTheBloomBadgeAndGrantsVerdantLash` reads them through the production path |
| `ZM_TrainerData.h` (the two columns' defaults) | **a compile-time `static_assert` over a nine-field aggregate** — the build fails if either default is removed. This exists *because* the review found the defaults had zero runtime coverage |
| `ZM_BattleDirector.cpp` | **Nothing — comment-only change.** No executable line changed |
| `Tools/unit_baselines.json` | `run_unit_gate.ps1`, which asserts `ran == baseline` EXACTLY |
| `Docs/Status.md` | `doc_lint` C7 — equality against the manifest and the registry count, both directions |
| `Docs/DecisionLog.md` | `doc_lint`'s id/marker checks. **The PROSE of a decision entry is read by no gate** — which is how two errors got into ZM-D-213 (below) |

**Definition of Done**

- [x] Beating Fenna awards the Bloom Badge through the EXISTING `AwardBadge` mask — no new badge state, no save-schema change
- [x] Beating Fenna grants Verdant Lash through the EXISTING `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE` path
- [x] Both survive a save/load ROUND TRIP, proven by reading them back off a reloaded save rather than off the mutated object
- [x] The reward path is reachable from a `const ZM_TrainerData&` row, so a unit can drive it with a hand-built fixture and its coverage cannot be retired by a content change
- [x] Awarding twice does not double-grant, and the badge count is right after a repeat win
- [x] **No committed scene byte moves: this slice authors nothing**
- [x] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

**Review — one BLOCKING finding, and it overturned the orchestrator**

`review.required` was true (risk MEDIUM + an ABSENCE claim). The absence claims all held:
`ZM_GameState.h` and `ZM_SaveSchema.cpp` are absent from the diff, no `.zscen` is in it, the
round trip genuinely re-decodes into a fresh `ZM_GameState`, and the by-ROW fixture would still
pass with Fenna deleted from the roster.

**The blocking finding was a judgement I had already accepted and recorded as fact.** The TM
grant was ungated, so a repeat win stacked a second copy. I had reasoned — following the
worker — that this matched prize money, which stacks under ZM-D-135. **The precedent does not
transfer.** ZM-D-208's correction states money's cause: it pays again *because* ZM-D-135
forbids a new `ZM_GameState` member to record "already paid". For an item that cause is absent
— `m_xBag` IS the record and `ZM_Bag::Has` answers it — so "adds no state" was an argument
FOR gating that I had recorded as one against. And the consequence was not cosmetic: Verdant
Lash is `m_bConsumable = false`, so a second copy's only use is `ZM_ShopSell` at its 500 sell
price — a farmable prize, the precise shape the per-trainer defeat flag exists to forbid.

Fixed at fix-forward 1 of 3, content-only, so the 3419 pin measured before it still stands and
the verify run re-confirmed it. Recorded as **ZM-D-214**, with **ZM-D-213 corrected in place**.

Four non-blocking findings were also taken: the by-ROW unit now uses a TM *distinct* from
Fenna's so the item half of "row-driven, not hardcoded" is proven rather than assumed; the
nine-column legend and the SC5 call-site comment were both stale; and the "load-bearing"
default initializers had **zero coverage** — deleting them left every gate green — now closed
by a `static_assert` rather than a comment.

**Deviations / follow-ups**

- **Two errors of mine in ZM-D-213, both caught by the review, both corrected before the
  commit.** The item-dedup reasoning above, and a claim that two files use `<vector>` when
  there are three — one of them production (`Source/World/ZM_GrassDensityMap.h`). A decision
  entry's prose is read by no gate; that is exactly why the review must cover orchestrator
  edits.
- **A "durable finding" shipped with no tripwire.** ZM-D-213 recorded the default-initializer
  trap as durable; the reviewer checked and found nothing enforced it. That is verbatim the
  defect ZM-D-212's review named two days earlier — *"a comment asserting a guard exists is
  worse than no guard"* — recurring inside the entry written by the tick that recorded the
  lesson. The rule worth keeping: when a tick records a durable finding, say what FAILS if it
  is violated; if the answer is "nothing", that is the finding.
- **Corrections made to the ticket's own text before inlining it (I3).** The body claimed
  *"`ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState` already has both shapes"* — it did not; both overloads
  were by-ID and this ticket had to BUILD the by-row seam. I pasted that through verbatim and
  the worker caught it at Step Zero. The body also cited `Source/Battle/ZM_BattleWriteBack.h`;
  the file is under `Source/Party/`. And the DoD's *"EXISTING `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE`
  path"* does not exist as a runtime path — the enum and rows have zero consumers, which
  ZM-D-196 Ruling 1 already established (*"no way to USE an item at all"*), so the grant is
  the TM ITEM into the bag. That correction went into the worker prompt rather than being
  discovered expensively.
- **An open Questions row was resolved by the review**, not by a human: the item-stacking
  question is answered and closed with the corrected reasoning recorded on it.
- **For ZM-23 when it is next claimed**: ZM-D-208 Ruling 2 *mandated* this by-ROW primitive by
  exact signature, scoped to ZM-23, and also said to re-point `ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099` at it.
  ZM-70 landed the primitive but deliberately did NOT re-point that test, so Ruling 2's first
  item is now half-done by a different ticket.
- **`zagent docs sync` COMPLETED — exit 0 in 24 seconds**, updating 7 pages, all `verified:
  true`. This is its first completion in six ticks; the previous five "hangs" were a
  per-page WebSocket over all 597 pages, root-caused and fixed in the previous board `05408ef`. The mirror
  is current, not one commit behind.
- The `<vector>` in the round-trip test follows `Tests/ZM_Tests_SaveSchema.cpp:25`'s
  established Encode/Decode idiom. The reviewer noted a `Zenith_DataStream(void*, uint64_t)`
  overload would avoid the container entirely — worth knowing before it becomes a third
  precedent.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

payload.body:
## Goal

`Roadmap.md` S8, Gym 1 — **slice G1-3: beating Fenna awards the Bloom Badge and
grants Verdant Lash.** Wire the reward onto the leader-defeat path and prove both
halves survive a save round trip.

**SPLIT OUT of ZM-28 on 2026-08-25**, alongside G1-1 (the pure data and placement
header) and G1-2 (authoring the scene). This slice is **PURE** — it re-authors
nothing and needs no scene, so it can run in PARALLEL with G1-2 once G1-1 lands.

## Almost all of the machinery already exists

This is a wiring slice, not a systems slice, and the scope is easy to overestimate:

- **Badge state is complete and persisted.** `uZM_BADGE_COUNT = 8`,
  `m_uBadgeMask`, `AwardBadge(uIndex)`, `HasBadge`, `GetBadgeCount` live in
  `Source/Party/ZM_GameState.h:89-176`, and save module 5 already reads and writes
  the mask (`Source/Core/ZM_SaveSchema.cpp:21`, `:980`, `:1058`). **Add no badge
  state and change no save schema.**
- **Teach-move already exists as an item effect** — `ZM_ITEM_CATEGORY_TM` and
  `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE` with `m_eTaughtMove`
  (`Source/Data/ZM_ItemData.h:30`, `:67`, `:169`). **Add no new effect kind.**
- G1-1 landed the Bloom Badge index and the Verdant Lash TM row.

So what is missing is the CONNECTION: nothing today awards a badge or grants a
reward when a leader is beaten.

## ★ Prefer a by-ROW seam over a by-id one

`ZM-D-208` §2 ruled on exactly this shape one slice earlier and the reasoning
carries: a helper keyed on `ZM_TRAINER_ID` can only ever be exercised through the
shipped roster, so its coverage dies the moment content changes, while a helper
taking a `const ZM_TrainerData&` can be driven by a hand-built row and cannot
drift. `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState` already has both shapes for the same
reason. Follow it: make the reward path reachable from a row, so the units do not
depend on Fenna specifically remaining the first gym leader forever.

★ **AND DO NOT ASSERT A REWARD THE PLAYER CANNOT KEEP.** "Persists" is the word in
the Definition of Done and it is the whole point: a badge awarded into a mask that
is never written, or a move taught to a party member that is not saved, passes an
in-memory assertion and fails the player. Prove both through an actual save/load
round trip, not by re-reading the object you just mutated.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Beating Fenna awards the Bloom Badge through the EXISTING `AwardBadge` mask
      — no new badge state, no save-schema change
- [ ] Beating Fenna grants Verdant Lash through the EXISTING
      `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE` path
- [ ] Both survive a save/load ROUND TRIP, proven by reading them back off a
      reloaded save rather than off the mutated object
- [ ] The reward path is reachable from a `const ZM_TrainerData&` row, so a unit
      can drive it with a hand-built fixture and its coverage cannot be retired by
      a content change (`ZM-D-208` §2's reasoning, applied here)
- [ ] Awarding twice does not double-grant, and the badge count is right after a
      repeat win
- [ ] **No committed scene byte moves: this slice authors nothing**
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

<!-- agent:worklog:start ZM-70 -->
## Work Log — 2026-08-26

**Outcome**: merged to `master` as `bc3a9ae7` · ran on sonnet/medium via MODERATE+MEDIUM · category Zenithmon

**What changed**

- `Source/Data/ZM_TrainerData.h` / `.cpp` — two trailing columns, `m_eBadgeReward` and `m_eItemReward`, appended per the struct's own *"New columns go AT THE END"* rule. Fenna's row is the first to carry real values (`ZM_BADGE_BLOOM`, `ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH`); every other row names the NONE sentinels. Both columns carry explicit default member initializers, backed by a compile-time probe (below).
- `Source/Party/ZM_BattleWriteBack.h` / `.cpp` — a by-ROW primitive `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool)`; the by-ID overload becomes classify → is-registered → resolve → forward. The badge goes through the shipped `AwardBadge`, the item through the shipped `ZM_Bag::Add`, **gated on `ZM_Bag::Has`**. Result gains `m_bBadgeNewlyAwarded` / `m_bItemGranted`.
- `Components/ZM_BattleDirector.cpp` — the SC5 call-site comment only; the call signature is unchanged.
- `Tests/ZM_Tests_Party.cpp` — 4 new units; the existing Vesper test strengthened with badge/item neutrality rather than duplicated.
- `Tools/unit_baselines.json` — `Zenithmon` 3415 → **3419**, from an OBSERVED `Null_` run.
- `Docs/Status.md`, `Docs/DecisionLog.md` — pin narration, **ZM-D-213** and **ZM-D-214**.

**Files** (`git diff --stat`)

```
 8 files changed · 4 new boot units · no new .cpp (so no regen needed)
 Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_Party.cpp          193 +
 Games/Zenithmon/Source/Party/ZM_BattleWriteBack.h  65 +
 ... plus the write-back .cpp, both TrainerData files, BattleDirector, 2 docs, the pin
```

**Gates**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `zenith build Zenithmon --headless` | exit 0 · 13.8s |
| `zenith build Zenithmon --config D3D12_vs2022_Debug_Win64_False` | exit 0 · 12.1s (non-tools path) |
| `zenith test Zenithmon --headless` | exit 0 · 1286.3s |
| `run_unit_gate.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | exit 0 · 91.2s — **3419 ran / 3417 passed / 0 failed**, 2 skipped |
| `doc_lint.ps1 -Game Zenithmon` | exit 0 · 2.0s — C7 reconciled the LIVE PIN block against the manifest and the registry count |

All 5 category gates ran; `skipped: []`, `deferred: []`, `headSha` matched HEAD. Nothing was
unioned in — the diff stays inside `Games/Zenithmon/**` plus `Tools/**`, deliberately outside
every category's `paths`. `zagent guard` clean, `gateSelectionStale: null`.

**Coverage**

| Changed file | What executes the changed line |
|---|---|
| `ZM_BattleWriteBack.cpp` (by-ROW primitive, badge + gated item) | all 4 new units in `ZM_Tests_Party.cpp`, plus the ~10 pre-existing write-back units in Section H that now run through the refactored by-ID path |
| `ZM_BattleWriteBack.h` (result fields) | the new units assert both new fields, including `m_bItemGranted == false` on a repeat win |
| `ZM_TrainerData.cpp` (Fenna's reward values) | `TrainerReward_BeatingFennaAwardsTheBloomBadgeAndGrantsVerdantLash` reads them through the production path |
| `ZM_TrainerData.h` (the two columns' defaults) | **a compile-time `static_assert` over a nine-field aggregate** — the build fails if either default is removed. This exists *because* the review found the defaults had zero runtime coverage |
| `ZM_BattleDirector.cpp` | **Nothing — comment-only change.** No executable line changed |
| `Tools/unit_baselines.json` | `run_unit_gate.ps1`, which asserts `ran == baseline` EXACTLY |
| `Docs/Status.md` | `doc_lint` C7 — equality against the manifest and the registry count, both directions |
| `Docs/DecisionLog.md` | `doc_lint`'s id/marker checks. **The PROSE of a decision entry is read by no gate** — which is how two errors got into ZM-D-213 (below) |

**Definition of Done**

- [x] Beating Fenna awards the Bloom Badge through the EXISTING `AwardBadge` mask — no new badge state, no save-schema change
- [x] Beating Fenna grants Verdant Lash through the EXISTING `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE` path
- [x] Both survive a save/load ROUND TRIP, proven by reading them back off a reloaded save rather than off the mutated object
- [x] The reward path is reachable from a `const ZM_TrainerData&` row, so a unit can drive it with a hand-built fixture and its coverage cannot be retired by a content change
- [x] Awarding twice does not double-grant, and the badge count is right after a repeat win
- [x] **No committed scene byte moves: this slice authors nothing**
- [x] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run

**Review — one BLOCKING finding, and it overturned the orchestrator**

`review.required` was true (risk MEDIUM + an ABSENCE claim). The absence claims all held:
`ZM_GameState.h` and `ZM_SaveSchema.cpp` are absent from the diff, no `.zscen` is in it, the
round trip genuinely re-decodes into a fresh `ZM_GameState`, and the by-ROW fixture would still
pass with Fenna deleted from the roster.

**The blocking finding was a judgement I had already accepted and recorded as fact.** The TM
grant was ungated, so a repeat win stacked a second copy. I had reasoned — following the
worker — that this matched prize money, which stacks under ZM-D-135. **The precedent does not
transfer.** ZM-D-208's correction states money's cause: it pays again *because* ZM-D-135
forbids a new `ZM_GameState` member to record "already paid". For an item that cause is absent
— `m_xBag` IS the record and `ZM_Bag::Has` answers it — so "adds no state" was an argument
FOR gating that I had recorded as one against. And the consequence was not cosmetic: Verdant
Lash is `m_bConsumable = false`, so a second copy's only use is `ZM_ShopSell` at its 500 sell
price — a farmable prize, the precise shape the per-trainer defeat flag exists to forbid.

Fixed at fix-forward 1 of 3, content-only, so the 3419 pin measured before it still stands and
the verify run re-confirmed it. Recorded as **ZM-D-214**, with **ZM-D-213 corrected in place**.

Four non-blocking findings were also taken: the by-ROW unit now uses a TM *distinct* from
Fenna's so the item half of "row-driven, not hardcoded" is proven rather than assumed; the
nine-column legend and the SC5 call-site comment were both stale; and the "load-bearing"
default initializers had **zero coverage** — deleting them left every gate green — now closed
by a `static_assert` rather than a comment.

**Deviations / follow-ups**

- **Two errors of mine in ZM-D-213, both caught by the review, both corrected before the
  commit.** The item-dedup reasoning above, and a claim that two files use `<vector>` when
  there are three — one of them production (`Source/World/ZM_GrassDensityMap.h`). A decision
  entry's prose is read by no gate; that is exactly why the review must cover orchestrator
  edits.
- **A "durable finding" shipped with no tripwire.** ZM-D-213 recorded the default-initializer
  trap as durable; the reviewer checked and found nothing enforced it. That is verbatim the
  defect ZM-D-212's review named two days earlier — *"a comment asserting a guard exists is
  worse than no guard"* — recurring inside the entry written by the tick that recorded the
  lesson. The rule worth keeping: when a tick records a durable finding, say what FAILS if it
  is violated; if the answer is "nothing", that is the finding.
- **Corrections made to the ticket's own text before inlining it (I3).** The body claimed
  *"`ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState` already has both shapes"* — it did not; both overloads
  were by-ID and this ticket had to BUILD the by-row seam. I pasted that through verbatim and
  the worker caught it at Step Zero. The body also cited `Source/Battle/ZM_BattleWriteBack.h`;
  the file is under `Source/Party/`. And the DoD's *"EXISTING `ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE`
  path"* does not exist as a runtime path — the enum and rows have zero consumers, which
  ZM-D-196 Ruling 1 already established (*"no way to USE an item at all"*), so the grant is
  the TM ITEM into the bag. That correction went into the worker prompt rather than being
  discovered expensively.
- **An open Questions row was resolved by the review**, not by a human: the item-stacking
  question is answered and closed with the corrected reasoning recorded on it.
- **For ZM-23 when it is next claimed**: ZM-D-208 Ruling 2 *mandated* this by-ROW primitive by
  exact signature, scoped to ZM-23, and also said to re-point `ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099` at it.
  ZM-70 landed the primitive but deliberately did NOT re-point that test, so Ruling 2's first
  item is now half-done by a different ticket.
- **`zagent docs sync` COMPLETED — exit 0 in 24 seconds**, updating 7 pages, all `verified:
  true`. This is its first completion in six ticks; the previous five "hangs" were a
  per-page WebSocket over all 597 pages, root-caused and fixed in the previous board `05408ef`. The mirror
  is current, not one commit behind.
- The `<vector>` in the round-trip test follows `Tests/ZM_Tests_SaveSchema.cpp:25`'s
  established Encode/Decode idiom. The reviewer noted a `Zenith_DataStream(void*, uint64_t)`
  overload would avoid the container entirely — worth knowing before it becomes a third
  precedent.
<!-- agent:worklog:end -->

## Goal

ZM-D-168 visual audit, item 4, and the half of ZM-58 a machine can do.
`Games/Zenithmon/Docs/History.md` records the finding as **"Dawnmere reads as an
open field, not a town — no buildings; the Trade Post and Care Center are
dialogue only."** Items 1, 2 and 3 of that audit closed on pixels (ZM-D-169 /
ZM-D-170 / ZM-D-171). Item 4 is still open.

**The gap is PLACEMENT, not assets.** Measured on `master` 2026-08-26; every
line number below was opened and confirmed on that date:

- `Games/Zenithmon/Assets/Buildings/` carries all **30** baked bundles, each
  complete — `.zmesh`, `.zmodel`, `.zmtrl`, `_facade.ztxtr` — `CareCenter` and
  `TradePost` among them. S4 `ZM_BuildingGen`'s SC5 disk bake shipped.
- **Not one of the seven committed `.zscen` files references a single one of
  them.** The string `Buildings/` occurs **zero** times in `Dawnmere.zscen`, and
  zero times in the other six.

So the town has a shop clerk NPC (`Npc_TradePostClerk`, authored at
`Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.cpp:70`), a Care Center heal
flow (`Games/Zenithmon/Source/CareCenter/ZM_CareCenter.cpp`), and roster rows for
both buildings with real 10.0 x 8.0 footprints
(`Games/Zenithmon/Source/Data/ZM_BuildingData.cpp:49-50`) — and no building
standing anywhere in the scene.

**ZM-58 is BLOCKED by this ticket and stays open.** ZM-58 is the aesthetic
judgement — a person looking at the finished town and deciding whether it reads
as one. **This ticket is not that.** Everything specified below is buildable and
machine-verifiable; finishing it is what gives ZM-58 something to look at.

### Constraints that bound the work

**★ THE TERRAIN RECIPE IS FROZEN — place inside the sites it already reserves.**
`Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp` reserves Dawnmere pads
`Plaza` (512, 512) r=60, `Home` (384, 496) r=36, `Lab` (640, 552) r=48 and
`RouteGate`, plus the `Plaza`, `PlazaLandmark` and `ReservedRivalHome` landmarks.
Editing ANY pad, path or landmark regenerates the WHOLE Dawnmere heightmap — the
recipe's hydraulic erosion pass is region-wide rather than pad-local, as ZM-D-173
found the expensive way — which re-measures every table in
`Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` and re-bakes the committed
navmesh. That is a different and much larger ticket.

**★ RE-AUTHORING `Dawnmere.zscen` STILL NEEDS A WINDOWED BOOT, FOR A REASON THAT
IS NOT THE OLD ONE.** ZEN-6 (`cbebea74`, 2026-08-26) removed the engine's `.zscen`
publish guard, so a headless boot may now CHANGE a committed scene. It deliberately
did not change Zenithmon: `Games/Zenithmon/Zenithmon.cpp:3848` still defers
Dawnmere's scene authoring on a Null backend by the game's own choice, logging
`sceneAuthoring=DEFERRED`. ZM-D-190's canonical order therefore still applies —
build both configs; authoring boot on `Vulkan_*_True` with `--skip-unit-tests`;
`git status` the WHOLE `Assets/` tree, because a Vulkan boot authors all five
scenes; a second boot proving byte-identity; only THEN the gate.

**★ `ZM_GreyboxVisual` HAS NO BUILDING POPULATION.** It serves three — BLOCKOUT,
HUMAN and PROP — and its BLOCKOUT branch is pinned to `1.0e-4f` by
`Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_AutoTests_InteriorTint.cpp:102`, so that branch must not
move. ZM-67's PROP branch is the nearest precedent for how a placed building
should resolve a generated static model. Its serialization contract is that
nothing new is written — `WriteToDataStream` emits a single version `u_int` — so a
fourth population must not grow the per-component byte count.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The Trade Post and the Care Center stand in `Dawnmere.zscen` as placed
      entities resolving the baked `Buildings/TradePost` and `Buildings/CareCenter`
      bundles, on measured ground, inside terrain sites the recipe already
      reserves — with the recipe itself unedited.
- [ ] Their placement coordinates live as compiled constants in
      `Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h`, derived rather than
      re-spelled, in the same measured-table idiom the Home shell and the SC-D lab
      numbers use.
- [ ] A boot unit in `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` reads
      the committed `Dawnmere.zscen` off disk and reds if either building is
      absent, so a later re-author cannot silently drop them.
- [ ] Two consecutive authoring boots produce byte-identical `Dawnmere.zscen`, and
      the other four committed scenes are left untouched.
- [ ] The committed-asset SHA256 row for `Dawnmere.zscen` in
      `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md` matches the re-authored bytes.
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run.

A boot unit in `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` reads the committed `Dawnmere.zscen` off disk and reds if either building is absent, so a later re-author cannot silently drop them.
Two consecutive authoring boots produce byte-identical `Dawnmere.zscen`, and the other four committed scenes are left untouched.
The committed-asset SHA256 row for `Dawnmere.zscen` in `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md` matches the re-authored bytes.
Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run.

payload.body:
## Goal

ZM-D-168 visual audit, item 4, and the half of ZM-58 a machine can do.
`Games/Zenithmon/Docs/History.md` records the finding as **"Dawnmere reads as an
open field, not a town — no buildings; the Trade Post and Care Center are
dialogue only."** Items 1, 2 and 3 of that audit closed on pixels (ZM-D-169 /
ZM-D-170 / ZM-D-171). Item 4 is still open.

**The gap is PLACEMENT, not assets.** Measured on `master` 2026-08-26; every
line number below was opened and confirmed on that date:

- `Games/Zenithmon/Assets/Buildings/` carries all **30** baked bundles, each
  complete — `.zmesh`, `.zmodel`, `.zmtrl`, `_facade.ztxtr` — `CareCenter` and
  `TradePost` among them. S4 `ZM_BuildingGen`'s SC5 disk bake shipped.
- **Not one of the seven committed `.zscen` files references a single one of
  them.** The string `Buildings/` occurs **zero** times in `Dawnmere.zscen`, and
  zero times in the other six.

So the town has a shop clerk NPC (`Npc_TradePostClerk`, authored at
`Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.cpp:70`), a Care Center heal
flow (`Games/Zenithmon/Source/CareCenter/ZM_CareCenter.cpp`), and roster rows for
both buildings with real 10.0 x 8.0 footprints
(`Games/Zenithmon/Source/Data/ZM_BuildingData.cpp:49-50`) — and no building
standing anywhere in the scene.

**ZM-58 is BLOCKED by this ticket and stays open.** ZM-58 is the aesthetic
judgement — a person looking at the finished town and deciding whether it reads
as one. **This ticket is not that.** Everything specified below is buildable and
machine-verifiable; finishing it is what gives ZM-58 something to look at.

### Constraints that bound the work

**★ THE TERRAIN RECIPE IS FROZEN — place inside the sites it already reserves.**
`Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp` reserves Dawnmere pads
`Plaza` (512, 512) r=60, `Home` (384, 496) r=36, `Lab` (640, 552) r=48 and
`RouteGate`, plus the `Plaza`, `PlazaLandmark` and `ReservedRivalHome` landmarks.
Editing ANY pad, path or landmark regenerates the WHOLE Dawnmere heightmap — the
recipe's hydraulic erosion pass is region-wide rather than pad-local, as ZM-D-173
found the expensive way — which re-measures every table in
`Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h` and re-bakes the committed
navmesh. That is a different and much larger ticket.

**★ RE-AUTHORING `Dawnmere.zscen` STILL NEEDS A WINDOWED BOOT, FOR A REASON THAT
IS NOT THE OLD ONE.** ZEN-6 (`cbebea74`, 2026-08-26) removed the engine's `.zscen`
publish guard, so a headless boot may now CHANGE a committed scene. It deliberately
did not change Zenithmon: `Games/Zenithmon/Zenithmon.cpp:3848` still defers
Dawnmere's scene authoring on a Null backend by the game's own choice, logging
`sceneAuthoring=DEFERRED`. ZM-D-190's canonical order therefore still applies —
build both configs; authoring boot on `Vulkan_*_True` with `--skip-unit-tests`;
`git status` the WHOLE `Assets/` tree, because a Vulkan boot authors all five
scenes; a second boot proving byte-identity; only THEN the gate.

**★ `ZM_GreyboxVisual` HAS NO BUILDING POPULATION.** It serves three — BLOCKOUT,
HUMAN and PROP — and its BLOCKOUT branch is pinned to `1.0e-4f` by
`Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_AutoTests_InteriorTint.cpp:102`, so that branch must not
move. ZM-67's PROP branch is the nearest precedent for how a placed building
should resolve a generated static model. Its serialization contract is that
nothing new is written — `WriteToDataStream` emits a single version `u_int` — so a
fourth population must not grow the per-component byte count.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The Trade Post and the Care Center stand in `Dawnmere.zscen` as placed
      entities resolving the baked `Buildings/TradePost` and `Buildings/CareCenter`
      bundles, on measured ground, inside terrain sites the recipe already
      reserves — with the recipe itself unedited.
- [ ] Their placement coordinates live as compiled constants in
      `Games/Zenithmon/Source/World/ZM_DawnmerePlacement.h`, derived rather than
      re-spelled, in the same measured-table idiom the Home shell and the SC-D lab
      numbers use.
- [ ] A boot unit in `Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_CommittedSceneBytes.cpp` reads
      the committed `Dawnmere.zscen` off disk and reds if either building is
      absent, so a later re-author cannot silently drop them.
- [ ] Two consecutive authoring boots produce byte-identical `Dawnmere.zscen`, and
      the other four committed scenes are left untouched.
- [ ] The committed-asset SHA256 row for `Dawnmere.zscen` in
      `Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md` matches the re-authored bytes.
- [ ] Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run.

payload.reason: ZM-58's deliverable is a human visual sign-off that Dawnmere reads as a town. There is nothing to sign off until the buildings exist: measured 2026-08-26, all 30 baked building bundles ship under Assets/Buildings/ and the string 'Buildings/' occurs zero times in every one of the seven committed .zscen files. ZM-71 authors the Trade Post and Care Center into Dawnmere.zscen; judging the result is ZM-58.

payload.title: R1-9 — camera-clearance coverage + re-derived budget
reasons: Migrated from the R1 slice table in Status.md, which declares R1-9 deps R1-6. The technical reason is blocker #4 in the R1 slice brief: the three camera-clearance tests are HARD-SCOPED to Dawnmere, and R1-9 extracts them into a region-parameterised header and RE-DERIVES the budget from fresh captures. That derivation raycasts Route 1 columns against the Route 1 PHYSICS WORLD, which R1-6 changes by adding two trainer bodies to it. Deriving the budget first means deriving it against a Route 1 that is about to change. Note the clearance maths is a function of ground and geometry and the sample table deliberately carries no rings around NPCs, so the effect is on the raycast world rather than on the sample set.
