values.Decision: The headless `.zscen` publish guard in `Zenith_Editor::SaveActiveScene` is REMOVED, because its cause was fixed rather than tolerated. `Zenith_TerrainEditor::EnsureTreeEntities` no longer returns false on its first line under `Zenith_IsNullRenderer()`: it creates `TerrainTrees_Trunk` and `TerrainTrees_Leaves` and their `Zenith_InstancedMeshComponent`s on every backend. No replacement branch was needed for the GPU half, because `Flux_InstanceGroup::InitialiseGPUBuffers` on the Null backend is already `Zenith_Null_MemoryManager` handing back dummy handles -- the backend supplies the skip. `Zenith_SceneData::CompareWithFile` and `Zenith_ScenePublishDelta` SURVIVE the removal, promoted from guard to audit and applied on every backend: `AuditScenePublish` logs `[ScenePublish] CREATED|IDENTICAL|CHANGED`, still skips a byte-identical write, and still reports a publish that drops entities as a `Zenith_Error` -- it no longer REFUSES, because deleting an entity is a legitimate authoring change, but the original defect's exact shape does not pass in silence. `EnsureTreeEntities` and the two entity-name constants are now public seams so a unit can pin them without driving a brush stroke.
values.Why: The guard treated a symptom. Its stated reason was correct -- a Null tools boot authored an INCOMPLETE world, and serializing that subset over a tracked asset once dropped RenderTest's two instanced-tree entities, ~323 KB of a 361,753-byte file, on every headless boot, with a dirty `git status` as the only symptom. But the incompleteness had a single cause: an authoring step that needed a live GPU resource bailed out ENTIRELY instead of skipping only the GPU part. That bail conflated two different things -- creating the entities and their components, which is SCENE DATA and exactly what `WriteToDataStream` serializes, against allocating the GPU buffers, which is not serialized at all. The decisive evidence is that a headless boot ALREADY ran the whole chain verbatim -- `LoadMesh -> EnsureInstanceGroupCreated -> Reserve -> InitialiseGPUBuffers -> SpawnInstanceWithMatrix` -- every time `Zenith_InstancedMeshComponent::ReadFromDataStream` loaded the committed scene's 2,520 tree instances. The authoring path and the load path differed only in that one bail, so there was never a GPU allocation to skip; the branch skipped the scene data instead. ★ THE COST THIS REMOVES: eight Zenithmon tickets carried `needs-gpu` for no reason other than that they re-author a committed scene, and six of the ten tickets on the S8 critical path sat behind one, so the chain alternated human and agent work and the loop could never get more than one ticket ahead of a keyboard session. ★ AND WHAT REPLACES THE GUARD AS PROTECTION IS A TEST, NOT A POLICY: `Editor.TreeAuthoringIsBackendNeutral` asserts the canonical authoring step produces its two entities BY NAME, each carrying the component and each non-transient, on whichever backend is running -- so a re-introduced Null bail reddens a unit instead of silently shrinking a tracked asset. `RT_SceneAssetIntegrity` becomes the end-to-end half: its assertions are unchanged, but they were near-vacuous headless (a headless boot never wrote the file) and are now real.
values.Tests that lock it: OBSERVED, not asserted. A `Null_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True` boot driven with `--automated-test <T> --skip-unit-tests` re-authored every committed scene both games publish and reported `[ScenePublish] IDENTICAL` for all five: RenderTest at 82 entities / 361,753 bytes (byte-for-byte the committed file, trees included), and Zenithmon's FrontEnd, PlayerHome, Battle and ProfLab. Zero `CHANGED` verdicts; `git status` clean afterwards. ★ THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THAT PROOF WAS WORTHLESS AND LOOKED EXACTLY LIKE SUCCESS: the unit-gate boot exits before the editor-automation queue drains, so it authors nothing, emits no scene marker and leaves a clean tree. A clean tree is the fail-open state here, and the proof requires an authoring boot plus the marker. Units: `Editor.HeadlessSaveNeverRewritesSceneAsset` (which pinned the removed policy, and carried its own `if constexpr` Null branch) is replaced by `Editor.ScenePublishWritesOnEveryBackend`, which asserts the same property on BOTH backends and so needs no branch; `Editor.TreeAuthoringIsBackendNeutral` is new; `SceneSaveDeltaClassifiesPublish` is untouched and still pins all three delta results. Net +1 unit, BACKEND-NEUTRAL, so every game's row moved and ALL THREE WERE MEASURED: Combat 1650->1651, Zenithmon 3419->3420, Null RenderTest 1741->1742. Gates: all 8 Engine builds green (every game compiles), Combat suite and unit gate green, and the full audit of all ten `Zenith_IsNullRenderer()` sites recorded -- three removed, five in `Zenith/Editor/` confirmed correct as written, two in `Flux/Vegetation` correct (they create no entity), one being the constexpr definition itself.

values.Decision: ZM-D-213's item-reward reasoning is CORRECTED before the commit: a repeat win over a gym leader now DEDUPLICATES the take-home item. `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState` gates the grant on `ZM_Bag::Has(xRow.m_eItemReward)`, so `m_bItemGranted` is false and the bag count stays 1 on a second win. The badge was already idempotent by its own structure (AwardBadge ORs one bit) and prize MONEY still stacks. Three columns, three mechanisms, and the header now states three reasons instead of arguing both sides. ZM-D-213's board row predates the review and still carries the superseded reasoning; the repo-local entry has been corrected in place and points here.
values.Why: ★ A PRECEDENT WAS APPLIED WITHOUT ITS CAUSE, AND THAT IS THE GENERAL LESSON. The first draft let the item stack, reasoning that prize MONEY stacks on a repeat win under ZM-D-135. But ZM-D-135's correction (ZM-D-208, DecisionLog.md:165-172) states money's cause explicitly: it pays again BECAUSE 'ZM-D-135 forbids a new ZM_GameState member to record it'. For an item that cause is ABSENT -- `m_xBag` IS the record and `ZM_Bag::Has` already answers 'do I own this', so gating adds no state whatsoever. Reading the ruling's DECISION ('money pays again') and not its WHY is what made a non-transferable precedent look binding, which is the same failure mode ZM-D-212 records one entry earlier about surveys, and the same shape the tick protocol now names as a ruling's third kind of sentence. AND THE CONSEQUENCE WAS NOT COSMETIC: Verdant Lash is `m_bConsumable = false` (ZM_ItemData.cpp:129, pinned by ZM_Tests_Gym1Placement.cpp:1206 -- 'TMs in this game are reusable'), so a second copy has exactly ONE use: `ZM_ShopSell` (ZM_ShopLogic.cpp:68-76) converting it to its `m_uSellPrice` of 500. That is a farmable prize -- precisely the shape ZM-D-208's postscript says the per-trainer defeat flag exists to forbid -- so the money precedent would have re-opened the hole the flag was added to close. It is moot in normal play because the defeat flag gates re-battles, which is exactly why no gate would ever have caught it: the assertion was a compiled constant that PASSED, `run_unit_gate` only checks `ran == baseline`, and `doc_lint` does not read C++. ★ SECOND FINDING, and it is why this entry exists rather than a silent edit: the 'load-bearing' default member initializers ZM-D-213 recorded as a DURABLE FINDING shipped with ZERO COVERAGE. Deleting `= ZM_BADGE_NONE` / `= ZM_ITEM_NONE` left every gate green, because all four real rows spell every column and the six fixtures never READ the new ones -- a comment asserting a guard exists, which ZM-D-212 already names as worse than no guard. Closed with a compile-time nine-field aggregate probe plus two static_asserts in `ZM_TrainerData.h`, needing no test file and moving no unit count. Note the trap is wider than first recorded: item enumerator 0 is `ZM_ITEM_CATCHORB`, a REAL item, not only `ZM_BADGE_BLOOM`.
values.Tests that lock it: `TrainerReward_SecondWinDoesNotDoubleAwardTheBadge` now asserts the badge count stays 1 AND the TM count stays 1 with `m_bItemGranted` false on the second win -- it previously asserted the count reached 2. `TrainerReward_ByRowPrimitiveGrantsWhateverTheRowNames`'s fixture now carries `ZM_ITEM_TM_TITANBEAM` rather than Fenna's own TM, with cross-checks that the row's item is present and Fenna's absent, so the ITEM half of 'reads off the row, not hardcoded' is proven rather than assumed -- previously it used the same TM Fenna awards and could not distinguish the two. `xZM_TRAINER_DATA_NINE_COLUMN_DEFAULTS_PROBE` plus two static_asserts in `ZM_TrainerData.h` fail the BUILD if either trailing column loses its NONE default. `ZM_Bag::Has` is total over `ZM_ITEM_NONE` (GetCount range-checks before `PocketIndexFor` reaches the asserting `ZM_GetItemData`), so NONE rows are unaffected. Unit count UNCHANGED: no ZENITH_TEST added or removed -- assertions, one fixture value and comments only -- so the 3419 pin measured before the fix stands and was re-confirmed by the verify phase.

values.Decision: ZM-70 (G1-3) wires the leader-win reward onto the SHIPPED write-back seam rather than building anything new. `ZM_TrainerData` gains two trailing columns, `m_eBadgeReward` and `m_eItemReward`; Fenna's row is the first to carry real values (`ZM_BADGE_BLOOM`, `ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH`) and every other row names the NONE sentinels. Per ZM-D-208 Ruling 2's reasoning, which ZM-70 cites, a by-ROW primitive `ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool)` is extracted and the by-ID overload becomes classify + is-registered + resolve + forward, so the reward mechanism can be driven by a hand-built fixture row and its coverage cannot be retired by a content change. The badge goes through the existing `ZM_GameState::AwardBadge` mask (save module 5) and the TM through the existing `ZM_Bag::Add` (module 6): NO new ZM_GameState state and NO save-schema change. `Components/ZM_BattleDirector.cpp` needed no edit -- the call site's signature is unchanged. 'Grants Verdant Lash' is implemented as granting the TM ITEM into the bag, not as writing a move into a party monster's `m_axMoves`: there is no item-USE path anywhere in this game, which ZM-D-196 Ruling 1 already established ('no way to USE an item at all'), so the enum value and the data rows exist with ZERO runtime consumers. Building one would be a systems slice this ticket explicitly is not.
values.Why: ★ THE DURABLE FINDING, and it is why this is a decision rather than a work-log line: APPENDING A TRAILING ENUM COLUMN TO AN AGGREGATE-INITIALIZED ROW TABLE IS NOT SAFE WITHOUT AN EXPLICIT DEFAULT. `ZM_TrainerData` rows are POSITIONAL aggregate initializers -- the struct's own comment already warns that inserting a column mid-struct shifts every trailing value -- but the danger at the END is different and undocumented. `ZM_BADGE_BLOOM` is enumerator 0, so a trailing `ZM_BADGE_ID` with no default member initializer VALUE-INITIALIZES to 0, i.e. to 'this trainer awards the Bloom Badge'. `Tests/ZM_Tests_TrainerData.cpp` builds SIX hand-built fixtures using only the first nine positional fields, and every one of them would silently have claimed Gym 1's badge. The columns therefore ship with `= ZM_BADGE_NONE` and `= ZM_ITEM_NONE`, which are load-bearing rather than stylistic. SEVEN MORE GYM LEADERS will add reward rows, and the same trap arms itself for every future trailing column whose enum has a meaningful zero. Two further notes for whoever adds the next one. (1) The file that would have caught it was OUTSIDE the worker's permitted write list, and it was found only because a file list bounds WRITES and not READS -- the survey must read wider than it edits. (2) A repeat win does NOT deduplicate the item: `ZM_Bag::Add` yields a second copy, deliberately, because prize MONEY already stacks on a repeat win under ZM-D-135's ruling that 'pay once' is a CALLER-side gate rather than this primitive's job, and gating the item here would diverge from that precedent while adding no state. It is moot in production because the defeat flag gates re-battles. The behaviour is PROVEN by a unit rather than assumed, and an open Questions row on ZM-70 records the reading in case it should be overruled -- the fix would be one line.
values.Tests that lock it: Four new boot units in `Tests/ZM_Tests_Party.cpp` Section I, beside the existing write-back coverage in Section H: `TrainerReward_BeatingFennaAwardsTheBloomBadgeAndGrantsVerdantLash` (the production case -- badge, item, money and flag together), `TrainerReward_ByRowPrimitiveGrantsWhateverTheRowNames` (drives the by-ROW seam with a NON-Fenna hand-built fixture, plus its fail-closed loss arm, so the coverage survives any content change), `TrainerReward_SecondWinDoesNotDoubleAwardTheBadge` (badge count stays 1; documents that the item stacks to 2 rather than asserting an assumed dedup), and `TrainerReward_BadgeAndItemSurviveASaveLoadRoundTrip` (reads both back off a freshly-decoded `ZM_GameState`, never off the mutated original -- the DoD's whole point, since a badge in a mask that is never written passes an in-memory assertion and fails the player). The existing Vesper test was STRENGTHENED with badge/item neutrality rather than duplicated, so it moves no count. `<vector>` in the round-trip test follows `Tests/ZM_Tests_SaveSchema.cpp:25`'s established Encode/Decode idiom for the identical mechanism -- the only two files in the game that use it. Gate: Zenithmon --headless build, the D3D12 non-tools compile, `zenith test Zenithmon --headless`, `doc_lint`, and the boot unit gate OBSERVED at 3419 ran / 3417 passed / 0 failed, moving `Tools/unit_baselines.json` 3415 -> 3419. Registry unchanged at 70.

values.Decision: ZM-D-210's `Tests that lock it` is CORRECTED in two places, and the code it described is fixed. (1) The solvability proof's fourth anti-vacuity arm shipped BROKEN and was repaired before the commit landed. Its bound was `fMIDDLE_LIMIT = fZM_GYM1_INNER_MAX_X - fZM_GYM1_HEDGE_OPENING` -- derived from the very constant it claimed to police -- so widening the opening widened the restriction by exactly the same amount and the arm was invariant in the opening width. The bound is now `fZM_GYM1_INNER_MAX_X * 0.5f` (5.875 m, the middle half of the room), which reads only the shell. The opening width at which the arm reds is now COMPUTED -- `fREDS_AT_OPENING = innerMax - limit + playerRadius` = 6.275 m -- and asserted from both sides: it must EXCEED the authored 3.75 m (so today's layout is sealed as a geometric consequence rather than a lattice coincidence) and must sit under both half the inner width and twice the authored opening (so a materially widened opening reds). The lattice flip width (6.65 m, outermost admitted column x = +/-5.5) is computed through the search's own predicate and printed in the failure message. (2) The learnset mitigation was off by one: a level-<=5 build reaches the first TWO same-type picks (k=0, k=1), not three -- the third STAB pick is `auPicks[3]` at level 14/12/10. The mitigation stands with one index of margin. Also corrected: `ZM_MoveData.cpp`'s claim that 'a power at or below 50 would have moved them' -- at EXACTLY 50 the stable sort keeps table order, leaving Verdant Lash behind Seedshot at index 2, so the bound is STRICTLY below 50.
values.Why: ★ A SELF-REFERENTIAL GUARD PASSED EVERY GATE. The broken arm was inside a suite that ran 3415 units with 0 failures; the Zenithmon build, the D3D12 non-tools compile, the headless test suite and `doc_lint` were all green with it in place. It could not have been otherwise: the test PASSES, `doc_lint` does not read C++, and a build only proves the file compiled. Setting `fZM_GYM1_HEDGE_OPENING` to 11.75 m -- half the room's inner width, three token stubs rather than a maze -- left the entire suite green, because NOTHING in it bounded the opening from above. The per-band unit's opening clause compares `x.Min().x - innerMinX` against `fZM_GYM1_HEDGE_OPENING`, the same constant on both sides, and its only size clause is a LOWER bound. This is the guard-compared-against-a-recomputation-of-itself shape, and the only control that caught it was the independent reviewer. ★ AND THE DEFINITION OF DONE WOULD HAVE PASSED IT. The DoD asked for 'an anti-vacuity arm proving at least one wall genuinely blocks a shorter route'; arms (a)-(c) deliver exactly that and were verified non-vacuous. Arm (d) was the worker going BEYOND the DoD, and it was the broken one -- so a checkbox audit, which is what the protocol's Green-but-DoD-unmet arm inspects, reports this ticket complete. Nothing in the pipeline looks for a test that CLAIMS MORE THAN IT PROVES, and a comment asserting a guard exists is worse than no guard, because the next author reads it and stops looking. Two further instances of exactly that were found in the same file family and fixed: `ZM_Gym1Placement.h`'s solvability block attributed the opening ceiling to arm (3), which also does not bound it, and the per-band unit now carries an explicit signpost that its opening clause is a lower bound only and that the ceiling lives in the maze arm.
values.Tests that lock it: The repaired arm in `Gym1_EveryHedgeBandBlocksTheDirectRouteToTheLeader` (`Tests/ZM_Tests_Gym1Placement.cpp`). Its two meta-assertions pin `fMIDDLE_LIMIT` from both sides: loosen the strip past the gaps and the 'reds-at exceeds authored opening' clause fails; tighten it toward the centreline and the 'reds-at is under half the inner width, and under twice the authored opening' clause fails. Both existing vacuity guards are kept -- both endpoints must lie inside the restriction, and the same restriction over an EMPTY room must still succeed -- so the new bound cannot fail for the wrong reason. `ZM_GetGym1CameraSightClearanceOverFirstHedgeAtHeight(float)` was extracted so the camera anti-vacuity arm runs the SHIPPED function at a different height instead of a second copy of the interpolation, with an equality clause pinning the zero-arg accessor to it -- closing the same could-drift-silently shape one level down. Unit count UNCHANGED: no ZENITH_TEST added or removed, four assertions added inside existing units and one replaced, so the 3415 pin measured before the fix still stands and was re-confirmed by the verify phase. KNOWN AND DELIBERATE: between openings of 6.275 m and 6.65 m the meta-assertion reds while the search itself still passes -- that band says 'the seal is no longer provable, you are relying on the 0.5 m lattice', and a legitimate re-tune into it must move the bound rather than the assertion. Stated at the assertion.

values.Decision: ZM-28 (G1-1) lands Gym 1's pure half: `ZM_Gym1Placement.h` declares a 24x20 m interior hall whose maze is three full-width hedge bands with a single opening each, alternating sides (a serpentine), and ships the walkability predicate the tests and the future authoring both read rather than re-deriving geometry. `ZM_BadgeData.{h,cpp}` carries the eight GDD badge indices and names in the ZM-D-009 compiled-const-table idiom, with a static_assert tying its width to the EXISTING `uZM_BADGE_COUNT` rather than restating it -- no badge state, no save-schema change. Fenna is `ZM_TRAINER_GYM1_FENNA`: 3 GRASS monsters at the GDD's level 13, prize 2600, `ZM_AI_TIER_SMART`, defeat flag the ALREADY-REGISTERED `ZM_STORY_FLAG_GYM1_DEFEATED`. Verdant Lash lands as both `ZM_MOVE_VERDANTLASH` and `ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH`. Fenna is authored at IDENTITY rotation and the room is shaped so that is correct -- identity forward is +Z, she stands at z=-7.0 and the arrival is at z=+7.0, so she already faces the player, which sidesteps ProfLab's frozen-half-turn problem BY PLACEMENT and lets her legally wear an AABB collider (ZM-D-193). This slice AUTHORS NOTHING: no .zscen byte moved.
values.Why: ★ THE DURABLE FINDING, and it is the reason this entry exists rather than a work-log line: APPENDING A MOVE IS NEVER INERT. `ZM_MoveData` is not a lookup table -- it has two DERIVED consumers that scan the whole of it. `Source/Data/ZM_Learnsets.cpp:52` (`ZM_GetSpeciesLearnset`) rebuilds every species' level-up list by partitioning the entire move table by type and sorting the damaging buckets with `SortByEffectivePower`, a stable insertion sort ASCENDING on raw power; and `Source/Data/ZM_SpeciesData.cpp:555` (`ZM_GetSpeciesEggMoves`) scans the table again in table order for type matches not already in the learnset, capped at 6. So one appended GRASS move re-sorts every GRASS species' learnset, which propagates into `ZM_BuildWildEnemySpec`, `ZM_BuildMonsterRecord`, breeding and the battle tower. NO BLAST-RADIUS GREP FINDS THIS -- the coupling is by table scan, not by identifier, so a file-list survey over the changed symbols comes back clean. It was found only because the worker read the consumers. SEVEN MORE GYM REWARD MOVES REMAIN, so this recurs seven times unless it is written down. Mitigation taken here: Verdant Lash is 65 power, which sorts strictly ABOVE the shipped Leafcut (55) and therefore lands at sorted index >= 3 in the GRASS bucket -- the first three same-type picks are the only ones a level-<=5 build reaches, so the L5 starter and every Route 1 encounter are unaffected; deeper GRASS learnsets shift by one entry. That relationship is asserted as a COMPARISON against the shipped Leafcut row rather than as a literal 65, so it survives a re-tune of either move. Verified against the code at both cited sites, not against their comments. Secondary finding, same shape: `ZM_ITEM_ID` groups TMs in the MIDDLE of the enum, before the key items, and `ZM_SaveSchema` writes bag item ids as raw uint16 -- so filing the new TM with its siblings would have renumbered six key items and invalidated every existing save. It is appended at the true end after `ZM_ITEM_EGGVOUCHER`; `ZM_MOVE_ID` is grouped by type and got the same treatment. Scope context: badge STATE and the teach-move MECHANISM both already existed (ZM-D-209 item 4), so this slice adds rows and indices, never systems.
values.Tests that lock it: New `Tests/ZM_Tests_Gym1Placement.cpp` (13 boot units). Solvability is a 4-connected BFS over a 47x39 lattice at the shipped body radius, with three anti-vacuity arms rather than one: (a) the empty-room baseline must equal the EXACT straight-line cell count, so the search is known sound before it is trusted; (b) the maze route must be strictly longer than that baseline; (c) every band must block the arrival->leader centreline AND be shown to be the one blocking it (removing just that band unblocks that point); and the strongest arm -- restricting the walk to the middle of the room must make the maze UNSOLVABLE while both endpoints stay inside the restriction, which is what reds if someone widens an opening toward the centre. `ZM_GetGym1CameraSightClearanceOverFirstHedge()` measures the 2.0 m hedge against the 3.9 m settled camera (~0.59 m) with an anti-vacuity arm feeding the shell's own 4.0 m wall height through identical arithmetic and requiring it to FAIL. `Gym1_LeaderFacesTheArrivalAtIdentity` checks the identity-rotation claim through the shipped `ZM_ForwardFromRotation` rather than by restating the axis. `Fenna_AuthoredValuesAreExact` in `ZM_Tests_TrainerData.cpp` pins her row. Three pinned counts moved with the data -- `uEXPECTED_TRAINERS` 2->3, `uEXPECTED_ITEMS` 90->91, `uEXPECTED_MOVES` 218->219 -- each spelled in its TEST rather than read off the table, so a roster change is a failure and not a tautology. Gate: regen (both new .cpp files detected and compiled), Zenithmon --headless build, the D3D12 non-tools compile, `zenith test Zenithmon --headless`, and the boot unit gate OBSERVED at 3415 ran / 3413 passed / 0 failed, moving `Tools/unit_baselines.json` 3401 -> 3415. Registry unchanged at 70.

values.Decision: ZM-28 (Gym 1) is SPLIT into three slices: G1-1 ZM-28 data + placement header (PURE, re-authors nothing), G1-2 ZM-69 authors Gym1.zscen + the Thornacre door (needs-gpu + human-gate), G1-3 ZM-70 badge + teach-move on a leader win (PURE). G1-2 and G1-3 both depend only on G1-1 and run in PARALLEL. ZM-29's blocker moves from ZM-28 to ZM-69 AND ZM-70.
values.Why: One STORY carried a whole gym -- a scene, a leader battle, a badge award and a teach-move reward -- behind a four-line Definition of Done, and a survey done before dispatching found three separable seams plus a mislabelling. (1) SHAPE: the R1 slice table already splits PURE data and placement from SCENE AUTHORING, for the reason that authoring writes a tracked asset and pure work does not; Gym 1 has exactly that seam. (2) LABELS: ZM-28 carried human-gate, so even the pure data work would have parked at In Review and needed a person before the next slice could start. Only the scene slice wants a visual sign-off, and only it needs needs-gpu -- Gym1.zscen does NOT exist so creating it is headless-legal, but the Thornacre door is a CHANGE to a committed scene, which the .zscen publish guard refuses headless. That distinction is invisible at the whole-gym granularity. (3) PARALLELISM: the 2026-08-25 link audit found S8 composed as a single linear chain, so its queue depth was 1 and any stall stopped the sprint; G1-3 needs no scene, so making it depend on G1-1 rather than on G1-2 gives the sprint two claimable strands instead of one. (4) SCOPE was overestimated: badge state is already complete and persisted (uZM_BADGE_COUNT, m_uBadgeMask, AwardBadge/HasBadge in ZM_GameState.h:89-176, save module 5), and teach-move already exists as ZM_ITEM_EFFECT_TEACH_MOVE -- so G1-3 is a wiring slice, not a systems one, and the bodies say so to stop a worker rebuilding either. The design was NOT invented: GameDesignDocument.md already specifies Thornacre, Fenna (Grass, L13), the Bloom Badge, Verdant Lash and a hedge-maze layout, and all three bodies inline it per I3.
values.Tests that lock it: G1-1 carries a headless solvability unit over the declared maze WITH an anti-vacuity arm (a reachability test over an empty room passes vacuously, so at least one wall must be proven to block a shorter route). G1-2 requires two byte-identical windowed boots and a git status showing only the intended scene paths. G1-3 requires a save/load ROUND TRIP for both the badge and the taught move, read back off a reloaded save rather than off the mutated object, plus a by-ROW seam so its coverage cannot be retired by a content change (ZM-D-208 ruling 2's reasoning, applied here).

values.Decision: The Zenith living docs are MIRRORED into Notion pages, one way. The Markdown files stay authoritative; `zagent docs sync` never writes back.
values.Why: Four things depend on the files being on disk and would break under a move. (1) Tools/doc_lint.ps1 gates push-to-master by reading six of them and resolving their cross-links. (2) `zagent decide` appends to Games/Zenithmon/Docs/DecisionLog.md, because that is where a Zenith session greps. (3) Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md is the AUTHORITY for the pinned unit-gate baseline mirrored into zm-tests.yml and agent.config.json - an authority site you need a browser to read cannot be reconciled against a gate. (4) A loop worker is spawned with no Bash and no network; it reads its binding briefing off disk with the Read tool. The cost is owning the drift, and each page records a fingerprint of what was written so `zagent docs status` names the stale pages without touching anything.

values.Question: ZM-70: on a REPEAT win over a gym leader the badge is idempotent but the TM item stacks to a second copy. Is that right, or should the item dedupe too?
values.Context: DoD item 5 reads 'Awarding twice does not double-grant, and the badge count is right after a repeat win.' The badge is structurally idempotent -- AwardBadge ORs one bit -- so the badge half needs no code and is proven by TrainerReward_SecondWinDoesNotDoubleAwardTheBadge. The ITEM half is the open question: ZM_Bag::Add on a second win yields 2 copies of ZM_ITEM_TM_VERDANTLASH. The worker let it stack, citing the shipped precedent that prize MONEY is also paid again on a repeat win, because ZM-D-135 makes 'pay once' a CALLER-side gate (the sight FSM / defeat flag) rather than this primitive's job. The unit proves the actual behaviour rather than asserting an assumed one.
values.Best guess taken: Leave it stacking. Three reasons: it is consistent with money, which already stacks by ruling; it adds no ZM_GameState state, which ZM-D-135 forbids; and it is MOOT in production because the defeat flag gates re-battles, so the second win cannot occur through normal play. I read DoD item 5 as scoped to the badge -- 'the badge count is right' is the measurable clause and 'double-grant' is the badge verb. If that reading is wrong the fix is one line, gating the Bag::Add on !m_xBag.Has(xRow.m_eItemReward), and it would want its own decision entry because it diverges from the money precedent.
values.Resolution: ANSWERED, and the guess recorded above was WRONG. The item must deduplicate, and it now does -- ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState gates the grant on ZM_Bag::Has(xRow.m_eItemReward). The independent review found the ZM-D-135 money precedent does not transfer: ZM-D-208's correction (DecisionLog.md:165-172) states money's cause explicitly -- it pays again BECAUSE ZM-D-135 forbids a new ZM_GameState member to record 'already paid' -- and for an item that cause is absent, since m_xBag IS the record and ZM_Bag::Has already answers it, so gating costs no state at all. My 'adds no ZM_GameState state' was therefore an argument FOR gating, which I had recorded as an argument against. The consequence was also not cosmetic as I assumed: Verdant Lash is m_bConsumable = false, so a second copy has exactly one use -- ZM_ShopSell converting it to its 500 sell price -- a FARMABLE PRIZE, the precise shape ZM-D-208's postscript says the per-trainer defeat flag exists to forbid. So DoD item 5 was genuinely UNMET and would have merged Done on my reading. Recorded as ZM-D-214; ZM-D-213 corrected in place. The general lesson, now in tick.md: a ruling's WHY is what decides whether it transfers, and reading only its DECISION is how a non-transferable precedent looks binding.

values.Question: ZM-69 (Gym 1 door): once Gym1 is registered, ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry U4's independence arm has no unbacked target left. Rebuild it on a synthetic build index, or retire it?
values.Context: U4 (ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry.cpp:582-604) proves the registry is INDEPENDENT of the compiled world table by pointing at a scene that is declared in the table but deliberately unregistered. Its own comment says: 'if a gym scene has genuinely shipped, replace this arm with another unbacked target.' Gym1 is the last such target -- after ZM-69 all eight ZM_SCENE_ID rows are registered, so no real scene can play the role.
values.Best guess taken: Rebuild the arm on a SYNTHETIC build index rather than a real scene. That keeps the independence property under test, but it changes what the arm proves: today it proves a real declared-but-unbacked scene stays unregistered, and afterwards it would prove only that the lookup rejects an index nothing registered. That is a weaker claim about a stronger-typed input, and choosing it is a test-design ruling rather than a mechanical move. Retiring the arm outright is the other option and loses the independence coverage entirely.

values.Question: ZM-69 (Gym 1 door): where should the Thornacre gym-door ground column go, given the recipe's own FromGym landmark fails the pad-containment clause by construction?
values.Context: The Thornacre gym door and its FromGym spawn marker each need their own MEASURED ground column -- ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h:613-619 is explicit that a sensor reading its neighbour's column is 'part-buried or hovering with every scale constant still correct', and the two nearest existing columns are ~750 m away on separately-eroded ground. But the natural site fails an existing invariant: ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp:185 puts the 'Gym' pad at centre (760, 864) with m_fFlattenRadius = 50.0, and :214 puts the 'FromGym' landmark at (760, 28, 814) -- EXACTLY 50.0 m from that centre. fTH_PAD_CONTAINMENT_FRACTION = 0.75 (ZM_Tests_ThornacrePlacement.cpp:76) gives a 37.5 m limit, so a column on the recipe's own landmark REDS the same clause U12/U13 apply to the route-gate anchors. Verified independently by the orchestrator against all four constants. The 'Gym' landmark itself is at the pad centre (0 m) and is fine.
values.Best guess taken: Three options, none free. (a) Pull the marker inboard of 37.5 m -- a ZM_ThornacrePlacement.h change, but it DECOUPLES the authored marker from the recipe landmark, which is the coupling U12's shape exists to enforce. (b) Move the pad or the landmark in ZM_TerrainAuthoring.cpp -- that header warns a recipe change re-measures every ground table in the game. (c) Exempt the gym column from the containment clause -- weakening a deliberate assertion. (a) looks cheapest but trades away the invariant that makes these anchors auditable, so it is a ruling rather than a worker's pick.

values.Question: Should ZM-25 -> ZM-26 be FLIPPED? R1-9 derives a camera-clearance budget that R1-10 then invalidates.
values.Context: Found during the 2026-08-25 blocking-link audit. The R1 slice table in Status.md declares R1-10 deps R1-9, and ZM-26's own title says do LAST and in isolation because it re-authors both Dawnmere and Route1 -- so the link is a legitimate risk-isolation ordering and I kept it. But it sits in tension with the reason recorded on the neighbouring edge. ZM-24 -> ZM-25 holds because R1-9 re-derives its budget by raycasting Route 1 columns against the Route 1 PHYSICS WORLD, which R1-6 changes by adding two trainer bodies. R1-10 adds ANOTHER body to that same world (the relocated Warden). By the identical argument, running R1-9 before R1-10 derives a budget against a Route 1 that R1-10 then changes -- the exact staleness the R1-6 dependency exists to prevent, just one slice later. Mitigating: the clearance maths is a function of ground and geometry, and the sample table deliberately carries no rings around NPCs (ZM_AutoTests_CameraClearance.cpp header), so an NPC body may matter less than terrain would.
values.Best guess taken: Keep the ordering but make R1-10 re-derive. Either add a Definition-of-Done line to ZM-26 requiring the camera-clearance budget be re-confirmed after the Warden lands, or explicitly record that NPC bodies are out of scope for the clearance budget -- in which case the ZM-24 -> ZM-25 reason should be narrowed to the sample-set/parameterisation work rather than the physics world. Flipping the link is the third option but fights ZM-26's own do LAST instruction.

values.Question: What replaces the FLAGLESS half of Gate_ShippedRosterStillExercisesBothArms (ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp:2275) once Ruling 3 forbids any registered row being flagless?
values.Context: The unit is a roster ANTI-VACUITY guard: it asserts uFlaggedRows > 0 and uFlaglessRows > 0 over the shipped roster, then pins the two named fixtures individually (Vesper flagged at :2307, Rambler flagless at :2310). Its entire flagless premise is what ZM-D-196 Ruling 3 retires. Its own failure message instructs a future implementer to "point the flagless one at a row that really has no flag" — which ZM-D-208 §2.2 forbids in bold ("Do NOT keep some row flagless to preserve the phase"). So the file's own guidance becomes unsatisfiable, and the two options are the same two ruling §2.2 already weighed for phase 8. This is the ONLY thing blocking ZM-23; the other two Gate_* units are mechanical under ruling §2.1's own words. Note this is a coverage judgement, not a mechanical fix, which is why neither the worker nor the orchestrator made it.
values.Best guess taken: Apply ruling §2.2's disposition unchanged: keep the FLAGGED half (uFlaggedRows > 0 plus the Vesper fixture pin), and RETIRE the flagless half in the file with its reason recorded there, stating that the flagless arm is deliberately fixture-only from here because a flagless registered row IS the farmable-prize state. Then move the anti-vacuity guard to where it now belongs — assert that the hand-built fixture the re-pointed Gate_Flagless* unit uses really does carry ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE, so the fixture cannot silently gain a flag either. That preserves the guard's purpose at the new seam instead of deleting it.

values.Question: Ruling 3 says the flagless arm 'must stay covered by the existing test-only reconfiguration', but that remedy only reaches ONE of the three flagless-arm consumers. What happens to the other two?
values.Context: Flagging both Route 1 trainers (Ruling 3, DecisionLog.md:912) retires ZM_TRAINER_ROUTE1_RAMBLER as the only flagless PRODUCTION row. Three consumers exercise the ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE arm, and they split two ways. ZM_MayTrainerEngage(const ZM_TrainerData&, ...) (ZM_TrainerSightFsm.h:315) takes a ROW, so its units can use a test-local fixture - this is the case the ruling's remedy covers. But ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState takes a ZM_TRAINER_ID (ZM_BattleWriteBack.h:105 and :112 - BOTH overloads are by-id, verified), and ZM_Interactable::ConfigureTrainerSight(ZM_TRAINER_ID) likewise. No hand-built row can reach either. Once every registered row is flagged the only flagless ids are UNREGISTERED ones, which are a total silent no-op and therefore cannot exercise 'pays money but writes no flag'. Affected coverage: ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099 TrainerReward_UnflaggedRowStillPaysAndWritesNoFlag (3 assertions) and phase (8) of ZM_AutoTests_TrainerSight.cpp (:140, :3024).
values.Best guess taken: Option (a): add a by-ROW overload ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool) and re-point ZM_Tests_Party.cpp at it, keeping the coverage at the cost of a little production surface. Option (b) - retire the unit and phase 8 with a recorded reason - is cheaper but deletes the only end-to-end proof that the NONE arm pays and does not raise, and ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE remains live production code. Note also that Ruling 3's own reasoning is slightly off on mechanism: ZM_BattleWriteBack.h:101-104 records that a second win credits the money AGAIN ('pay once' is a caller-side gate), so the flag does not stop farming by itself - it stops it because ZM_MayTrainerEngage refuses to raise a defeated flagged trainer. The flag's value is real but is delivered through the sight FSM, not the payout helper.
values.Resolution: RULED: option (a), extended to name phase 8's disposition -- (a) as filed covers ZM_Tests_Party.cpp only and is silent on the third consumer, which is where the implementer would otherwise hit the same wall. THREE PARTS. (1) Add the by-ROW primitive ZM_ApplyTrainerResultToGameState(ZM_GameState&, const ZM_TrainerData&, ZM_SIDE, bool) and re-point ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099 at it. This is an EXTRACTION, not new logic: the by-id function already resolves the row at ZM_BattleWriteBack.cpp:133 and works purely from it thereafter, so by-id becomes classify + ZM_IsRegisteredTrainer + resolve + forward, mirroring how the ZM_BattleDirectorCore overload already forwards. Coverage is strengthened, not merely preserved -- a hand-built row cannot drift when content changes. (2) RETIRE phase 8 of ZM_AutoTests_TrainerSight.cpp, with the reason recorded IN THE TEST FILE: its precondition is a flagless REGISTERED trainer row, and Ruling 3 makes that state deliberately unreachable, so the phase would be proving the behaviour of a configuration production can no longer produce. Do NOT keep some row flagless to preserve the phase -- that is the farmable-prize state Ruling 3 exists to forbid, and preserving a test by preserving the defect it warns about is the wrong trade. (3) Do NOT give ZM_Interactable::ConfigureTrainerSight a by-row overload. It stores m_eTrainerId and re-derives it in OnStart from the serialized NPC row (the deliberate zero-byte route); a by-row configure would need somewhere to put a row outside the registry and would fight that design. WHAT SURVIVES: ZM_MayTrainerEngage's flagless/latch arm by row in ZM_Tests_IntroBeat.cpp:176 with an anti-vacuity arm; the FSM latch in ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp; the write-back NONE arm by row in ZM_Tests_Party.cpp. WHAT IS GENUINELY LOST: the live-component end-to-end proof that a flagless row pays and does not raise. That is a real cost, recorded rather than waved away. ALSO CARRY FORWARD the question's correction to Ruling 3's stated mechanism: the flag does NOT stop farming through the payout helper -- ZM_BattleWriteBack.h:101-104 records that a second win credits the money AGAIN, since 'pay once' is a caller-side gate -- it stops it because ZM_MayTrainerEngage refuses to raise a defeated flagged trainer. The flag's value is real but is delivered through the sight FSM, not the payout helper.

values.Question: How should the NPC greybox appearance palette gain headroom? It has ZERO free appearances, so no new NPC of any kind can be authored until this is ruled on.
values.Context: ZM_GetHumanPaletteColour is 0.45*outfit.primary + 0.25*outfit.accent + 0.30*hair and reads NEITHER skin tone, build, attachment NOR hair style. The usable space is therefore 6 non-themed outfits x 6 non-DYED hairs = 36 cells. Npc_AuthoredAppearancesAreMutuallyDistinct requires 0.15 separation between every pair of NPC rows naming different ids; Npc_EveryAuthoredRowClearsTheBlockoutFallbackGrey adds 0.15 from (0.52,0.55,0.60). Of the 15 existing ZM_HUMAN_IDs outside the 7-row cast, ZERO clear the floor - the best is TRAINER_ANGLER at 0.1350. Exactly ONE cell in the whole space is free (TRAVELER+BLONDE, rgb 0.4145/0.3450/0.2250, nearest neighbour the Warden at 0.1594) and NO ZM_HUMAN_ID stands in it, so even a new ZM_HumanData row could supply only ONE of the two appearances ZM-23 needs. Recomputed independently by the orchestrator from the source tables and corroborated three ways: the worker's analysis, the orchestrator's own script, and Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Shortfalls.md, which already records TRAINER_RANGER at 0.0873 from the Villager and predates this ticket.
values.Best guess taken: Option C - append an outfit slot (e.g. ZM_HUMAN_OUTFIT_FORAGER) and/or a hair colour. Both enums are append-only and save-stable, a new slot adds a whole row/column of cells, and it moves NO existing NPC colour by a single float. The alternatives are worse: (A) new ZM_HumanData rows cannot work alone, only one free cell exists; (B) widening the palette basis to read skin/build/attachment moves EVERY existing colour, redding ZM_AutoTests_RivalVesper's material scan and invalidating every value quoted in ZM_HumanData.cpp and Shortfalls.md; (D) re-scoping the invariant to rows that can share a frame needs a scene column on ZM_NpcData that does not exist. This is a CONTENT decision (new authored colours) and the agent loop declined to take it unilaterally.
values.Resolution: RULED: option C. Append an outfit slot and/or a hair colour to gain headroom for R1-5. Both enums are APPEND-only and save-stable, a new outfit adds a row of 6 candidate cells and a new hair colour a column of 6, and no existing NPC colour moves by a single float - so no committed scene, material scan or quoted value is disturbed. Rejected: (A) new ZM_HumanData rows cannot work alone, only one cell (TRAVELER+BLONDE) is free and R1-5 needs two; (B) widening the palette basis to read skin/build/attachment moves EVERY existing colour, redding ZM_AutoTests_RivalVesper's material scan and invalidating every value quoted in ZM_HumanData.cpp and Shortfalls.md, and it deepens the proxy's entanglement with appearance rather than fixing it; (D) is CORRECT but needs a scene column on ZM_NpcData that does not exist. Two caveats the implementer must carry. FIRST, appending a slot yields CANDIDATE cells, not usable ones: the new outfit's primary and accent must be chosen so every resulting blend clears the 0.15 floor against all existing rows and against the blockout grey (0.52,0.55,0.60). Report the achieved separations rather than asserting them. SECOND, this is a REFILL, not a fix - 6 cells covers R1-5's two and little else. The structural fix is filed as ZM-68 (option D, scene-aware distinctness, S9) and related to ZM-31. Lowering the 0.15 floor was considered and REJECTED: it is the same shape as widening a sight cone to fit a badly-placed anchor, and this codebase's own rule is to move the anchor.

values.Gap: ZM_GroundItemPropModel is total over all nine ZM_ITEM_CATEGORY values, but only ZM_ITEM_CATEGORY_BALL has its own model: MEDICINE, BATTLE, HELD, BERRY, EVO, TM, KEY and FIELD all present ZM_PROP_ITEM_PHIAL. A future TM or key-item ground prop would look like medicine. The switch in ZM_GroundItem.cpp lists every category explicitly so the arm to add is obvious; the fix is one ZM_PropData roster row plus one switch arm. Belongs with S11 drop tuning rather than with ZM-67.

The survey was done at FILE granularity and records that "the FSM latch in ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp" survives. That is true of the Latch_* units and FALSE of three Gate_* units in the same file, which pin the flagless arm of ZM_MayTrainerEngage against the Rambler's ROSTER row rather than a hand-built one: Gate_FlaglessRowKeysOnTheSessionLatchAndIgnoresTheFlag (fixture :2163, reds at :2177 and :2179), Gate_ShippedRosterStillExercisesBothArms (reds at :2300 and :2310), and Gate_PartylessPlayerIsClosedOnBothArms (flagless fixture :2222 — stays GREEN while its stated purpose and its "the FLAGLESS rambler" label silently stop holding). The specific miss is that a BY-ROW helper can still be pinned against a ROSTER row; "the helper takes a row" reads as "hand-built fixture, therefore safe" when it is not. The same survey made the correct call on ZM_Tests_Party.cpp:1099 and on phase 8, so the method is sound and only the granularity is wrong.
values.Filed as: ZM-23 (blocked a second time on this)

values.Area: Zenithmon / the story-flag registry has a SECOND pinned site that nothing documents
values.Gap: Appending any ZM_STORY_FLAG_ID necessarily edits Games/Zenithmon/Tests/ZM_Tests_StoryFlags.cpp, which holds TWO deliberately-literal pins: Registry_ShippedIndicesAreFrozenAndRivalOneIsSix asserts ZM_STORY_FLAG_COUNT == 7u (:343) and ZM_STORY_FLAG_NONE == 7u (:346), and Codec_EnumValueIsTheWireBitIndex requires the hand-spelled 7-row axEXPECTED_WIRE_BITS table (:78-89) to name EVERY registered flag. Both are correct and intentional - the point is that an append cannot pass silently. The gap is that this is nowhere documented as a pin site: Docs/SaveFormat.md:263-268 states the append-only rule without naming the file that ENFORCES it, and ZM_StoryFlags.h's own header comment tells you to add a flag here rather than leaving a numeric gap, without saying what else must move. The practical consequence is that a ticket scoped to add a story flag will be filed with a file list that omits the one file the change cannot avoid, which is exactly what happened on ZM-23's fix-forward attempt: the worker prompt instructed 'check whether any unit pins ZM_STORY_FLAG_COUNT and update it if so' while the exhaustive file list omitted the only file that pins it, so the two instructions could not both be obeyed and the worker correctly stopped without editing anything.

values.Area: Zenithmon / NPC appearance palette + the ratchet that guards it
values.Gap: Npc_AuthoredAppearancesAreMutuallyDistinct ratchets on ZM_NPC_COUNT but NOTHING asserts how much headroom is left. The palette space is 36 cells (outfit x hairColour - the blend reads neither skin, build, attachment nor hair style); the 7 authored rows plus the blockout grey have consumed all of it, leaving exactly one free cell that no ZM_HUMAN_ID occupies. The exhaustion happened when Aster took the cast to 7, and nothing went red then - it surfaced three slices later as ZM-23, an IMPOSSIBLE ticket, after a full opus worker dispatch. The general rule: a ratchet on a FINITE RESOURCE that only asserts the current rows are valid cannot report that the next row has nowhere to go, so it always fails at the slice that NEEDS the resource rather than the slice that CONSUMED it.

OPEN DEFECT: replacing the body of a page that ALREADY has content does not land. The client emits a correct ~370-byte append update, the realtime server receives all 376 bytes on the wire, and Yjs integrates it into a ~19-byte no-op with no pending structs - the new blocks simply never appear. Writing to an EMPTY page works every time (74/74 pages created and verified). Reproduced with and without a second client connected, with and without the server touching root types through the second Yjs module copy, and against both a single delete-then-insert and an append-then-delete. NOT root-caused. Mitigated, not fixed: the write is two-phase (append, verify the appended state persisted, only then drop the superseded blocks), so a failed update leaves the page on its PREVIOUS revision and reports verified:false, instead of leaving it blank. Consequence today: the initial mirror is correct and idempotent, but a doc that changes in the repo will report `updated ... verified:false` and the page will keep the old text until this is fixed. Suspect the dual Yjs module instance the server prints on every boot ('Yjs was already imported'). — RESOLVED 2026-08-16. Root cause: TWO copies of Yjs in the realtime server process. y-websocket/bin/utils is CJS and require()s yjs/dist/yjs.cjs; every module we wrote imported yjs/dist/yjs.mjs. bindState seeded a y-websocket doc with the ESM copy, so the store held ESM Items — and an appended item does not carry its parent on the wire, so Yjs recovers it from its left neighbour via `this.left.constructor === Item` (Item.getMissing). Across two copies that identity check is false, parent stayed null, and Item.integrate fell through to `new GC(...)`: the insert was integrated as GARBAGE, silently. Empty pages were unaffected because the first item in a fragment carries its parent name inline; deletes were unaffected because a delete set is applied by id — which is why the naive single-transaction delete+insert blanked pages instead. It only ever reproduced UNBUNDLED (tsx, i.e. dev and the Playwright fleet); esbuild collapsed both importers onto one copy, so the deployed container never had it. Fix: server code takes Yjs from packages/realtime/src/server/yjs.ts (which require()s it, the way y-websocket does), ws-server.ts refuses to boot on a mismatch, and eslint bans the bare import under src/server/. Covered by apps/notion/e2e/docs-sync.spec.ts ("a page that already has a body is replaced, not left on its old revision") and packages/realtime/src/server/yjs.test.ts. The two-phase write is KEPT — it is what stopped this from blanking pages.

values.Suggestion: Give the Engine category a `decisionLog` in zagent.project.json, or make the project-level decisionLog a fallback for categories that declare none.
values.Friction: ZEN-6's DoD item 4 read 'the headless publish guard is removed, and the reasoning is recorded in the decision log' -- and the claim payload came back with `decisionLog: null` and `decisionIdPrefix: null`, because only the Zenithmon and DevilsPlayground categories declare one. So an Engine ticket that asks for a recorded ruling has no repo-local decision log to record it in, and `zagent decide --ticket ZEN-6` writes the board's Decisions database only. That matters more than it sounds: I3 tells every tick to GREP the decision log for the rulings that govern its subject, and a loop worker has no shell and no network -- it reads the file off disk. An engine ruling recorded only on the board is invisible to exactly the audience I3 exists to serve, and ZEN-6's ruling is one every future scene-authoring ticket needs (it is what makes `needs-gpu` wrong for scene re-authoring). I worked around it by narrating the Zenithmon-visible half into Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md, which is where a ZM tick greps -- but that is the wrong home for an ENGINE decision and it only reaches ZM. Options: (a) declare a decisionLog for Engine, e.g. Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md with prefix ZEN-D-; (b) let a category with no decisionLog inherit a project-level one; (c) at minimum, have `zagent decide` WARN when the ticket's category declares no decisionLog, so the tick notices instead of silently getting a board-only row. Right now the omission is silent -- `decide` returns exit 0 and says 'Wrote a row to Agent - Decisions', which reads exactly like success.

values.Suggestion: Four changes to tick.md, all earned by the 2026-08-25 ZM run: paste a ruling's WHY not just its Decision; grep the SUBJECT not the prose on a reversal ticket; a durable worker finding becomes a DecisionLog entry rather than a work-log line; and retire the docs-sync timeout prose, which now rests on a disproved premise.
values.Friction: (1) PASTE THE WHY. ZM-D-196 Ruling 2 reads 'Explicitly NO gym door'. Read as a decision it forbids ZM-69 outright. Read with its WHY -- 'Gym1 ... declared but unauthored, so a door to an unauthored scene is a permanent black screen' -- it is a PRECONDITION that ZM-69 discharges by authoring Gym1. tick.md already separates a ruling's JUDGEMENT from its SURVEY; this is a third kind, a judgement whose validity is CONDITIONAL on a stated fact, and pasting only the Decision line (which is what 'paste the ruling verbatim' naturally produces) makes a legitimate ticket look like a violation. (2) GREP THE SUBJECT. ZM-69's tripwire table found 4 of 8 sites. The gap has a clean cause: I enumerated files that MENTION 'gym door', and ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry.cpp never uses that phrase -- it says 'the Gym'. The sites that matter ASSERT THE ABSENCE and name the SYMBOL (ZM_SCENE_GYM1, ZM_IsSceneRegisteredForLoad). Step 5's file-list rule currently says 'start from the DoD's nouns and follow them into the repo'; nouns are prose. For a ticket that reverses a recorded assertion the survey pattern must be the identifier. (3) DURABLE FINDINGS NEED A HOME. ZM-28's worker found that appending a move is never inert -- ZM_Learnsets.cpp:52 and ZM_SpeciesData.cpp:555 both DERIVE from the whole move table by scanning it, which no blast-radius grep can find. Seven more gym reward moves remain, so it recurs seven times. I3 tells every tick to GREP the DecisionLog for governing rulings, but no step ever CREATES one from a discovery; step 8's 'Deviations / follow-ups' is a work-log row on a closing ticket that the next worker never reads. One sentence in step 8 fixes it, and the mechanism (zagent decide) already exists. (4) RETIRE THE DOCS-SYNC PROSE. Step 7's 'timed out -- the mirror is one commit behind is a legal and expected work-log outcome', the mandatory `timeout 120` wrapper and the Bash(timeout *) allowed-tools entry all rest on the belief that docs sync hangs and has never completed. It does not: the previous board's 05408ef root-caused it to a WebSocket per page for all 597 pages including unchanged ones, and it now exits 0 in 9 seconds. The machinery and the paragraph should go.

values.Suggestion: zagent claim should archive an existing .zagent/run/<KEY>/ to <KEY>.prev/ so a stale GREEN gate verdict cannot be sitting there when a tick starts.
values.Friction: Claiming ZM-28 on 2026-08-25 freshly wrote ticket.json, body.md and drift.txt and left in place, from an earlier attempt on the same key: a tick_gates.json reading state=complete, exitCode=0, verdict='all gates green' at a headSha of a DIFFERENT commit, plus a gates.json whose recorded changed-set was ['Tools/tick_gates.ps1'] -- an unrelated diff -- plus gates.log, gates.prev.log and three gate_*.ps1 scratch scripts. The only thing between that and a tick that skips its gates is a PROSE rule ('if headSha does not match current HEAD, treat it as absent'), which is exactly the shape this repo keeps naming as the defect: a rule in prose standing in front of a check. Get-RecordedGateSelection (ZagentClient.psm1:727) returns the raw file with no headSha, no timestamp and no comparison. The gates.json half is largely self-defending, because the board re-derives the gate LIST from the CURRENT changed set and a mismatch fails -- so it is only invisible when the list is identical, in which case running those gates was right anyway. The tick_gates.json half is defended by nothing mechanical. FIX: make the CLAIM the boundary of an attempt. Archiving to <KEY>.prev/ keeps I6 forensics while making a stale artifact impossible, and it is cheaper and stronger than adding a `zagent verdict` subcommand that the protocol would then have to remember to call.

values.Suggestion: Write zagent's exit code to .zagent/last.exit on every exit path, so the protocol's most-broken rule becomes a file read like every other rule.
values.Friction: tick.md spends ~40 lines and three measured war stories on 'NEVER PIPE OR SUFFIX A CALL WHOSE EXIT CODE YOU INTEND TO READ', and it is still the most-broken rule in the protocol. It broke twice more on 2026-08-25: I ran `zagent check ZM-70 2>&1 | head -20; echo EXIT=$?` and read 0 when the real code was 5, within the hour of reading the warning; and the harness's own completion notification reported exit 0 for a tick_gates run that exited 10 (MEASURED: a pin needs bumping) -- branching on that commits a stale baseline. The asymmetry is the whole point: EVERY other value the protocol says to read from a file IS on disk (ticket.json, body.md, drift.txt, gates.json, tick_gates.json) precisely because pipes corrupt them, and the exit code -- the single most-warned-about value -- is reachable ONLY through the channel the protocol says never to trust. .zagent/last.json carries the ticket payload and no exit code; nothing writes a last.exit. tick_gates.ps1 already solved this for itself with tick_gates.json, which is why its verdict survived while the shell's did not. FIX: zagent.ps1 ends in `exit $result.exitCode` (:356) with 8 earlier exit paths (:82,:91,:125,:129,:133,:148,:181,:223). Wrap them in one Exit-Zagent function that writes the code to .zagent/last.exit and then exits, and assert it in Test-ZagentClient.ps1. Two lines of real change, and it deletes the entire error class rather than warning about it -- which matters because the protocol's own history says the warning does not hold.

values.Suggestion: doc_lint needs a check that reconciles AssetManifest.md's roster arithmetic and generator version stamps against the headers. C1 cannot be widened to cover them.
values.Friction: ZM-67 moved ZM_PROP_COUNT 25 -> 28 and uZM_PROPGEN_VERSION 1 -> 2, and five claims across AssetManifest.md and TestPlan.md went stale with every gate green -- a human reviewer found them. AssetManifest.md has now been added to C1's file list (it was in NO doc_lint file list at all, so it had zero coverage), but that does not close the class, and it is worth being explicit about why rather than assuming it did. C1's regexes match `N tests passing|registered|in the suite|in batch` and `N/M tests`, and its CEILING is the ZENITH_AUTOMATED_TEST_REGISTER count. The stale claims are `Family total: 25 props x 4 = 100 files`, `uZM_PROPGEN_VERSION (currently 1)` and `It ships **8** pure/all-config ZM_Gen units` -- roster arithmetic and version stamps, not test counts, and comparing a unit-count claim against the AUTOMATED registry ceiling would be comparing two different populations. The right shape is a separate check that reads ZM_PROP_COUNT and uZM_PROPGEN_VERSION out of the headers and asserts the doc's stated numbers match, the way C7 already does for the LIVE PIN block against unit_baselines.json.

values.Suggestion: tick.md step 5 should say: a Definition of Done that asks for BEFORE evidence ORDERS your dispatches -- the harness that produces the evidence must land, and be run, before the change it measures.
values.Friction: ZM-67's DoD ends 'Before/after captures of all three props recorded in the work log, so the visual sign-off has something to judge', and it is human-gate, so that evidence IS the deliverable. No camera-on-the-props harness existed. A BEFORE image can therefore only come from a tree that has the harness and NOT the change -- which one worker dispatch cannot produce, since a single worker authors both at once. Step 5 reads as one-dispatch-per-ticket and never warns that evidence-producing DoD items constrain authoring ORDER; a loop following it literally lands both together, captures only an AFTER, and silently destroys what the human gate exists for. This is the same shape step 6.2 already documents for PINS in the ZM-65 nine-step order (the freeze goes BETWEEN the two identical boots) -- the lesson was learned for measurements and never generalised to evidence. ZM-67 was run as stage 1 (harness only, appearance frozen) then stage 2 (the visual work).

values.Suggestion: `tick_gates.ps1 -Phase measure` should report the gate lines it deferred, and should print the registry count as well as the unit pin.
values.Friction: Two separate gaps in one phase. (1) The measure phase wrote `verdict: "all gates green"` with `skipped: []` having run build+unit but NOT `zenith test` or `doc_lint` -- 2 of the 4 Zenithmon lines. That is correct behaviour (rule 3 measures first) but tick.md documents `skipped` as 'the gate lines that never ran' and instructs you to 'read skipped before concluding anything about what was verified'. Follow that literally at measure and you conclude a subset run was a full run. Listing deferred lines in `skipped` with reason 'deferred to verify phase' would make the field's name true again. (2) The LIVE PIN block carries TWO measured numbers and doc_lint C7 asserts both, but measure only produces one -- the registry count comes from `zenith test`, which runs in verify, AFTER the narration it feeds must be written. A phase that says 'Edit Tools/unit_baselines.json (and any Status.md narration) NOW' should hand you every number that narration needs.

values.Suggestion: Fix or retire `zagent docs sync`. It has now hung on FOUR consecutive ticks and has never once completed.
values.Friction: tick.md step 7 mandates `timeout 120 zagent docs sync --json` and documents three prior hangs (300s, 120s, 120s), stating it 'has never once completed'. ZM-67 is the fourth: killed at 120s, zero-byte log, exit 143. The timeout mitigation works and the tick correctly continued -- but a mandated step with a 0/4 success rate is not a step, it is a ritual, and it costs two minutes of every tick that touches a doc. Either fix the WebSocket path it depends on or drop it from the mandated flow and make the mirror an explicit human-run command.
values.Resolution: FIXED in the previous board 05408ef, and the premise was wrong in a way worth recording. docs sync was never hanging and had never failed to complete its WORK: it opened a WebSocket session for EVERY page (199 on this checkout, 597 across the three projects that map to it), including every page already identical to its source, at a handshake plus 2x DEFAULT_SETTLE_MS each and two sessions per replace. A no-op sync therefore ran about ten minutes and every caller's timeout killed it around page 40 of 199, discarding the --json report (emitted at the end) and leaving a zero-byte log. That is exactly why the mirror always looked CURRENT for docs sorting early (Status, DecisionLog) and never for Conventions -- the pages were being written correctly the whole time. syncPage now answers the no-write case from the persisted row with no socket, using the same decideWrite predicate the live path applies, and takes that path ONLY for a clean 'unchanged' (a CONFLICT and --force both still open the session). Measured on this checkout: five consecutive timeouts at 120-300s became exit 0 in 9 SECONDS. Write path re-verified by editing one doc: updated 2, verified true, on exactly the two pages the change touched, 595 skipped. Consequence for the protocol: tick.md step 7's 'timed out -- the mirror is one commit behind is a legal and expected work-log outcome' rests on a false premise and should be retired along with the timeout wrapper it justifies.

values.Suggestion: Add a non-tools (_False) build line to each category's gate list, copied verbatim from the CI step that already exists.
values.Friction: 0 of the 15 gate lines in zagent.project.json name a _False config -- every one is --headless, i.e. Null_vs2022_Debug_Win64_True with ToolsEnabled ON. So no gate can compile anything under the #else of #ifdef ZENITH_TOOLS. ZM-67 added exactly that (an ZM_EnsurePropBaked stub plus a newly-unconditional include) and the whole gate list was structurally incapable of building it; a reviewer had to point it out and the orchestrator ran the build by hand. CI DOES have such a step (zm-tests.yml:104-122 builds Zenithmon as D3D12_vs2022_Debug_Win64_False, comment: '_False omits editor/tools'), but branching is direct and push is false, so CI never runs before the commit lands on master -- the break would surface later on a commit several tickets deep. CLAUDE.md already requires gate lines be copied VERBATIM from CI and names zagent.project.json a downstream consumer in the same commit; CI grew this step and the gate list did not. Same shape as the recorded backend-rot lesson, rotated onto the tools axis.

values.Suggestion: For `zagent check` specifically, let the DURABLE contract verdict (exit 4) win over the TRANSIENT I5 repo-busy verdict (exit 5). Keep 5 winning for claim/next, where the lock is the whole point.
values.Friction: With a ticket in flight, `zagent check` returned exit 5 for an epic (ZM-17), a needs-human ticket (ZM-30) and an out-of-stage ticket (ZM-45) alike. tick.md step 2 states an EPIC comes back exit 4 from check 'on the queue AND by name' -- true only when the repo is idle. check is the one verb documented as writes-nothing/claims-nothing, i.e. the planning tool meant to be safe while something is in flight, which is exactly when it is least informative. And tick.md's standing rule is 'Exit codes are the interface -- branch on them, not on stdout prose', so a caller obeying it cannot distinguish 'this is an epic and never claimable' from 'busy, try later'. The CONTRACT line is still printed, so only the machine-readable half is lost.

values.Suggestion: At file time, grep the repo for the identifiers a Definition of Done proposes to change and warn when hits land outside the ticket's declared file list.
values.Friction: zagent already refuses a DoD naming a protectedPath. ZM-23 failed for the adjacent reason: a DoD that is reachable but whose blast radius exceeds the declared list. One rg for ZM_TRAINER_ROUTE1_RAMBLER would have surfaced Tests/ZM_Tests_TrainerSightFsm.cpp before the claim, the one-ticket-per-repo lock slot and two opus worker dispatches. Raised by the ZM-23 worker itself.

values.Suggestion: Preserve the FULL text of every Definition-of-Done checkbox in the claim payload, including continuation lines. Until then, tick.md step 5 must say explicitly: inline the DoD from body.md, never from the definitionOfDone array.
values.Friction: The payload's definitionOfDone[].text truncates each checkbox at its first newline. On ZM-23 that deletes the entire substance of two items: item 1 loses 'not bumped to a larger count ... caught as a DOUBLE CLAIM on ZM_TRAINER_RIVAL_VESPER, proven by an anti-vacuity arm' (the whole point of the ticket), and item 3 loses 'are REPORTED from the shipped tables rather than asserted' (the clause preventing a self-referential guard). I3 makes the DoD the worker's verbatim specification, and the array is the obvious thing to inline because it is structured and already in the payload. A tick that does so ships a mutilated spec, and the worker cannot tell, having no shell and no board. It also weakens finish --status Done's unticked-box refusal, which reads the same truncated text.
values.Resolution: Both halves are now closed. The board half landed in the previous board's 9d03869 (2026-08-25): parseTicket carries continuation lines, so definitionOfDone[].text is no longer truncated at the first newline -- verified against ZM-23, the ticket that exposed it. The tick.md half is stated and STILL STANDS, but on a reason that never depended on the bug: the array holds the checkboxes and never the prose that qualifies them, and ZM-23's body carried two load-bearing instructions OUTSIDE any checkbox. So 'inline from body.md, never from the array' is a rule about what the array IS, not a workaround. The worked example of what the truncation cost -- including that the reachability scan could not see a protectedPath written on a continuation line -- moved to Docs/TickProtocolHistory.md, since it is now history rather than a live hazard. Zenith e411b451.

values.Suggestion: AUDIT WRAP-UP 2026-08-24: what landed in the Zenith checkout, and the four halves that are BOARD-SIDE and still open. Landed here across ae475483 (tick.md + settings.json) and 39b24437 (Tools/zagent, +12 assertions, 158 total, smoked against the real board): the refused-claim rollback, the drift resolver's category ranking, the finish --status Done DoD refusal, client UTF-8 output, TaskStop and Bash(timeout *) in allowed-tools, rulings added to I3's inline list, the windowed-authoring correction plus a nine-step needs-gpu runbook, step 6's total ordering, step 7's third arm, the three orchestrator-owned measurements, reconciliation against code rather than comments, a file-list derivation rule, and I2 widened to distrust 'it cannot be done' as well as 'it works'. STILL BOARD-SIDE, in priority order: (1) zagent claim should VALIDATE BEFORE IT MUTATES -- the client now rolls a refused claim back, but that is a bandage over a transaction that writes then checks, and 'zagent check' already evaluates needsHuman and EPIC without writing, so the same gate can run before the transaction; (2) 'zagent docs sync' HANGS -- four ticks, four hangs, four zero-byte logs, most recently exit 143 on ZM-65 -- and wants a --timeout-seconds flag so the bounded call stays a bare zagent invocation rather than needing a generic process wrapper on the allowlist; (3) review.required should gain a third OR term, 'the ticket's subject matter is governed by a recorded decision', computable from the decisionLog that zagent.project.json already declares -- ZM-23 was reviewed only by the luck of MEDIUM sitting in reviewOn, and that review is the only thing that caught it violating ZM-D-203 Ruling 3; (4) the claim payload could resolve candidate rulings into .zagent/run/<KEY>/rulings.md the way it already writes drift.txt, which turns I3's new rulings clause from prose into a file the orchestrator cannot fail to see. Also note guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes looks mis-tiered against measurement: the one observed MODERATE run used 94 percent of its 30-minute budget while both COMPLEX runs used about 16 percent of 90.

values.Suggestion: The reviewer caught the ORCHESTRATOR, not the worker, and the protocol does not expect that. ZM-65's review returned three BLOCKING findings and all three were in material the orchestrator wrote after the gates: a stale banner still announcing a row unfrozen 50 lines above the frozen row; a new DecisionLog entry describing a source-only commit that 'moves no scene byte' in a commit that re-authored a tracked binary; and a FABRICATED causal explanation committed to two living docs (the claim that other regions' larger 12 m seam deltas arise because those pairs 'differ in flatten containment' - the terrain recipe inverts it: all three comparison pairs are identically contained, and the one pair that differs moved the LEAST). Every control points at the worker - I1 'you own the gate, the worker only authors', I2 never trust the worker, step 6.3 'review the diff' - while the orchestrator's edits are the ones no control covers: the worker has exited, gates cannot read prose, and doc_lint's seven checks never test whether a comment's assertion matches the line beneath it. And the orchestrator writes the highest-leverage text in the repo: the pin narration, the committed-asset hashes, the decision-log entry that becomes the binding record. FIX: say in step 6.3 that the review covers the WHOLE diff including orchestrator edits, and extend the existing 'grep the doc for the value you just changed' rule to every file a freeze touches, source comments included.

Also adds the two habits that catch most of it earlier -- grep every file a freeze touched for the value just changed, and treat an invented MECHANISM as a claim needing a source.

values.Suggestion: The drift resolver names the WRONG GAME's file whenever two games share a filename, and it is deterministic rather than occasional. Measured across four ZM tickets: Roadmap.md and Board.md exist only under Games/Zenithmon, so the resolver suggests the Zenithmon path and is right BY LUCK; Status.md and Shortfalls.md exist under BOTH Zenithmon and DevilsPlayground, and the resolver suggested the DevilsPlayground path every time (ZM-23, ZM-30 x2). It walks in path order and takes the first match, and DevilsPlayground sorts before Zenithmon. It then presents that single pick as an answer - 'a file of that name is at X' - with no sign a second candidate exists, while tick.md step 5 tells the orchestrator to reconcile drift.txt and correct the worker prompt from it. So it is right exactly when there is no ambiguity and wrong exactly when the hint would have carried information. FIX: rank candidates by the ticket's category paths prefix, and when more than one survives print them ALL - a list reads as a question, one path reads as an answer.

values.Suggestion: Two allowed-tools gaps in .claude/commands/tick.md that stall an unattended loop. (1) Step 5 mandates TaskStop for the wedged-worker guardrail ('If elapsed wall-clock exceeds guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes, stop the agent (TaskStop)') but TaskStop is NOT in the frontmatter allowed-tools list - so the one enforcement action for that guardrail needs a tool the skill never granted. Measured near-miss: ZM-65's worker ran 28.1 min against a 30 min MODERATE cap. The protocol's own escape hatch ('if you can see the worker still producing tool calls') is unusable because background dispatch surfaces no progress signal and tailing the subagent transcript is forbidden. (2) Step 7 mandates 'timeout 120 zagent docs sync --json' but the permission entries are Bash(zagent:*) and Bash(zagent *), both anchored on zagent as the FIRST token - 'timeout 120 zagent ...' matches neither. The fix for the hang moved the command out from under its own permission entry, at the one step that stalls AFTER the commit lands and BEFORE finish. Better fix: give 'zagent docs sync' a --timeout-seconds flag so the bounded call stays a bare zagent invocation. Note the hang itself reproduced again on ZM-65: exit 143, zero-byte log - four ticks, four hangs.

values.Suggestion: tick.md step 7 branches on GATE COLOUR ONLY, so a green partial reaches Done with the DoD unmet.
