values.Suggestion: CRITICAL: zagent claim MUTATES BEFORE IT VALIDATES. A targeted claim on a needs-human ticket (reproduced on ZM-64) writes 'status: To Do -> In Progress' and 'assignee: none -> the agent', THEN returns exit 4 refusing it. The ticket is left assigned, In Progress, and holding the I5 one-ticket-per-repo lock - a following 'zagent next' returned exit 5 (repo busy). So one /tick <needs-human-key> deadlocks the whole queue for every project this checkout serves, and tick.md step 2 ('targeted exit 4: report the error and change nothing') guarantees it stays deadlocked. needs-human's stated contract is 'never claimed, by the queue or by name' - it IS claimed by name and only refused after. FIX: run the needsHuman/EPIC gate before the transaction (zagent check already evaluates both without writing), or roll back to previousStatus + clear assignee on contract failure.
values.Friction: (not recorded — filed as a one-line suggestion)

values.Suggestion: The defect is narrower and sharper than the first row implied. Roadmap.md says cross-cutting work is 'scheduled against sprints' - and a CONTINUOUS, always-in-scope sprint is precisely the arrangement under which it is never scheduled and always claimable. So the fix is not to re-home 18 tickets; it is to make the 'Cross-cutting - no stage' sprint non-continuous. A cross-cutting item then gets worked only when someone pulls it into the ACTIVE milestone sprint via zagent sprint add, which is exactly what Roadmap.md describes, and it makes 'only tasks in the current sprint are picked up' true without inventing false milestone homes for genuinely stage-less work. On the evidence, re-homing by content would move about ONE ticket (ZM-63, a live quality failure in shipped content that also blocks ZM-56); ZM-51 and ZM-52 are open questions under ZM-16 and ZM-59 is polish debt under ZM-18, all correctly stage-less. The four enforcement proposals in the original row stand unchanged - they are what makes any of this hold.
values.Friction: CORRECTION to the milestone-ordering row filed minutes earlier in this database. Two things in it were overstated and a human triaging it should have the accurate version. (1) I wrote that the 'Cross-cutting - no stage' sprint holds 18 issues 'all claimable regardless of the active milestone'. The sprint holds 18, but only FOUR are actually claimable today: ZM-63, ZM-51, ZM-52, ZM-59. The rest are needs-human, deferred, blocked, or epics. Separately, the seven tickets showing sprint '(none)' are ALL epics, which are never claimable - so hole A's only real victims were ZM-65 and ZM-66, the two tickets the loop itself filed during S8, both since moved into S8 by hand. Hole A is still real and still self-worsening, but its blast radius today is 2, not 7. (2) I did not account for Roadmap.md's explicit design intent. Roadmap.md states of the cross-cutting epics: 'These four epics carry items the stage plan has never had a home for... These have no stage gate. They are scheduled against sprints and releases on the board, not against S0-S12.' So the cross-cutting EPICS (ZM-14 engine gaps, ZM-15 tech debt, ZM-16 open questions, ZM-17 test infra, ZM-18 visual polish) are deliberate and correct, and re-homing their children into S8-S12 by content would contradict the living doc.
values.Resolution: Done, with one deliberate difference in mechanism worth recording.  The outcome this row argued for is in place: a cross-cutting item is now worked only when somebody pulls it into the ACTIVE milestone sprint with zagent sprint add, which is what Roadmap.md already said should happen. The four enforcement proposals it endorsed from the original row have all shipped (see gqbpgj4s).  It was NOT done by flipping the Cross-cutting sprint to non-continuous. Strict IN_SCOPE_SPRINT reaches the same place from the claim query instead: once a project has a non-continuous ACTIVE stage, a continuous bucket stops qualifying, so the sprint row keeps its honest description of itself and the queue stops honouring it while a stage runs. That preserves the reason continuous was added in the first place - a board with no stage in progress still offers the bucket - which flipping the flag would have destroyed.  Your reading of the evidence held up exactly. Re-homing by content would indeed have moved about one ticket, and the other three are correctly stage-less: doctor now reports all four by key rather than proposing false milestone homes for them.

values.Suggestion: Requested behaviour from the repo owner: one sprint per milestone, the current milestone sprint tracked, ONLY tasks in the current sprint picked up, and the next sprint startable only when every task in the current one is complete. Enforcement, all board-side: (1) the claim query refuses any ticket not in the project ACTIVE sprint - which means retiring both 'sprints are optional' and the continuous/always-in-scope exemption, or reducing the latter to something explicit, rare and audited; (2) zagent create requires --sprint, or defaults it to the ACTIVE sprint, so a ticket that cannot be routed to a milestone fails at FILE time exactly as a missing --complexity already does - this is the hole the loop itself widens every time it files a follow-up; (3) zagent sprint start refuses unless every issue in the current ACTIVE sprint sits in a DONE-category status, naming the ones that do not; (4) zagent doctor grows a row counting claimable tickets outside the ACTIVE sprint, which today would read 18+ and is reported nowhere. Precedent for the shape: zagent board status already exits 1 on Roadmap drift, so the drift-detection habit exists - it just does not cover sprint membership.
values.Friction: Milestone ordering is not enforced, so the queue hands out work from outside the ACTIVE sprint. The mapping itself is right: sprints are one-per-milestone (S8 ACTIVE, S9-S12 PLANNED, matching Roadmap.md S0..S12) and the PLANNED gate works - ZM-45, ZM-46 and ZM-37 all correctly report OUT OF STAGE. What leaks is everything that never enters that gate. HOLE A: a ticket with NO sprint is claimable, and create never assigns one - zagent show prints '(none - claimable, sprints are optional)'. This is self-worsening, because the loop files follow-ups during a milestone and every one lands outside milestone control: ZM-65 and ZM-66, both filed by the loop during S8 today, had no sprint until added by hand, and ZM-17 still shows none. HOLE B: the 'Cross-cutting - no stage' sprint is continuous/always-in-scope and holds 18 issues claimable regardless of the active milestone. Its members are not stage-less chores - ZM-51 (player gender), ZM-52 (LFS question), ZM-59 (NPC palette), ZM-63 (PlayerHome tint) are ordinary feature/bug work that belongs to some milestone. Concretely: with ZM-22 finishing Blocked, ZM-23/R1-5 stays blocked, and the next tick would have claimed ZM-63 - Cross-cutting - while S8 is the active milestone. HOLE C: nothing requires the ACTIVE sprint to be complete before the next is started; S8 stands at 21/81 pts over 14 issues.
values.Resolution: All four enforcement proposals in this row have shipped, board-side, across three commits in the previous board's repo.  (1) The claim query refuses a ticket outside the project ACTIVE sprint. IN_SCOPE_SPRINT is strict now but self-configuring rather than absolute: a project with a non-continuous ACTIVE stage offers that stage ONLY, so both the sprint_id IS NULL and the continuous exemptions stop qualifying, while a board with no stage in progress keeps its previous behaviour unchanged. (17be92f)  (2) zagent create defaults --sprint to the ACTIVE stage, and warns by name when no --parent is set. That closes the hole the loop itself widened every time it filed a follow-up mid-stage. (17be92f)  (3) A stage cannot be completed while its work is unfinished, and the refusal names the tickets that are not done. Since startSprint already refuses a second ACTIVE sprint, completing the current one is the only route to starting the next, which makes this the enforcement point you asked for. --force still carries work to the backlog, because a stage sometimes genuinely ends with scope unlanded; it just has to be deliberate. (17be92f)  (4) zagent doctor grows a queue row per project counting To Do work that is ready and parked outside the ACTIVE stage. It reads 4 on ZM right now: ZM-63, ZM-51, ZM-52 and ZM-59. It counts UNSCHEDULED work apart from work in a later stage, because nothing will ever un-park the first kind, and it goes red only when the queue is ALSO dry, which is the incident it exists to explain. A permanently red check is one nobody reads. (af1873b)

values.Suggestion: Record `move` and `finish` in jira.issue_activity, the way `claim` now does. `updateTicket` was the only writer of that table, so the ticket LIFECYCLE left no per-issue trail at all: a claim wrote nothing (fixed), and moveTicket/finishTicket still write only the org-wide activity feed (recordActivity), which is a different table with a different shape. The helper is already there -- packages/agent/src/board.ts `recordClaim` -- and both call sites already know the from/to status, so this is a few lines each. Until then `zagent history <KEY>` shows a ticket being claimed and never being closed, which reads as an in-flight ticket that nobody finished.
values.Friction: Reconstructing what happened to a ticket means reading the org activity feed and correlating by timestamp, rather than reading the ticket's own history. The gap was invisible for as long as nothing wrote the claim either -- `history` on a freshly claimed ticket said 'No recorded changes', so the whole table looked unused rather than half-used.
values.Resolution: Shipped in the previous board's dc80c1e. `recordTransition` is now the one writer of jira.issue_activity for both status and assignee, and `recordClaim` is a caller of it rather than a parallel implementation; `moveTicket` and `finishTicket` both record their move. `planAgentMove` returns the from-status and from-assignee it had already loaded, so no caller re-reads the row. moveTicket became a transaction where it was a bare UPDATE, so the move and its history row land together. `zagent history <KEY>` now shows To Do -> In Progress -> Done in order, which is asserted as a SEQUENCE (a test that only checked "some row mentions Done" would pass on a trail with the moves backwards).

values.Suggestion: Add --label / --unlabel to `zagent update`, taking the same comma list `create` already accepts. That alone makes `windowed` applicable on discovery, which is when you actually learn a ticket needs a person. Worth considering a second label for the distinct case ZM-56 represents: not "needs a windowed run to PRODUCE the deliverable" (what windowed means today) but "the only branch a headless agent can complete is the destructive one". Those want the same queue filtering and different explanations to whoever picks it up.
values.Friction: Labels can only be set at CREATE time. `zagent create` takes --label, but `zagent update` accepts only --priority/--points/--severity/--repro/--environment/--due and answers "Nothing to update -- pass at least one field" for --label. So a ticket that is DISCOVERED to need a human after filing cannot be protected. That matters because `windowed` is the board's one mechanical guard for unrunnable work -- filtered from the claim query, contract-invalid on a targeted claim -- and it is exactly the guard you want to apply after reading a ticket, not before. Concrete case: ZM-56 is "ZM_InteriorTintPixels_Test passes windowed, or is retired with a recorded reason". It is a requiresGraphics test, so a headless loop cannot run the fix branch and can only verify the RETIRE branch -- an agent handed "fix it or delete it", unable to test a fix, deletes coverage. It carries labels tech-debt,visual and is not marked windowed, so nothing stops the loop claiming it. The protection is prose in tick.md, which is precisely the shape of guard this repo keeps finding does not hold.
values.Resolution: Shipped: `zagent update` takes --label/--unlabel (flags.ts COMMAND_FLAGS.update), so a marker can be applied AFTER filing, which is when you learn one is needed. The follow-on it asked about also shipped: `windowed` was split into needs-gpu and needs-human (the previous board's migration 0028).

values.Suggestion: Rewrite that DoD line once across the ten tickets to "Every affected game's row bumped in Tools/unit_baselines.json from an OBSERVED run". The CLI cannot edit DoD text (update takes --points/--severity/--priority, not the body), and commenting requires claiming each ticket because of the ownership guard, so ten claims to fix ten sentences is worse than the problem -- this wants a board-side edit or a bulk update command. Longer term the DoD should not name pin SITES at all: it is duplicating a fact that changes, which is the same duplication the manifest refactor removed from the build. "Bump the pinned baseline from an observed run" says everything a worker needs and cannot go stale when the plumbing moves.
values.Friction: TEN open tickets carry a Definition-of-Done line that is now WRONG and points a worker at protected paths: ZM-20, ZM-21, ZM-22, ZM-23, ZM-24, ZM-25, ZM-26, ZM-27, ZM-28, ZM-31 all say some form of "Baseline bumped in Status.md AND zm-tests.yml AND zagent.project.json". Since b6f211d6 the pin has ONE home, Tools/unit_baselines.json, and the workflows and zagent.project.json name the GAME instead of a number. Two of the three sites those DoDs name are protectedPaths, so a worker that follows the inlined DoD literally edits files zagent guard refuses and the ticket Blocks on work that is now a one-line edit to an unprotected file. The DoD is inlined verbatim into the worker prompt by I3, so it competes directly with tick.md step 6, which now carries the correct instruction. Giving a worker two conflicting instructions and hoping it picks the right one is not a contract.
values.Resolution: Shipped: all ten tickets (ZM-20,21,22,23,24,25,26,27,28,31) now read "Every affected game's pinned baseline bumped from an OBSERVED run" and none names a pin site -- verified by reading each body, not by sampling. The enabling capability it said was missing, `zagent update --dod`, exists.

values.Suggestion: Scale the timeout by complexity rather than pinning one number for every ticket: TRIVIAL/SIMPLE keep something tight (10-15 min), MODERATE 30, COMPLEX 60+. The board already knows the complexity -- it is what picks the model -- so this needs no new field. Alternatively make the guardrail a HEARTBEAT rather than a wall-clock cap: kill a worker that has produced no tool call for N minutes, which is what "wedged" actually means, instead of one that is simply doing a large job slowly. A COMPLEX ticket taking 40 minutes of steady tool calls is working; a TRIVIAL one silent for 10 is not.
values.Friction: guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes is 30, and step 5 says to TaskStop the worker past it and treat the ticket as a failed attempt. Observed worker wall-clock this session: ZM-53 109s, ZM-57 793s, ZM-50 517s then 838s, ZM-49 904s then 499s, ZEN-2 2601s then 935s. ZEN-2's first worker ran 43 minutes -- 45 percent over the guardrail -- and produced the chunk-span design that shipped. Killing it at 30 minutes would have destroyed correct work and cost a full re-dispatch, so the orchestrator let it run and the guardrail silently did not apply. A limit that is right to ignore is worse than no limit: it trains the operator to skip the check, and then it is not there on the run that genuinely wedges. Note the routing tiers make this predictable rather than random -- every run over 15 minutes was opus on a COMPLEX ticket, and every sonnet/haiku run finished well inside 30.
values.Resolution: Shipped: guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes is per-complexity, not one number -- {TRIVIAL:15, SIMPLE:15, MODERATE:30, COMPLEX:90}, read at board.ts:1351 as ticketTimeoutMinutes[issue.complexity]. That is the tiering this row asked for (10-15 / 30 / 60+). The heartbeat alternative was not taken.

values.Suggestion: Two options, not exclusive. (1) At file time, warn when the key about to be allocated is already cited in any living doc under the categories' docs dirs -- the board knows the next key and the client already uploads the docs tree for sync, so the check costs one grep and would have caught this exactly. (2) Make the convention explicit in AgentBriefing/CLAUDE.md: never write a ticket key into a doc until the ticket EXISTS, because keys are allocated sequentially and a forward reference is a booby trap that arms itself later. Prefer describing the work ("an engine-side twin, unfiled") over inventing a key for it.
values.Friction: Filing a ticket can silently CAPTURE a phantom forward-reference in the docs, turning a dangling cross-reference into one that resolves to the wrong real ticket. Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Questions.md tagged Q-2026-08-14-001 as [ZM-50 / ZEN-2], meaning "tracked as ZM-50 on the ZM board and ZEN-2 on the engine board". ZEN-2 did not exist -- it was aspirational, and ZEN-3..6 still do not exist. Filing an unrelated engine ticket today allocated key ZEN-2 to it, so that reference now resolves to a terrain-performance ticket that has nothing to do with the wall-clock question. That is strictly worse than the dangling state: a reader who follows it lands somewhere plausible and wrong, and nothing flags it. This is the same species as the dangling ZM-D-177 citation that ZM-53 was filed to fix, with the failure mode upgraded from "leads nowhere" to "leads somewhere false". Tools/doc_lint.ps1 cannot catch it -- its C6 check resolves markdown LINKS, and these are bare bracketed keys in prose.
values.Resolution: Option (1) shipped in Zenith bf6d6707, which this row called the real fix. `zagent create` greps the living-doc dirs for the key it just allocated and warns naming every file:line -- client-side and AFTER the create, because the board would need the 932 KB docs tree uploaded to grep it, and the key the board ACTUALLY allocated beats predicting the next one. Option (2), documenting the convention, was deliberately NOT taken as the close: prose in front of a check is the defect this repo keeps naming. The guard was inert when first written (it read $result.key; the key is under payload) and is now a tested function, Get-CreatedKey. The DANGLING direction this does not cover -- a bare key citing a ticket that never existed -- is filed as ZEN-8.

values.Suggestion: Extend contract validation to scan the Definition of Done (and ideally the Goal) for paths matching the effective protectedPaths union, and fail at FILE time the way a missing --category already does -- refusing only when filing straight into Ready for Agent, warning when filing into To Do, matching the existing behaviour. A DoD line naming .github/**, zagent.project.json or .claude/** is a ticket no agent can finish, and finding that out at claim time wastes a claim, a slot in the one-ticket-per-repo lock, and whatever model time the worker burns before someone notices. If static path detection is too brittle, the cheaper version is a `human-only` label that behaves exactly like `windowed`: filtered from the queue, contract-invalid on a targeted claim.
values.Friction: Two consecutive tickets carried a Definition-of-Done item the loop provably cannot satisfy, and `contractValid` was true for both. ZM-54 requires "a Zenithmon invocation runs in CI" -- that is .github/workflows/doc-lint.yml, protected, so zagent guard refuses it. ZM-50's class requires bumping a pinned unit baseline, which for Zenithmon lives in three files of which .github/workflows/zm-tests.yml and zagent.project.json are both protected. In both cases the loop claimed the ticket, spent time reading the repo, and only then discovered the work was unreachable. Contract validation currently checks routing, category, complexity and risk -- whether the ticket can be ROUTED -- but not whether what it asks for can be DONE by an agent bound by protectedPaths. The board already has the concept and the machinery: `windowed` keeps work that needs a human at a keyboard out of the claim query entirely, and a targeted claim on one fails the contract by name.
values.Resolution: Shipped: contract validation scans the Definition of Done for the effective protectedPaths union and refuses at FILE time (board.ts:1091), so a ticket no agent could finish never costs a claim. The cheaper label alternative it offered was not needed.

values.Suggestion: Give the baseline ONE home that is not protected -- e.g. Tools/unit_baselines.json (or a per-game file next to the game), read by run_unit_gate.ps1, referenced by zm-tests.yml, and named rather than duplicated by zagent.project.json's gate line. Then a count change is a one-file edit the loop can make and the guard permits, while .github/** and zagent.project.json stay protected. That also removes the standing four-site sync hazard the docs already warn about repeatedly -- a stale pin reds a REQUIRED check with zero failing tests, which is the same failure this ticket describes, just triggered by a human forgetting a site instead of by the guard. If a single home is not acceptable, the alternative is to accept the limit explicitly: label such tickets so the claim query filters them out the way it already filters `windowed`, so the loop never claims work it provably cannot finish.
values.Friction: The agent loop can NEVER land a ticket that adds or removes a unit test, and until now nothing said so -- tick.md actively instructed the opposite. The gate asserts `ran == Baseline` EXACTLY, so adding one test reds it with zero failures. Bumping the pin means editing every site that carries it, and for Zenithmon two of the three are PROTECTED: Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md (editable), .github/workflows/zm-tests.yml (protected by .github/**), and zagent.project.json (protected). zagent guard refuses both, so step 6.4 Blocks the ticket however green everything else is. A backend-neutral ENGINE unit is worse -- it moves every game's pin plus Tools/run_unit_gate.ps1's default. tick.md said "the fix is to bump every pinned site in the same commit" and named both protected files, so the protocol told the loop to do the exact thing its own guard would Block it for. That has been corrected to say park-and-file, and to warn against the tempting wrong fix (deleting the worker's tests to buy a green gate, which looks identical to success on the board). But the underlying limit stands, and it is severe: this repo mandates tests with all new code, so most real feature work is permanently out of the loop's reach. Every ticket run so far has been unit-count-neutral by luck of selection, not by design.
values.Resolution: Shipped, at the filename this row proposed: Tools/unit_baselines.json is the single unprotected home. run_unit_gate.ps1 resolves the number by -Game, and the workflows plus zagent.project.json name the GAME rather than duplicating the count -- so bumping a pin is now work the loop can do.

values.Suggestion: Either (a) derive the gate list from the diff: any change touching Zenith/** unions in the Engine category's gates regardless of filing category, which generalises to any shared top-level directory; or (b) require a hard BLOCKS/BLOCKED-BY link between a category ticket and its cross-category twin, so the claim query's existing mechanical blocker check forces the engine-side verification to happen in the right order. (a) is preferable because it needs no human to remember to file the twin. As a stopgap the orchestrator can run the extra category's gates by hand, which is what this run did -- but that is a convention, not a mechanism, and it is exactly the kind of thing that works until the one time nobody does it.
values.Friction: A ticket's gate list is selected by its filing CATEGORY, never by which directories the diff actually touches. ZM-50 is category Zenithmon but edits Zenith/EntityComponent/Components/Zenith_GraphComponent.Tests.inl -- engine-shared code compiled into the Zenith lib that every game links. So the run executed Zenithmon's four gates and never built or tested Combat, and never checked the engine pin (1638). The ticket's own goal text even says "the fix is engine-side - this ticket is filed against the ENGINE board on purpose", so the body and the category disagree and only the category has any mechanical effect. The worker and the independent reviewer both flagged this without being told the other had. Questions.md tags the entry [ZM-50 / ZEN-2], implying an Engine-side twin, but nothing requires ZEN-2 to run, or to run AFTER this commit rather than before it. This is the same shape as the defect ZM-50 itself is about: a shared engine unit rotting invisibly for one game while looking fine for another.
values.Resolution: Shipped as option (a), the one this row called preferable: dispatch.ts gateSelection() calls effectiveGates({changedPaths}), so a diff touching Zenith/** unions in the Engine category gates regardless of filing category. No human has to remember to file a twin.

values.Suggestion: If queueing is meant to be UI-drag-only (CLAUDE.md says "handing work over is a drag, not a command"), then transitions should omit "Ready for Agent" for a ticket the caller does not own, and move should fail with "queueing is done on the board" rather than an abandonment message. If it is not meant to be UI-only, permit To Do -> Ready for Agent without ownership. Either way the advertised transition set and the accepted transition set should agree.
values.Friction: zagent transitions <KEY> lists "Ready for Agent  Queue for the agent" as a legal move from To Do, but zagent move <KEY> "Ready for Agent" then fails exit 5 with "is no longer assigned to the agent - abandoning without writing". It is an ownership guard: the same move succeeds once the agent holds the ticket. Reproduced against BOTH the PowerShell client and the Node client, so it is board-side, not client-side. Two problems: transitions advertises the one move that by definition happens BEFORE ownership exists, and the error text describes abandonment - an unrelated failure mode - so the reader hunts for a lost claim rather than a permissions rule. Found while running /tick end-to-end for the first time; it forced that run into targeted mode instead of queue mode.
values.Resolution: Resolved by removal rather than by either fix proposed: the Ready for Agent lane was retired (migration 0026_retire_ready_for_agent) and To Do is the queue, so the advertised and accepted transition sets no longer disagree about a lane that no longer exists.

values.Suggestion: Give the Engine category a `decisionLog` in zagent.project.json, or make the project-level decisionLog a fallback for categories that declare none.
values.Friction: ZEN-6's DoD item 4 read 'the headless publish guard is removed, and the reasoning is recorded in the decision log' -- and the claim payload came back with `decisionLog: null` and `decisionIdPrefix: null`, because only the Zenithmon and DevilsPlayground categories declare one. So an Engine ticket that asks for a recorded ruling has no repo-local decision log to record it in, and `zagent decide --ticket ZEN-6` writes the board's Decisions database only. That matters more than it sounds: I3 tells every tick to GREP the decision log for the rulings that govern its subject, and a loop worker has no shell and no network -- it reads the file off disk. An engine ruling recorded only on the board is invisible to exactly the audience I3 exists to serve, and ZEN-6's ruling is one every future scene-authoring ticket needs (it is what makes `needs-gpu` wrong for scene re-authoring). I worked around it by narrating the Zenithmon-visible half into Games/Zenithmon/Docs/Status.md, which is where a ZM tick greps -- but that is the wrong home for an ENGINE decision and it only reaches ZM. Options: (a) declare a decisionLog for Engine, e.g. Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md with prefix ZEN-D-; (b) let a category with no decisionLog inherit a project-level one; (c) at minimum, have `zagent decide` WARN when the ticket's category declares no decisionLog, so the tick notices instead of silently getting a board-only row. Right now the omission is silent -- `decide` returns exit 0 and says 'Wrote a row to Agent - Decisions', which reads exactly like success.

values.Suggestion: Four changes to tick.md, all earned by the 2026-08-25 ZM run: paste a ruling's WHY not just its Decision; grep the SUBJECT not the prose on a reversal ticket; a durable worker finding becomes a DecisionLog entry rather than a work-log line; and retire the docs-sync timeout prose, which now rests on a disproved premise.
values.Friction: (1) PASTE THE WHY. ZM-D-196 Ruling 2 reads 'Explicitly NO gym door'. Read as a decision it forbids ZM-69 outright. Read with its WHY -- 'Gym1 ... declared but unauthored, so a door to an unauthored scene is a permanent black screen' -- it is a PRECONDITION that ZM-69 discharges by authoring Gym1. tick.md already separates a ruling's JUDGEMENT from its SURVEY; this is a third kind, a judgement whose validity is CONDITIONAL on a stated fact, and pasting only the Decision line (which is what 'paste the ruling verbatim' naturally produces) makes a legitimate ticket look like a violation. (2) GREP THE SUBJECT. ZM-69's tripwire table found 4 of 8 sites. The gap has a clean cause: I enumerated files that MENTION 'gym door', and ZM_Tests_SceneRegistry.cpp never uses that phrase -- it says 'the Gym'. The sites that matter ASSERT THE ABSENCE and name the SYMBOL (ZM_SCENE_GYM1, ZM_IsSceneRegisteredForLoad). Step 5's file-list rule currently says 'start from the DoD's nouns and follow them into the repo'; nouns are prose. For a ticket that reverses a recorded assertion the survey pattern must be the identifier. (3) DURABLE FINDINGS NEED A HOME. ZM-28's worker found that appending a move is never inert -- ZM_Learnsets.cpp:52 and ZM_SpeciesData.cpp:555 both DERIVE from the whole move table by scanning it, which no blast-radius grep can find. Seven more gym reward moves remain, so it recurs seven times. I3 tells every tick to GREP the DecisionLog for governing rulings, but no step ever CREATES one from a discovery; step 8's 'Deviations / follow-ups' is a work-log row on a closing ticket that the next worker never reads. One sentence in step 8 fixes it, and the mechanism (zagent decide) already exists. (4) RETIRE THE DOCS-SYNC PROSE. Step 7's 'timed out -- the mirror is one commit behind is a legal and expected work-log outcome', the mandatory `timeout 120` wrapper and the Bash(timeout *) allowed-tools entry all rest on the belief that docs sync hangs and has never completed. It does not: the previous board's 05408ef root-caused it to a WebSocket per page for all 597 pages including unchanged ones, and it now exits 0 in 9 seconds. The machinery and the paragraph should go.

values.Suggestion: zagent claim should archive an existing .zagent/run/<KEY>/ to <KEY>.prev/ so a stale GREEN gate verdict cannot be sitting there when a tick starts.
values.Friction: Claiming ZM-28 on 2026-08-25 freshly wrote ticket.json, body.md and drift.txt and left in place, from an earlier attempt on the same key: a tick_gates.json reading state=complete, exitCode=0, verdict='all gates green' at a headSha of a DIFFERENT commit, plus a gates.json whose recorded changed-set was ['Tools/tick_gates.ps1'] -- an unrelated diff -- plus gates.log, gates.prev.log and three gate_*.ps1 scratch scripts. I3 makes the DoD the worker's verbatim specification, and the array is the obvious thing to inline because it is structured and already in the payload. A tick that does so ships a mutilated spec, and the worker cannot tell, having no shell and no board. It also weakens finish --status Done's unticked-box refusal, which reads the same truncated text.
values.Resolution: Both halves are now closed. The board half landed in the previous board's 9d03869 (2026-08-25): parseTicket carries continuation lines, so definitionOfDone[].text is no longer truncated at the first newline -- verified against ZM-23, the ticket that exposed it. The tick.md half is stated and STILL STANDS, but on a reason that never depended on the bug: the array holds the checkboxes and never the prose that qualifies them, and ZM-23's body carried two load-bearing instructions OUTSIDE any checkbox. So 'inline from body.md, never from the array' is a rule about what the array IS, not a workaround. The worked example of what the truncation cost -- including that the reachability scan could not see a protectedPath written on a continuation line -- moved to Docs/TickProtocolHistory.md, since it is now history rather than a live hazard. Zenith e411b451.

values.Suggestion: AUDIT WRAP-UP 2026-08-24: what landed in the Zenith checkout, and the four halves that are BOARD-SIDE and still open. STILL BOARD-SIDE, in priority order: (1) zagent claim should VALIDATE BEFORE IT MUTATES -- the client now rolls a refused claim back, but that is a bandage over a transaction that writes then checks, and 'zagent check' already evaluates needsHuman and EPIC without writing, so the same gate can run before the transaction; (2) 'zagent docs sync' HANGS -- four ticks, four hangs, four zero-byte logs, most recently exit 143 on ZM-65 -- and wants a --timeout-seconds flag so the bounded call stays a bare zagent invocation rather than needing a generic process wrapper on the allowlist; (3) review.required should gain a third OR term, 'the ticket's subject matter is governed by a recorded decision', computable from the decisionLog that zagent.project.json already declares -- ZM-23 was reviewed only by the luck of MEDIUM sitting in reviewOn, and that review is the only thing that caught it violating ZM-D-203 Ruling 3; (4) the claim payload could resolve candidate rulings into .zagent/run/<KEY>/rulings.md the way it already writes drift.txt, which turns I3's new rulings clause from prose into a file the orchestrator cannot fail to see. Also note guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes looks mis-tiered against measurement: the one observed MODERATE run used 94 percent of its 30-minute budget while both COMPLEX runs used about 16 percent of 90.

values.Suggestion: The reviewer caught the ORCHESTRATOR, not the worker, and the protocol does not expect that. ZM-65's review returned three BLOCKING findings and all three were in material the orchestrator wrote after the gates: a stale banner still announcing a row unfrozen 50 lines above the frozen row; a new DecisionLog entry describing a source-only commit that 'moves no scene byte' in a commit that re-authored a tracked binary; and a FABRICATED causal explanation committed to two living docs (the claim that other regions' larger 12 m seam deltas arise because those pairs 'differ in flatten containment' - the terrain recipe inverts it: all three comparison pairs are identically contained, and the one pair that differs moved the LEAST). Every control points at the worker - I1 'you own the gate, the worker only authors', I2 never trust the worker, step 6.3 'review the diff' - while the orchestrator's edits are the ones no control covers: the worker has exited, gates cannot read prose, and doc_lint's seven checks never test whether a comment's assertion matches the line beneath it. And the orchestrator writes the highest-leverage text in the repo: the pin narration, the committed-asset hashes, the decision-log entry that becomes the binding record. FIX: say in step 6.3 that the review covers the WHOLE diff including orchestrator edits, and extend the existing 'grep the doc for the value you just changed' rule to every file a freeze touches, source comments included.

values.Suggestion: The drift resolver names the WRONG GAME's file whenever two games share a filename, and it is deterministic rather than occasional. Measured across four ZM tickets: Roadmap.md and Board.md exist only under Games/Zenithmon, so the resolver suggests the Zenithmon path and is right BY LUCK; Status.md and Shortfalls.md exist under BOTH Zenithmon and DevilsPlayground, and the resolver suggested the DevilsPlayground path every time (ZM-23, ZM-30 x2). It walks in path order and takes the first match, and DevilsPlayground sorts before Zenithmon. It then presents that single pick as an answer - 'a file of that name is at X' - with no sign a second candidate exists, while tick.md step 5 tells the orchestrator to reconcile drift.txt and correct the worker prompt from it. So it is right exactly when there is no ambiguity and wrong exactly when the hint would have carried information. FIX: rank candidates by the ticket's category paths prefix, and when more than one survives print them ALL - a list reads as a question, one path reads as an answer.

values.Suggestion: Two allowed-tools gaps in .claude/commands/tick.md that stall an unattended loop. (1) Step 5 mandates TaskStop for the wedged-worker guardrail ('If elapsed wall-clock exceeds guardrails.ticketTimeoutMinutes, stop the agent (TaskStop)') but TaskStop is NOT in the frontmatter allowed-tools list - so the one enforcement action for that guardrail needs a tool the skill never granted. Measured near-miss: ZM-65's worker ran 28.1 min against a 30 min MODERATE cap. The protocol's own escape hatch ('if you can see the worker still producing tool calls') is unusable because background dispatch surfaces no progress signal and tailing the subagent transcript is forbidden. (2) Step 7 mandates 'timeout 120 zagent docs sync --json' but the permission entries are Bash(zagent:*) and Bash(zagent *), both anchored on zagent as the FIRST token - 'timeout 120 zagent ...' matches neither. The fix for the hang moved the command out from under its own permission entry, at the one step that stalls AFTER the commit lands and BEFORE finish. Better fix: give 'zagent docs sync' a --timeout-seconds flag so the bounded call stays a bare zagent invocation. Note the hang itself reproduced again on ZM-65: exit 143, zero-byte log - four ticks, four hangs.
